superlatives: PaletteColorStrip.vue:47-71 — the weighted-segment computation is the one place in this folder where the specimen is treated as DATA, and it is genuinely well designed: a complete fallback ladder (explicit weights prop -> the colours' own weight fields -> equal widths), an 8 % legibility floor so small quantizer clusters survive, and a renormalisation pass (:66-67) so the floored set still sums to 100 %. The seam is documented at the prop (:38-43) with the reason ('an extracted palette carries its population story ON the palette, so the card's own strip is proportional by construction'). Independently endorsed at challenge-D-design.md:1022-1025.

PaletteCardMenu.vue:24-30 and :44-51 — the K-INV5 pattern: a tripped availability latch DISABLES the doomed action and NAMES the degraded state in-register (`:disabled="apiOffline"` with the current state annotated) rather than letting the user fire it and catch a toast. Verified in source; better than most of the product, as the D axis says.

PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:2-31 and ShadowPalette.vue:2-40 — whatever the geometry drift (D3-6, L-43), the MOTION discipline is exemplary and is the reason PRM is correct on these two by construction: both tune only through published producer seams (`--skeleton-shimmer-delay`, `--skeleton-shimmer-tint`, `--pulse-aura-opacity-max`, `--animate-ambient-pulse-easing`) and say so at the seam — 'never re-defined here (§No-workaround)' (PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:21-22), 'tuned ONLY through the published seams... never a demo re-declaration of the producer keyframes' (:114-119). ShadowPalette.vue:36-40 also gets the announcement contract right for the right reason: aria-hidden with no role=status because 'nothing is loading — a shimmering aria-hidden plate does not lie to AT'.

demo/styles/foundation.css:653-696 and :793-841 — the two-tier forced-colors / print policy is a genuinely first-rate piece of design-system thinking: ONE named colour-display roster, declared once and reused by both media queries, with the tier split stated as a principle ('the surfaces whose whole PURPOSE is to show a color must survive WHCM's system-color substitution. The chrome... adopts system colors by default'), plus the U-F25 focus bind restoring a real system `outline` where box-shadow rings cannot paint. It is so good that the D axis mistook its absence-from-this-folder for absence-from-the-app and wrote a redundant producer letter — and the only real defect left is one missing selector on that roster.

The centrally governed motion architecture — demo/styles/animations.css:184-193 plus glass-ui a11y-overrides.css — where the two PRM guards interact to something stronger than either alone: under `reduce` the transition PROPERTY LIST itself is rewritten so transform/max-height/border-radius/filter are deleted rather than shortened, while colour legs survive deliberately. Provenance: motion-quarantine.md §1 and §5 S-1/S-4. It is why vj-morph and vj-celebrate are correct for free, and precisely why C4-1 is a defect: the one hand-rolled JS family is the one the architecture cannot reach.

confirmed.claim: "The root has role=list, but comments assume children use role=article; that is not equivalent to listitem and not enforced." (challenge-D-design.md:14; L-3 restates weakly at challenge-L-library.md:11)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, and stronger than stated — this is not "unenforced", it is VIOLATED in the live tree at both call sites. PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 sets role="list"; PaletteCard.vue:22 sets role="article"; `grep -rn 'role="listitem"' demo/` returns ZERO hits repo-wide. ARIA 1.2 gives `list` Required Owned Elements: `listitem` — `article` is not a permitted owned element, so axe-core `aria-required-children` fails and AT reports no item count / cannot enter list navigation. Both consumers are affected: PalettesPane.vue:82-97 and BrowsePane.vue:92-117 each v-for `PaletteCard` directly into the default slot with no listitem wrapper. The grid's own comment (PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-8) asserts the structure is fine, which is why it has survived.

confirmed.claim: "`contain: content` is unconditional; no escape exists for descendants that require overflow" (challenge-C-implementation.md:14) / "a performance choice with visual consequences for overflow, sticky descendants, and positioned affordances" (challenge-D-design.md:16)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED via a victim neither axis named — though both axes' own enumerated victims are WRONG. PaletteCardGrid.vue:50-52 sets `contain: content` (= layout+paint+style; paint containment clips descendants to the padding box). PaletteCard.vue:19 applies `cartoon-surface`, defined in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/styles.css as `@utility cartoon-surface { position: relative; border-width: 2px; box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md); }`, and `--shadow-cartoon-md` = `-3px 3px 0 …, -5px 5px 0 …, -7px 7px 0 …` (glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/shadow.css:1) — a hard 3-layer stamp lying ENTIRELY OUTSIDE the card's border box, up to 7px LEFT and 7px DOWN. The grid has zero padding and `grid-cols-1`, so each card's border box left edge is exactly the grid's padding box left edge: the whole left limb of the cartoon shadow is clipped on EVERY card in BOTH grids at rest, and the last card's bottom limb too. `.cartoon-cast` (glass-atom.css) compounds it — `box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md)` plus `translate: -6px/+6px` and `scale: 1.18` at full press. This amputates a ratified design register: demo/DESIGN.md:239 makes the cartoon register law ("cards consume the cartoon register (`cartoon-surface` + `.cartoon-cast` + `useLiquidPress`)"), and DESIGN.md's R4 row pins it to `PaletteCard.vue` root as "landed". The irony the axes missed: PaletteCard.vue:12-18 explicitly refuses a card-level clip ("NO overflow-hidden (S.W5-10 / S-15-A)") and its parent clips it anyway. NOTE both axes' stated victims are refuted — sticky/positioned affordances ESCAPE containment because they portal out: SwatchHoverMenu.vue:37 uses `<Teleport to="body">` and PaletteCardMenu.vue:2-7 uses reka-ui DropdownMenu (body-portalled).

confirmed.claim: "Loading, transport failure, filtered-zero, permission-denied, and first-run empty require distinct copy and actions; the grid exposes only one `empty` bit." (challenge-D-design.md:15)
confirmed.proof: The filtered-zero limb is CONFIRMED with a live lie in the copy (the loading/error limb is refuted separately — see killed). PalettesPane.vue:77 binds `:empty="pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0"` while hardcoding `empty-text="No saved palettes yet."` (:79) and `empty-hint="Add colors above, then save the set."` (:80). `filteredSaved` is search-filtered — usePalettePorts.ts:112-114 `useFilteredList(savedPalettes, searchQuery, (p,q) => p.name.toLowerCase().includes(q) || p.slug.includes(q))`, and useFilteredList.ts:8-12 returns `items.value.filter(...)` whenever the query is non-empty. So a user holding 10 saved palettes who types a non-matching query is told "No saved palettes yet." — factually false — and is handed a remedy ("Add colors above, then save the set") that cannot resolve the state, while the actual remedy (clear the search) is never offered. Identical defect in BrowsePane.vue:83-86: `:empty="displayedBrowse.length === 0"` (derived from `pm.filteredBrowse` at BrowsePane.vue:339-340, itself behind search + tier + tag + color filters) renders "No published palettes here yet. Publish one from My Palettes and start the wall." This is one `empty` boolean carrying two mutually exclusive meanings, and the wrong one is asserted with confident prose.

confirmed.claim: "The implementation relies on a single-element root for an external `$el` consumer, but no automated guard prevents a future fragment root regression." (challenge-C-implementation.md:13); L-5: the `$el`/useSortable requirement "is folklore rather than a typed adapter" (challenge-L-library.md:13)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED — and the corpus understated it, because a guard is CLAIMED to exist and does not work. PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11 documents that a leading comment node would make this multi-root and break `$el`; PalettesPane.vue:180-183 consumes exactly that (`sortableGridRef` → `(sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el as HTMLElement | undefined` → `useSortable`), with `as any` erasing the type. The nominal guard is e2e/smoke/walk.spec.ts:71, commented "PaletteCardGrid is role=\"list\" — the B.W1 single-root invariant", asserting `main.getByRole("list").last()` is visible. That assertion CANNOT detect the regression: under a fragment root the `<div role="list">` still renders and is still visible, so the test passes green while `$el` resolves to the comment node and drag-reorder dies. And nothing else covers it — grepping e2e/ for sortable|drag|reorder returns only slider/spectrum drag perf specs (reactivity-instant.spec.ts:41, perf/drag-frame-budget.spec.ts:33); there is zero e2e coverage of palette reorder. So the invariant is load-bearing, silently breakable, and protected by a test whose comment misrepresents what it checks.

This is an INFO-grade API-hardening observation, not evidence of a red component.

missed.claim: Both shipped a11y comments assert a false ARIA fact — that `article` and `list` are landmark roles — and that false premise is precisely what licensed the broken list/listitem structure (D-4).
missed.proof: PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-8: "role=\"list\" — each child PaletteCard (role=\"article\") sits in a list landmark." PaletteCard.vue:2: "role=\"article\" provides a landmark for each palette." Neither role is a landmark. The ARIA 1.2 landmark roles are exactly: banner, complementary, contentinfo, form, main, navigation, region, search — `article` and `list` are document-structure roles and expose no landmark to AT rotors. So the stated benefit ("a landmark for each palette") is not delivered by any code on the page, and the reasoning that made role=article look like a sufficient list child is unsound at its root. All three axes read these comments (D-4 quotes the role=article line) and none challenged the ARIA claim inside them. Cure is structural, not prose: wrap each card in `role="listitem"` (or emit `<ul>/<li>`), which fixes D-4 and retires the misconception together.

missed.claim: The grid keeps `role="list"` while rendering the empty plate, so the true-empty state is announced as an empty list wrapping a status region — a second, distinct aria-required-children failure that survives even after D-4 is cured.
missed.proof: PaletteCardGrid.vue:2-6 puts `role="list"` on the root unconditionally; when `empty` is true the only child is the EmptyState (PaletteCardGrid.vue:21-31), whose empty branch is `<div … role="status">` (EmptyState.vue:28). The resulting tree is `list > status` with zero listitem children — malformed regardless of how the populated case is fixed, because the plate is not an item. This is the state both e2e oracles exercise (o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:187-234), so it is the state most likely to be reached and least likely to be caught. Correct shape is to drop the list role when there are no items, or render the plate as a sibling outside the list root. No axis addressed the empty branch's list semantics — D-4 and L-3 reason only about populated children.

missed.claim: Comment-to-code ratio and register: 20 of 53 lines are comments, most of them internal tranche archaeology shipped in product source.
missed.proof: PaletteCardGrid.vue:13-20 is an eight-line block opening "T.W6.5 · Lane S (R12 — the owner overrule of the D9 as-filler deployment; MANDATE §0.6 t33-audit-07/08/12)", and PaletteCardGrid.vue:48-49 carries "(D.W4 Lane A §4: colocated from styles/style.css)". superlatives: The two-species empty/error discipline is exemplary and rare. EmptyState.vue:1-13 states the law ("loading ≠ empty, error ≠ empty"), EmptyState.vue:76 encodes it as a typed prop (`variant?: "empty" | "error"`), and the error branch (EmptyState.vue:14-27) genuinely changes register — `role="alert"` instead of `role="status"`, no eyebrow, no ghost trio, a destructive glyph, the raw machine string quarantined to a Fira detail line, and a real Retry in the action slot (wired at BrowsePane.vue:68-77). Most codebases collapse these into one grey box. It is e2e-pinned: "O-9 · error ≠ empty — the Browse error plate wears NO ghost and NO trio" (o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:236).

The TRUE-EMPTY "zero fillers" ruling is enforced, not merely written down. The decision that an empty plate is the invitation ALONE — never ghost cards masquerading as content — is recorded at PaletteCardGrid.vue:13-20 and then held by executable oracles at BOTH call sites: o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:187-201 (My Palettes) and :203-234 (Browse), each calling `assertTrio` + `assertNoFillers`. The Browse oracle even routes a shape-correct empty API response so the true-empty branch (not the error plate) is deterministically on screen (:206-224). Design intent with a test that can actually fail is the strongest pattern in this component's neighbourhood.

The caption-contrast cure is measured, sourced, and shared. EmptyState.vue:49-54 records that the previous static `text-muted-foreground` composited at 3.84:1 over the My Palettes plate in light — below the 4.5:1 small-text floor — and EmptyState.vue:94-104 lands the fix as `.plate-ink { color: var(--ink-muted, var(--muted-foreground)); }` on a boot-stamped, floor-clamped rung, deliberately at the ONE shared empty atom "so every consumer inherits the cure" (:98-99). Fixing a11y at the shared atom rather than per-site, with the failing ratio cited, is textbook.

The single-root comment (PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11) is genuinely load-bearing prose of a kind that is almost never written: it explains not just the invariant but why the comment's own POSITION matters ("This comment is the div's first CHILD, not a sibling: a leading comment node would make this a multi-root component"), and names the downstream victim (`PalettesPane` reading `$el` for `useSortable`). It documents a real, silent, non-obvious Vue failure mode. (Its "list landmark" clause is wrong — see missed #1 — but the mechanism it protects is correctly identified.)

Glass-ui's `.cartoon-cast` PRM handling is elegant beyond compliance: rather than merely disabling the transition, `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .cartoon-cast { --motion-weight: 0; transition: none; } }` (glass-atom.css) zeroes the input variable, so `--cast-travel` (`calc(6px * var(--motion-weight) * …)`) collapses to 0 and `--cast-spread` collapses to exactly 1 — the element lands in its correct rest geometry instead of freezing mid-pose. This is also why no PRM defect is carryable here; motion-quarantine.md:275 lists PaletteCardGrid as vacuously cleared on C · D · L, consistent with the global neutraliser at demo/styles/animations.css:184-193.
unproven: UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE: the perceptual magnitude of the cartoon-shadow clipping (CONFIRMED #2). The clipping itself is statically proven from the cascade — `contain: content` on a zero-padding `grid-cols-1` container versus a `-3/-5/-7px` outset box-shadow on a full-bleed child — but exactly how many px survive at each viewport, and whether the left limb is fully or partially amputated once `border-width: 2px` and the pane's own `px-4 sm:px-6` are composited, requires a rendered measurement (getComputedStyle + element screenshot diff at the grid's left edge). Barred here by probe parsimony.

UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE: whether the v-if'd `role="status"` empty plate is actually announced on a filter transition. PaletteCardGrid.vue:22 inserts the whole EmptyState (and thus the live region itself, EmptyState.vue:28) into the DOM at the same moment as its content. The ARIA/APG guidance is that a live region should exist in the DOM before its content changes for reliable announcement, so the filtered-zero transition may be silent for AT users — which would compound CONFIRMED #3. Deciding this needs a real screen-reader pairing (NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver), not static reading.

UNPROVEN: the exact px at which `min-h-[120px]` binds (missed #3). The empty-state inertness is exact (~194px computed from EmptyState's own utilities), but the single-card case depends on live `text-subheading` line-height and whether PaletteCardMeta adds a second row; my ~90px card estimate is arithmetic over PaletteColorStrip.vue:10 (`h-10`) plus PaletteCard.vue:43 (`px-3 py-2.5`) plus the 2px cartoon border, not a measurement.

confirmed.claim: `Button` arrives via a forwarding barrel and `variant="outline"` is not the installed glass-ui Button API — dead intent.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, twice over. Barrel: `demo/ui/button/index.ts:1` is literally `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` — a one-line forwarding barrel, and `demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:34` imports through it. API: installed glass-ui is 7.0.0 (`node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json:3`) and `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-19` declares `ButtonProps` = {emphasis, tone, size, iconOnly, loading, type, disabled, class} — NO `variant`. The producer states the prohibition explicitly: `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/_shared/axes.d.ts:16` — "The tone axis — the semantic status register …; NEVER a `variant` member." Runtime consequence proven from the compiled component `node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js:11-13`: props default `emphasis:"secondary", tone:"neutral", size:"md"`, and `variant` is absent from the props object, so `variant="outline"` at `PaginationBar.vue:8` and `:22` falls through `$attrs` onto the reka-ui `Primitive` and is emitted as a literal non-standard `variant="outline"` DOM attribute on `<button>`. Both bar buttons therefore paint `data-emphasis="secondary"` glass-wash capsules, not outline. `size="sm"` IS honoured (`ButtonSize` = xs|sm|md|lg), so the axis is stale, not wholly wrong. Scope: 29 `variant="outline"` + 28 `variant="ghost"` occurrences across `demo/` (13 outline on Button elements) — PaginationBar is 2 of a fleet-wide stale-shadcn-axis residue. NOTE for the cure: `variant` IS still valid on Badge (`dist/components/badge/Badge.vue.d.ts:4`), so this is a per-component, not a blanket, kill.

confirmed.claim: Events carry no destination and there is no pending guard; users can double-activate while results load, with no relation between the page text and the rows.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED at the integration boundary, with a mechanism the axes did not supply. `PaginationBar.vue:10,24` gate the buttons on `hasPrev`/`hasNext` ONLY — the component declares no `loading`/`busy` prop (`:37-42`), and neither call site passes one (`AdminAuditPanel.vue:83-90`, `AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:126-133`). The handler `useAdminAudit.ts:73-78` does `page.value++` then `loadAuditLog()` WITHOUT awaiting; `loadAuditLog` (`:48-71`) sets `loading=true`, awaits `getAuditLog`, then unconditionally assigns `entries.value = res.data; total.value = res.total`. A second click while the first is in flight passes the `hasNext` guard again (page is already incremented, pageCount unchanged) and issues a second request. `demo/palettes/api/admin-audit.ts:24-36` takes no `AbortSignal` and returns a bare promise — there is no sequence token, no last-write-wins guard, and the `finally { loading = false }` of whichever response lands first clears the flag for both. Out-of-order responses therefore write page N-1's rows under a "Page N" label, permanently, until the next load. `useAdminFlagged.ts:105-117` is the byte-identical twin. The cure the axes want already exists in the producer and is unused: `Button.vue.d.ts:16` — `loading?: boolean` — "Marks an in-flight command and suppresses activation until it settles" (compiled: `button-Bu9F4uU6.js:36` folds `loading` into the disabled computation and stamps `aria-busy`).

confirmed.claim: `aria-live` announces page-text mutations not bound to completion of the corresponding list request.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, and it is unconditional rather than merely possible. `PaginationBar.vue:17-19` is an `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` span reading `Page {{ page }} of {{ pageCount }}`. `page` is a prop mirroring `audit.page`, which is mutated SYNCHRONOUSLY at `useAdminAudit.ts:75` (`page.value++`) before `loadAuditLog()` is even called at `:76`. So on every activation the assistive announcement of the destination page fires on the same tick as the click, while the rendered rows are still the previous page's (`entries.value` is not reassigned until `:61`, after the await). This is not a rare 'rapid update' race as D-4 hedges — it is the ordinary single-click path. `useAdminFlagged.ts:107` is identical.

confirmed.claim: Users receive no relation between the displayed page text and the displayed rows.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED by a second, independent mechanism the axis never located — the bar is outside its panel's state chain. In `AdminAuditPanel.vue` the loading/error/empty branches form a `v-if`(:36)/`v-else-if`(:43)/`v-else-if`(:56) chain that ENDS at line 56; the entries block at `:59` carries only `v-for` (no `v-else`) and `PaginationBar` at `:83` carries no condition at all. Both therefore render unconditionally. During a load, the skeletons (`:37`) AND the stale previous-page rows AND a fully interactive pagination bar are on screen simultaneously; after a load failure, the 'The ledger is unreachable.' EmptyState (`:43-53`) renders ALONGSIDE the stale rows and an interactive bar (because `total`/`pageCount` retain their last-good values — `loadAuditLog`'s catch at `:64-67` never resets them). `AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16/22/37/44/126` is structurally identical. This directly contradicts the in-file W5-5 doctrine comment at `AdminAuditPanel.vue:40-41` ('error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as a clear ledger'): the ledger still costumes, it just adds an error card on top.

killed.claim: `hasPrev`/`hasNext` are trusted instead of derived, allowing "Page 1 of 2" with Previous enabled or Next disabled.
killed.refutation: REFUTED. Both — and the only two — call sites derive them from the same `page`/`pageCount` the bar renders: `useAdminAudit.ts:44-46` and `useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57` are byte-identical `pageCount = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/pageSize))`, `hasNext = page < pageCount`, `hasPrev = page > 1`, all Vue `computed`s. `AdminAuditPanel.vue:84-87` and `AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:127-130` pass exactly those four computeds. There is no third consumer (`grep -rn PaginationBar demo src test` → 4 hits, 2 templates + 2 imports). The specific state the finding names — 'Page 1 of 2 with Previous enabled' — requires `page===1 && hasPrev===true`, which is `1 > 1` and unreachable by construction. The claimed 'Cartesian product' does not exist in the live tree; the props are three derivations of one scalar plus that scalar.

killed.claim: `pageCount > 1` is the sole guard; `page=0`, `page>pageCount`, non-integer, or negative values are rendered verbatim.
killed.refutation: MOSTLY REFUTED — three of four limbs are unreachable. `page` is initialised to `1` (`useAdminAudit.ts:37`, `useAdminFlagged.ts:50`) and mutated in exactly three places: `page.value++` behind `if (hasNext)` (`useAdminAudit.ts:74-75`), `page.value--` behind `if (hasPrev)` i.e. `page > 1` (`:81-82`), and `audit.page.value = 1` on filter change (`AdminAuditPanel.vue:114`). No fractional or negative write exists, and `page=0` would require decrementing from 1 past the `hasPrev` guard. `pageCount` cannot be zero or negative either — `Math.max(1, …)` clamps it (`useAdminAudit.ts:44`), which also kills D-1's 'invalid negative/zero totals' limb. The fourth limb (`page > pageCount`) IS reachable, but not by the mechanism this finding asserts (contradictory props at the boundary); it is caused by the parent mutating `total` without clamping `page` — re-filed with its full mechanism as the missed finding 'unclamped page survives an optimistic delete'. As written, the finding predicts the right symptom from the wrong cause.

killed.claim: `page`, `pageCount`, `hasNext`, and `hasPrev` can contradict each other; the boundary should accept one normalized pagination state.
killed.refutation: REFUTED as stated. Three of the four scalars are `computed`s over the fourth (`useAdminAudit.ts:44-46`, `useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57`) — the pairwise contradictions the finding posits between `hasNext`/`hasPrev` and `page`/`pageCount` are structurally impossible. Only ONE contradiction is reachable (`page > pageCount` after an unclamped optimistic delete), and it is a parent-side mutation bug, not a boundary-shape bug: normalizing the prop into a single object would carry the same wrong `page` inside it. The prescribed cure at `challenge-L-library.md:15` (`PaginationState = unknown | ready | loading | error` plus a named command result) is also over-built for a 48-line bar with two consumers and collides with standing owner law (`feedback_kiss_no_contrivance.md`: no invented shared abstractions). NOTE the producer already ships the exact three-state vocabulary if one is ever wanted — `dist/components/data-table/types.d.ts:24`, `DataTableStatus = "ready" | "loading" | "error"` — so the fourth `unknown` case is the author's invention, not producer vocabulary.

killed.claim: The live-region sentence is locally authored; other paginated surfaces can announce at a different phase.
killed.refutation: REFUTED — there are no other paginated surfaces. `grep -rn pageCount demo src api` returns hits in exactly three files: `PaginationBar.vue`, `useAdminAudit.ts`, `useAdminFlagged.ts`. The remaining admin panels (`AdminUsersPanel.vue`, `AdminNamesPanel.vue`, `AdminTagsPanel.vue`) contain no pagination at all, and glass-ui 7.0.0 exports no Pagination component (`dist/index.d.ts:1-27` — `PagerDots` is a carousel dot rail keyed on slide `count`, `dist/components/pager-dots/PagerDots.vue.d.ts:2-4`, not a page-of-N readout). The divergence hazard is hypothetical; there is exactly one authored sentence and one consumer of it.

killed.claim: This generic pattern belongs in glass-ui or a shared application collection package, not independently in each admin panel.
killed.refutation: REFUTED on its factual premise. The pattern is NOT 'independently in each admin panel' — there is one file, `demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue`, imported by two panels (`AdminAuditPanel.vue:102`, `AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:144`). Zero duplication. It is also correctly encapsulated: the hardened admin barrel `demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts` (NAMED-re-exports-only, PI-6) exports the five panels and deliberately does NOT export PaginationBar, so it is a private implementation detail by construction. 'Belongs in glass-ui' is unactionable (the producer ships no such component and the repo cannot author into it from here), and 'a shared application collection package' is precisely the invented-shared-surface move that `feedback_kiss_no_contrivance.md` forbids. The only defensible residue is a colocation nit filed at INFO in `missed`.

killed.claim: The bar disappears whenever `pageCount <= 1`; that conflates a verified single page with unknown count, loading, error, and invalid negative/zero totals.
killed.refutation: REFUTED in its two load-bearing limbs, and inverted in the third. (a) 'Invalid negative/zero totals' cannot occur — `Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/pageSize))` (`useAdminAudit.ts:44`, `useAdminFlagged.ts:55`) clamps pageCount to ≥1 for any total including 0 and negatives. (b) The bar does NOT disappear on loading or error: `pageCount` is derived from `total`, and neither `loadAuditLog`'s catch (`useAdminAudit.ts:64-67`) nor `loadFlagged`'s (`useAdminFlagged.ts:72-76`) resets `total`, so after any successful first load the bar keeps rendering — at full opacity and fully interactive — over both the loading skeletons and the error EmptyState (see the confirmed D-2 second-limb finding). The real defect is the exact opposite of the one alleged: persistence, not disappearance. (c) The surviving limb — first paint with `total=0` hides the bar, so 'still loading' looks like 'one page' — is benign, because the skeleton block (`AdminAuditPanel.vue:36-38`) carries the loading signal at that moment. INFO at most.

missed.claim: An optimistic delete/dismiss decrements `total` without clamping `page` or reloading — producing the false 'Page 3 of 2' label the C axis predicted from the wrong cause, and, when `pageCount` falls to 1, permanently stranding the admin on an empty page with the pagination control REMOVED.
missed.proof: `useAdminFlagged.ts:81-91` (`dismiss`) and `:93-103` (`deletePalette`) both do `items.value = items.value.filter(...)` then `total.value = Math.max(0, total.value - 1)` and then STOP — no reload, no `page` clamp, no `if (page > pageCount) page = pageCount`. Two reachable outcomes. (1) FALSE LABEL: total=41, pageSize=20 (`:51`) → pageCount=3; on page 3 (one row); dismiss it → total=40 → pageCount=2 while `page` is still 3. `PaginationBar.vue:3` (`pageCount > 1`) still passes, so the bar renders 'Page 3 of 2' (`:18`) with Previous enabled (`hasPrev = 3 > 1`) and Next disabled. This is precisely the class of false label `challenge-C-implementation.md:9` asserts, now with a real mechanism. (2) STRANDING (the serious case): total=21 → pageCount=2; on page 2 (one row); dismiss it → total=20 → pageCount=1 → `PaginationBar.vue:3` evaluates false and the ENTIRE bar unmounts while `page` remains 2. The panel now shows '20 flagged' in the toolbar (`AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:5-7`) beside the 'No flagged palettes.' EmptyState (`:37-41`) and no navigation control whatsoever. The only remaining affordance, Refresh (`:10`), calls `loadFlagged()` which computes `offset = (2-1)*20 = 20` (`useAdminFlagged.ts:67`) and returns an empty page forever. The state is unrecoverable without a full page reload. Note the same file already proves the authors know how to re-clamp — `AdminAuditPanel.vue:114` resets `page.value = 1` on filter change — the delete paths simply omit it. `useAdminAudit.ts` is immune (no mutations).

missed.claim: The producer's `iconOnly` prop — the declared API for exactly this shape — is not passed, so the two icon commands render as wide pills instead of square icon buttons and lose the `data-icon-only`/`data-control-target` stamps.
missed.proof: `PaginationBar.vue:6` self-identifies the shape ('W5-a11y: icon-only pagination buttons need aria-labels') and `:7-15`/`:21-29` pass only `variant`/`size`/`disabled`/`aria-label` — never `iconOnly`. The producer declares it at `dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:17`: 'Square geometry for an accessibly named icon command', defaulting false (`dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js:15-18`). The compiled render stamps `"data-icon-only": iconOnly || undefined` and `"data-control-target": iconOnly ? "" : undefined` (`button-Bu9F4uU6.js:53-54`), so both are absent here. Consequence, from `dist/components/button/styles.css:1`: `.button[data-icon-only] { inline-size/block-size/min-block-size: var(--button-size); padding: 0 }` never applies, so the buttons keep `[data-size="sm"]`'s `padding-inline: calc(0.75rem * var(--ui-scale))` and render as ~52px-wide pills around a 16px glyph rather than square `--control-h-sm` targets. HONEST LIMIT: the WCAG tap-target floor is NOT breached — `min-block-size: var(--button-size)` and, under `@media (pointer: coarse)`, `--ui-scale: 1.5` with `--control-floor: var(--touch-target, 2.75rem)` (`dist/styles/tokens/light-dark.css:1`, `dist/styles/tokens/sizing.css:1`) make `--control-h-sm` = max(54px, 44px) = 54px, so the 44px floor that `[data-control-target]` would have guaranteed (`dist/styles/utilities/responsive.css:1`) is met incidentally. This is a geometry/producer-contract miss, not an a11y breach.

missed.claim: Advancing to the last page with the keyboard destroys the user's focus: the focused button becomes natively `disabled` under the pointer, dropping focus to `<body>`.
missed.proof: `PaginationBar.vue:24` binds `:disabled="!hasNext"`; the compiled Button applies the NATIVE attribute (not `aria-disabled`) whenever it renders as a `<button>`, which is the default `as` — `dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js:38-42`: `disabled: h.value ? m.value : void 0` with `h = !asChild && as === "button"`, plus `.button:disabled { pointer-events: none }` (`dist/components/button/styles.css:1`). Sequence: a keyboard user tabs to Next and presses Enter on the second-to-last page → `hasNext` recomputes to false (`useAdminAudit.ts:45`) → the currently-focused element is disabled in the same tick → browsers blur it and reset the focus pointer to `<body>`, so the next Tab restarts from the top of the document, far from the pagination bar. Symmetric on Previous reaching page 1. The producer itself models the soft-disable idiom for exactly this reason (`button-Bu9F4uU6.js:40`: `"aria-disabled": !h.value && m.value ? "true" : void 0`), and the disabled-state CSS is already written against both selectors (`styles.css:1`: `.button:disabled, .button[aria-disabled="true"]`) — so the fix is available in-producer with no CSS work. All three axes discussed disabled state (C-2, D-2) and none noticed the focus consequence.

missed.claim: The chevron glyphs are sized with `h-4 w-4`, which does not trip the producer's declared escape hatch, so they defeat the `--ui-glyph` scale axis by cascade-layer accident rather than by opt-out — and under coarse pointer they under-render at 16px against the producer's intended 24px.
missed.proof: `PaginationBar.vue:14` and `:28` set `class="h-4 w-4"`. The producer sizes bare glyph children at `dist/components/button/styles.css:1`: `.button > svg:not([class*="size-"]) { inline-size: var(--ui-glyph); block-size: var(--ui-glyph) }` — the `:not([class*="size-"])` guard is the SANCTIONED override idiom, and `h-4 w-4` does not contain `size-`, so the producer rule still matches. The winner is decided by cascade layer, not specificity: `demo/styles/foundation.css:1` (`@import "tailwindcss"`) establishes theme/base/components/utilities and glass-ui's compiled sheet is imported at `:56-57` into `@layer components`, so Tailwind's `.h-4`/`.w-4` (utilities) beat `.button > svg:not(...)` (components) despite the latter's higher specificity — physical `height`/`width` and logical `block-size`/`inline-size` cascade together for the same box dimension. `--ui-glyph: calc(1rem * var(--ui-scale))` (`dist/styles/tokens/sizing.css:1`) with `--ui-scale: var(--ui-coarse-scale, 1.5)` under `@media (pointer: coarse)` (`dist/styles/tokens/light-dark.css:1`) means the producer intends 24px glyphs on touch; the hard-coded `h-4 w-4` pins 16px. Fleet-wide, not local: `grep -rho 'class="size-[0-9]' demo | wc -l` → 0, `grep -rho 'class="h-[0-9] w-[0-9]"' demo | wc -l` → 20. The demo never once uses the escape hatch the producer wrote for it, so every icon button in the tree is silently overriding by layer order instead of opting out by contract.

missed.claim: The typo class that produced the `variant` defect is structurally uncatchable by this repo's hard CI gate — `strictTemplates` is nowhere enabled, so vue-tsc accepts any unknown attribute on any component as a fallthrough attr.
missed.proof: `grep -rn vueCompilerOptions tsconfig*.json vite.config.ts` returns nothing; `tsconfig.demo.json:31` extends `tsconfig.base.json`, whose only relevant flag is `"strict": true` (`:7`) — a TS flag, not a Vue-template flag. With Volar's `strictTemplates` defaulting to false, `variant="outline"` on a component with no `variant` prop is legal and lands in `$attrs`. This is why `npm run typecheck` (`package.json:65`, `vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit`) is green despite 57 stale-axis attributes across `demo/`, and why the W44 CI hardening did not surface any of them. Filing this as its own row because fixing PaginationBar's two lines without flipping the gate leaves 55 identical latent defects and no mechanism to prevent the 58th.

missed.claim: PaginationBar and the pagination state it renders have ZERO automated coverage — no unit test, no e2e assertion — despite being the only paginated surface in the product.

superlatives: `tabular-nums` on the page counter (`PaginationBar.vue:17`) — the digits are the one thing in the bar that changes, and lining figures stop the sentence from re-flowing between 'Page 9 of 12' and 'Page 10 of 12'. Textbook icon-button naming: `aria-label` on the interactive element and `aria-hidden="true"` on the decorative glyph, on both buttons (`PaginationBar.vue:11,14` and `:25,28`), with the intent recorded in-line at `:6` so a later reader cannot delete it by accident. Correct privacy for an internal: `demo/palettes/browser/admin/index.ts` is a NAMED-re-exports-only hardened surface (its own header cites PI-6) exporting the five panels and deliberately NOT PaginationBar, AdminListItem, or AdminListSkeleton. 48 lines, zero local state, zero lifecycle, zero dead code, no `withDefaults` ceremony, modern `defineEmits<{ prev: []; next: [] }>()` tuple syntax (`:44-47`) rather than the legacy call-signature form. Under my lens — dead code, leaks, module size, duplication — the component file itself is clean: nothing to delete, nothing that leaks, nothing duplicated. Every defect I confirmed or found is a contract defect at its edges (the producer above it, the composables below it), not a defect in its body.

`pageCount = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total.value / pageSize))` appears byte-identically at `useAdminAudit.ts:44` and `useAdminFlagged.ts:55`. The `Math.max(1, …)` is what makes C-1's zero/negative limbs and D-1's 'invalid negative/zero totals' limb unreachable — a one-token guard, written twice without drift, that pre-refutes two of the three axes' headline claims. Duplication across the two composables is the only blemish, and at nine tokens it is under the threshold where extraction would pay.
unproven: D-3 ('no first/last or direct-page affordances; no threshold or large-count design exists') — outside my library/code lens and undecidable statically. It is a product-scope question, not a correctness one: with `pageSize = 20` (`useAdminAudit.ts:38`, `useAdminFlagged.ts:51`) the affordance gap only bites at admin datasets large enough to make prev/next tedious, and no such dataset size is established anywhere in the tree. Leaving to the D axis; no defect asserted.

The exact cascade winner for `h-4 w-4` vs `.button > svg:not([class*="size-"])` is argued from the layer ORDER established by `@import "tailwindcss"` at `demo/styles/foundation.css:1` and glass-ui's `@layer components` wrapper — I did not observe a computed style. The layer analysis is sound and the finding stands on the contract violation regardless of which rule wins (the sanctioned `size-*` escape hatch is not used, so the outcome is accidental either way), but the specific '16px paints where 24px was intended on touch' consequence is UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

The stranding scenario's user-visible endpoint (empty page, no bar, Refresh cannot recover) is derived from the source with complete arithmetic — `total`/`page`/`offset` are all traced — but the terminal render was not observed. Every step is statically decidable; only the composite is UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE. It needs ≥21 flagged palettes to reproduce.

confirmed.claim: "The implementation relies on a single-element root for an external `$el` consumer, but no automated guard prevents a future fragment root regression." (challenge-C-implementation.md:13)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED as stated, and the seam is worse than the axis knew. LIVE: PalettesPane.vue:180-181 `const sortableEl = computed(() => (sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el as HTMLElement | undefined)` feeds PalettesPane.vue:183 `useSortable(sortableEl, ...)`. PaletteCardGrid.vue:2-6 is a single root only because the narrating comment sits INSIDE the div (PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11). Consequence chain re-derived: a leading root comment makes the dev compiler emit a DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT, `$el` resolves to the fragment's Text anchor, `unrefElement` returns it verbatim (node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js `start()`), and sortablejs throws `el must be an HTMLElement` inside the `tryOnMounted` hook — Vue's error handler swallows it, drag dies, nothing else breaks. The ONE named guard is mislabeled: e2e/smoke/walk.spec.ts:71-72 comments "PaletteCardGrid is role=\"list\" — the B.W1 single-root invariant" but asserts only `expect(main.getByRole("list").last()).toBeVisible()`, which is insensitive to root arity and stays green through the regression. Repo-wide there is no other test: `PaletteCardGrid|palette-card-grid` hits only walk.spec.ts and o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts, and .github/workflows/ci.yml runs lint/vue-tsc/build/vitest with ZERO playwright steps — so even that oracle is not a gate. The sibling PaletteCard.vue:2-4 and PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:2-31 already commit the exact root-leading-comment shape, so the hazard is demonstrated live one level down.

confirmed.claim: "`contain: content` is unconditional; no escape exists for descendants that require overflow or layout participation" (challenge-C-implementation.md:14) / "`contain: content` … has visual consequences for overflow, sticky descendants, and positioned affordances; those consequences are not part of the design contract" (challenge-D-design.md:16)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED-RESCOPED: the mechanism is real, the axes' named casualties are not. REFUTED casualties: `sticky` → 0 hits under demo/palettes/browser/; the positioned affordances are all portaled (SwatchHoverMenu.vue:37 `<Teleport to="body">`, PaletteCardMenu via reka-ui portals) and ActionFeedback.vue is in-flow, not fixed/absolute. REAL casualty, derived from bytes: PaletteCardGrid.vue:50-52 sets `contain: content` (= layout+paint+style) on a container with ZERO padding (PaletteCardGrid.vue:4 `grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 min-h-[120px]`), so paint containment clips descendants at a padding box flush with every card's left and right edges. PaletteCard.vue:19 wears `cartoon-surface`, which node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/styles.css defines as `box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md)`, and node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/shadow.css defines `--shadow-cartoon-md: -3px 3px 0 …, -5px 5px 0 …, -7px 7px 0 …` — LEFT + DOWN. demo/styles/foundation.css:366-367 and :518-519 re-point only `--shadow-cartoon` / `--shadow-cartoon-hover` to 8px RIGHT+down; `-md` keeps the producer's leftward cast. Result: every card's entire left leg (up to −7px) is clipped, and the last card's bottom leg too (interior bottom legs survive inside the 12px `gap-3`). PaletteCard.vue:16-18 explicitly declines `overflow-hidden` to protect this exact caster; the grid clips it one level up. The two decisions are provably aware of each other and still collide.

confirmed.claim: "The root has `role=list`, but comments assume children use `role=article`; that is not equivalent to `listitem` and not enforced." (challenge-D-design.md:14)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED and EXTENDED to a second state the axis missed. PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 `role="list"`; PaletteCard.vue:22 `role="article"`; census `grep -rn 'role="listitem"' demo/ src/ e2e/` → 0 hits repo-wide. ARIA 1.2 makes `listitem` the Required Owned Element of `list`, so the populated state is a standing `aria-required-children` violation. EXTENSION: in the TRUE-EMPTY state the grid's sole owned child is EmptyState.vue:28 `role="status"` — also not `listitem` — so a fix aimed only at the populated state leaves the empty state violating. The in-file comment at PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-8 is wrong twice: `article` is not `listitem`, and neither `list` nor `article` is a landmark role (both are structure roles). The comment is the only "enforcement" that exists.

confirmed.claim: "Loading, transport failure, filtered-zero, permission-denied, and first-run empty require distinct copy and actions; the grid exposes only one `empty` bit." (challenge-D-design.md:15)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED-NARROWED to ONE limb (filtered-zero); the other four are refuted as grid obligations. SURVIVING LIMB, both call sites: PalettesPane.vue:77 computes `:empty="pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0"` from the FILTERED projection (usePalettePorts.ts:112-114 → useFilteredList.ts:8-12) while PalettesPane.vue:19-25 renders a count Badge from the UNFILTERED `savedPalettes.value.length` and PalettesPane.vue:62 keeps the "Delete all saved palettes" trigger live on the same unfiltered count. So N saved palettes + a non-matching query simultaneously renders: badge "N", a live delete-all-N button, and PalettesPane.vue:79-80's plate reading "No saved palettes yet. / Add colors above, then save the set." — the plate states a falsehood and the contradiction is in the accessibility tree. Same shape at BrowsePane.vue:83 vs :85-86 ("No published palettes here yet. / Publish one from My Palettes…") reached through the search/tag filter or the client-side colour filter at BrowsePane.vue:339-349. REFUTED limbs: loading and transport-failure already ship as SIBLING branches one altitude up (BrowsePane.vue:43-54 skeletons, :61-78 error plate with a real Retry, all three inside one `<Transition mode="out-in">` at :40); permission-denied exists nowhere in the feature; first-run empty IS the true-empty branch and is already correct. The prescribed cure (a `CollectionSurfaceState` union inside a 53-line leaf) is unsound — the correct cure is one honest branch of copy at the two hosts, which already own the query state.

killed.claim: "`empty` can contradict the default slot; there is no item count or state union to enforce exclusivity" (challenge-C-implementation.md:9) / "A caller can render cards and the empty plate simultaneously, or neither" (challenge-D-design.md:11)
killed.refutation: No live producer, and the prescribed cure is unsound. Both — and only — consumers derive `empty` from the very array they iterate, in adjacent lines: PalettesPane.vue:77 `:empty="pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0"` vs :83 `v-for="palette in pm.filteredSaved.value"`; BrowsePane.vue:83 `:empty="displayedBrowse.length === 0"` vs :93 `v-for="palette in displayedBrowse"`. Exclusivity holds by construction at 2/2 sites. The cure the row demands (derive count from the default slot) requires reading `$slots.default?.()` VNode output, which is opaque — v-for produces a Fragment, dev builds inject comment nodes, and PaletteCard itself compiles to a dev root fragment (PaletteCard.vue:2-5) — so a leaf that guesses collection size from slot VNodes would be a NEW defect. Residual is INFO-tier API hygiene only.

killed.claim: "`v-if="$slots.emptyAction"` checks only whether a slot function exists, not whether it produces an actionable node" (challenge-C-implementation.md:10) / "couples rendering to Vue slot presence rather than a typed action model" (challenge-L-library.md:12)

killed.claim: "Optional text props are passed through unchanged, so an empty plate can be semantically empty" (challenge-C-implementation.md:11) / "A true-empty surface can therefore render blank annotation fields and lose the careful invitation hierarchy" (challenge-D-design.md:12)
killed.refutation: The plural is false at every reachable site. EmptyState.vue:90 `withDefaults(…, { variant: "empty", eyebrow: "· empty plate ·", dots: true })` — the eyebrow and the ghost trio cannot blank, by construction. `hint` is `v-if`-guarded at EmptyState.vue:61, so an absent hint renders no element rather than a blank field. "Blank annotation fields" (plural) has no reachable instance.

killed.claim: "Arbitrary `gridClass` can override columns, display, containment, or visibility and makes layout testing unbounded" (challenge-C-implementation.md:12) / "every responsive decision arrives through `gridClass`; the component cannot guarantee card width, reading order, or breakpoint behavior" (challenge-D-design.md:13) / "exports raw styling authority to every consumer, defeating a stable library API" (challenge-L-library.md:10)
killed.refutation: Four independent refutations. (a) CONTAINMENT CANNOT BE OVERRIDDEN: PaletteCardGrid.vue:47-53 is a `<style scoped>` block with no Tailwind directives, so it compiles to an UNLAYERED `.palette-card-grid[data-v-hash] { contain: content }` while any `contain-*` utility lands inside `@layer utilities` — unlayered always beats layered regardless of specificity. The word "containment" in C-4 is simply wrong. (b) READING ORDER is DOM order and is unconditionally guaranteed. (c) The single live consumer passes an OPACITY DIM, not a layout program: BrowsePane.vue:87-90 `'transition-opacity duration-fast ' + (pm.sortLoading.value ? 'opacity-50' : '')`; PalettesPane passes nothing. (d) The surviving half (a caller could pass `grid-cols-2` or `hidden`) does not distinguish `gridClass` from ambient Vue behaviour at all — a single-root component already merges fallthrough `class`, so removing the prop would change nothing about what a consumer can do. That is the actual finding, and it is redundancy, not unbounded authority (booked below).

killed.claim: "`EmptyState` is a demo-local primitive reached by a deep relative path; the grid has no shared collection-state primitive for loading/error/filtered empty." (challenge-L-library.md:9)
killed.refutation: Both clauses fail. killed.refutation: KILLED as stated: the child contract is documented IN-FILE at PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11 and is partly executable (o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:187-201 pins the TRUE-EMPTY composition on both hosts). killed.claim: "The component has no relation to the sortable/reorder library despite comments about `$el` and `useSortable`; the structural requirement is folklore rather than a typed adapter." (challenge-L-library.md:13)

killed.id: REG-PG-9 (adjudicated-registry row, not an axis row)
killed.claim: registry/adjudicated/PaletteCardGrid.md:36 — "the list has no accessible name, NONE CAN BE SUPPLIED (no prop, no attrs passthrough contract for it)"
killed.refutation: The parenthetical is false and should be struck; the underlying gap is real but is a call-site omission, not a missing mechanism. PaletteCardGrid.vue has a single element root (:2-6) and does NOT set `inheritAttrs: false` (there is no `defineOptions` anywhere in :35-45), so Vue's implicit fallthrough already delivers `aria-label` — and `role` — straight onto the root div, with fallthrough `role` overriding the template's own via `mergeProps`. `<PaletteCardGrid aria-label="Saved palettes">` names the list TODAY, with no code change. confirmed.proof: Structural half verified from vendor CSS: `.katex-mathml{border:0;-webkit-clip-path:inset(50%);clip-path:inset(50%);height:1px;overflow:hidden;padding:0;position:absolute;width:1px}` — the canonical visually-hidden-but-AT-exposed pattern; `clip-path` does not remove from the accessibility tree. `Katex.vue:41` sets `output: "htmlAndMathml"`, emitting `<semantics><mrow>…</mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">RAW TEX</annotation></semantics>` inside it. I read `probes/KTX-probe7.mjs`: it measures `getComputedStyle(ann).display` — a reliable computed-style read — reporting `block` on webkit vs `none` on chromium. The cure `.katex-mathml annotation { display: none }` is structurally sound (it is exactly Chromium's UA behavior; the presentation MathML in `<mrow>` is untouched). SEVERITY DISPUTED: rated BLOCKER, but the AT-announcement half rests on Playwright's `ariaSnapshot`, its own a11y serialization rather than a platform screen-reader read; and this is duplicate/verbose announcement, not content loss, cured by one CSS rule. MAJOR.

confirmed.claim: Display math overflows into a scroll container with zero affordance, no name, no role and no keyboard reach.
confirmed.proof: Structural half fully verified: the only overflow owner is `Markdown.vue:303` (`@apply overflow-x-auto`) inside the `> div.inline-block:has(> .katex-display)` rule at `:301-306`. All 49 lines of `Katex.vue` read — it emits no `tabindex`, no `role`, no `aria-label`, no mask, no fade, no `::after`; `Markdown.vue:301-306` adds none either. Vendor CSS forces the content wide: `.katex-display>.katex{...white-space:nowrap}`. The `content-visibility: auto; contain-intrinsic-size: auto 200px` at `Markdown.vue:107-108` is real and is exactly the measurement trap challenge-C:149-154 documents. The pixel geometry is live-only and I could not re-run it, but the two harnesses cross-validate (predicted 290px hidden at a 332px container; live probe4 measured `rootScrollW 622, rootClientW 332, maxScrollLeft 290`).

confirmed.claim: The math is a fourth typographic voice at a rogue 1.21x rung, entering through a vendored `font:` shorthand.
confirmed.proof: Vendor CSS read directly: `.katex{font:normal 1.21em KaTeX_Main,Times New Roman,serif;line-height:1.2;position:relative;text-indent:0;text-rendering:auto}`. 1.21 x 16 = 19.36 exactly, matching the measured `19.360001px`. The `font` shorthand also resets weight/style/variant/stretch and imposes `line-height: 1.2`, so the leading is imposed not inherited — that follows from the shorthand's own definition. 20 `@font-face` rules ship through the `Katex.vue:20` import (`grep -o "@font-face" katex.min.css | wc -l` → 20). The φ ladder it is off is real: `demo/styles/foundation.css:458-462` — `--phi-0: 0.382rem` / `--phi-1: 0.618rem` / `--phi-2: 1rem` / `--phi-3: 1.618rem` / `--phi-4: 2.618rem`.

confirmed.claim: Selecting a formula yields triple-duplicated text: HTML layer glyphs + MathML text + the raw LaTeX annotation.
confirmed.proof: Structurally certain from `Katex.vue:41` (`output: "htmlAndMathml"`) plus the vendor CSS: the MathML layer is hidden by `clip-path: inset(50%)` / `position: absolute` / 1px box, a technique that removes it from paint but not from selection or find-in-page. Its `<annotation encoding="application/x-tex">` carries the clean source. Neither layer carries `user-select: none` — no such rule exists in `Katex.vue`, `Markdown.vue` or `katex.min.css`. The three-way concatenation follows by construction.

confirmed.claim: The display block's centring axis is displaced by exactly half a φ-3 rung at every viewport.
confirmed.proof: Arithmetically exact from the tree, no measurement needed: `Markdown.vue:304` is `padding: var(--phi-1) 0 var(--phi-1) var(--phi-3);` — asymmetric, left-only. `demo/styles/foundation.css:461` gives `--phi-3: 1.618rem` = 25.888px at a 16px root; half is 12.944px, matching the reported 12.94px. killed.claim: "BLOCKER — RTL mirrors scientific notation: subscripts and superscripts swap sides" (challenge-D-design.md:94-125).
killed.refutation: Severity fails challenge-D's own stated vocabulary. challenge-D:88 defines BLOCKER as "loses or destroys content in a **shipped, default configuration**." RTL is not a shipped configuration: `demo/color-picker/index.html:11` is `<html lang="en" dir="ltr">`, hardcoded, and there is no direction switch anywhere — `grep -rn 'dir="rtl"|setAttribute("dir"|documentElement.dir' demo/ src/` returns exactly one hit and it is the *comment* at `index.html:6`. That comment block (`index.html:2-6`) describes `dir="ltr"` as "**RTL mechanical readiness** … the `dir` seam so `dir="rtl"` flips the whole document" — a readiness posture held for a future capability, not a mode any user can reach. D-1's own reproduction instruction (challenge-D:115-116) is `document.documentElement.setAttribute("dir","rtl")` — the auditor induced the state. The mechanism is real and cheap to cure (KaTeX inherits document direction — `grep -o "direction:[a-z]*" katex.min.css` yields only two `flex-direction` hits, confirming the vendor never sets it; `Katex.vue:2` emits no `dir` and no `unicode-bidi: isolate`), but it is a MINOR RTL-readiness gap and must not be counted as one of D's two BLOCKERs.

killed.claim: "`content-visibility` reserves 200px for blocks that are 76–110px tall … across the four blocks that is ~360px of phantom height in a card that is itself the scroll container — a lying scrollbar and a scroll position that shifts as blocks are rendered." (challenge-D-design.md:495-506)
killed.refutation: The declaration carries the `auto` keyword, which D-14 quotes but does not read. Live: `demo/scenes/about/markdown/Markdown.vue:107-108` — `content-visibility: auto; contain-intrinsic-size: auto 200px;`. In `contain-intrinsic-size: auto <length>`, the `auto` prefix instructs the browser to remember the element's **last-rendered** size and substitute it for the 200px fallback on every subsequent skipped render. The 200px is a first-render-only placeholder, not a standing reservation. The claimed steady-state ~360px of phantom height, the "lying scrollbar", and the shifting scroll position all presuppose the non-`auto` form. At most this is a first-paint transient. The axes are inconsistent with each other here: challenge-C's measurement-trap note (challenge-C:149-154) depends on the same keyword semantics and gets them right.

killed.claim: "occluded: 110.61px → **190.4%** of the ink is above the header's bottom edge" (challenge-D-design.md:458-463).
killed.refutation: Arithmetic category error. The same block reports `formula ink: y = 129.98 … 188.06`, `ink height: 58.08px`, `header bottom edge: y = 240.59`. You cannot occlude 110.61px of a 58.08px-tall object. 110.61 = 240.59 − 129.98 is the *overshoot* of the header's bottom edge past the formula's top — a distance, not an occlusion. The correct statement is: 100% occluded, with 110.61px of overshoot. The headline "190.4%" is the ratio of a distance to an unrelated height and means nothing. The underlying finding survives and is real — `Markdown.vue:121` applies `scroll-m-20` to `> h1..h6` only, and the katex wrapper rule at `:301-306` sets no `scroll-margin`, so math is the only scroll target with 0. Carry at MINOR on the structural fact; drop the metric.

missed.claim: `@types/katex` is a redundant shadowed dependency, and challenge-L certifies it as clean in its negative proof.

Under `moduleResolution: bundler` the package's own `types` condition wins; `@types/*` is consulted only when a package ships none. `@types/katex` at `package.json:90` is therefore never resolved. challenge-L-library.md:41-43 records the opposite — "`katex` and `@types/katex` are correctly `devDependencies` … Those two boundaries are sound" — and repeats it in its negative-proof table (challenge-L:416, :526). A negative proof that certifies a redundant dependency as sound is a miss in a lens whose job is dependency hygiene.

superlatives: The AB-1 comment block at `demo/scenes/about/katex/Katex.vue:8-19`. Twelve lines that name the exact mechanism of a past catastrophic regression (a `@import` inside `<style scoped>` → Vite suffixed every selector with `[data-v-*]` → only the root div carried the attribute → all 231 rules matched nothing → body-sans HTML layer, a second visible MathML copy, a 6400px stretchy brace), name the cure, name why the cure is *structural* rather than incidental ("a script-side import is unscopeable by construction"), and cross-reference the sibling cure (R.W4-C1 in Markdown.vue). I verified the stake: `.katex-mathml{clip-path:inset(50%);height:1px;overflow:hidden;position:absolute;width:1px}` is the real rule that would have been dead. Highest-density defect provenance I found on this path — and challenge-C's K-11 independently re-audited the import and confirmed it correct (382 of 383 selectors anchored on `.katex*`; one `body{counter-reset}` leak).

The `htmlAndMathml` rationale at `Katex.vue:34-41`. It records not just the decision but the risk it accepted, by name and by engine: "MathML-only delegated glyph metrics to each browser's math engine — WebKit's MathML-Core is the least mature, an S-22 (Safari-truth) risk." challenge-C's K-1 then measured that exact engine and found the risk realized in a different form (`annotation` computing `display: block`). A comment that correctly predicts the class of its own eventual defect is rare and should survive verbatim through any cure.

The post-mortem at `demo/scenes/about/markdown/Markdown.vue:291-300`. Ten lines explaining why `:has(> .katex)` was a direct-child test that could never match (`div.inline-block > span.katex-display > span.katex`), why `:has(> .katex-display)` is "the display-block's true structure", and the second-order consequence nobody would have guessed — that once the stylesheet came alive, `.katex-display > .katex { white-space: nowrap }` is what let wide rows overflow. The coupling it documents is itself a defect (L-3/L-4/K-8/D-11 all found it), but the documentation of the coupling is exemplary.

challenge-C's measurement-trap disclosure (challenge-C-implementation.md:149-154). The auditor found that their own earlier probes (`KTX-probe1.mjs`, `KTX-probe3.mjs`) returned `scrollWidth === clientWidth === 462` — a false green — diagnosed it as `content-visibility: auto` (`Markdown.vue:107-108`, verified) returning the `contain-intrinsic-size` placeholder, published the falsified probes *alongside* the corrected one, and left an explicit warning for any future gate. Self-falsification, published rather than quietly discarded. It is also why I weight that axis's geometry above the other two.

challenge-C's K-7 mutation framing (challenge-C-implementation.md:339-353): "delete the entire body of `renderKatex` so the component renders an empty `<div>`; `npm test` passes, `npm run typecheck` passes, `npm run lint` passes, and the Safari visual matrix passes." I verified every leg independently — zero katex references in `test/` and `e2e/`, `assets/` outside `tsconfig.demo.json`'s include, `**/*.md` in the eslint ignores at `eslint.config.js:53`, 0 hits for katex/about in `visual/REPORT.json`, and `vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` exiting 0. One sentence that proves an entire gate stack vacuous, and it is exactly right.

The φ ladder and its comment at `demo/styles/foundation.css:455-462` — `--phi-0: 0.382rem` through `--phi-4: 2.618rem`, with "The docs body rhythm (Markdown.vue) AND the About pane's sectional padding read the same rungs — one ladder, never a re-hardcoded arbitrary value." D-13's 12.94px axis displacement falls out of it arithmetically (`--phi-3` 25.888px ÷ 2 = 12.944, from the asymmetric `padding: var(--phi-1) 0 var(--phi-1) var(--phi-3)` at `Markdown.vue:304`) with no measurement required. A token system honest enough that its defects are computable from source is a genuine asset.

killed.refutation: The attribution is backwards. The glass-ui root already ships `w-full max-w-lg` on the centred dialog — verified in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/dialog-TNRDkcE4.js: `ne = "fixed left-1/2 top-1/2 z-modal grid w-full max-w-lg gap-4 [--overlay-pad-inline:--spacing(6)] ... px-(--overlay-pad-inline) py-(--overlay-pad-block)"`, and dist/components/dialog/placement.css declares widths ONLY for the left/right sheet placements (`width: 75%; max-width: 24rem`), never for `center`. The consumer's `max-w-sm` (384px) is strictly MORE protective than the root, not the cause of the 320px full-bleed. The real defect is the producer's `w-full` with no viewport inset reserve, and it belongs to glass-ui. Consequently DialogContentProps (DialogContent.vue.d.ts:4-22) exposes no width axis at all, so "producer-owned width" is not a prop the consumer can reach — the cure requires a producer change the axis does not name as such.
