killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:10 — "hasPrev/hasNext are trusted instead of derived, allowing 'Page 1 of 2' with Previous enabled or Next disabled."
killed.refutation: REFUTED. Both named contradictions are arithmetically impossible in the live tree. `hasPrev = computed(() => page.value > 1)` and `hasNext = computed(() => page.value < pageCount.value)` — /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:45-46 and /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:56-57 — read the SAME `page`/`pageCount` refs that /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminAuditPanel.vue:84-87 (and AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:127-130) hand to PaginationBar.vue:39-41. "Page 1 of 2 with Previous enabled" needs hasPrev true at page===1, i.e. 1>1 — false. "Page 1 of 2 with Next disabled" needs hasNext false at page=1,pageCount=2, i.e. NOT(1<2) — false. There is no third consumer (grep for `PaginationBar` across /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo returns exactly AdminAuditPanel.vue:102 and AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:144). The axis mistook a permissive prop signature for an unsound derivation; the derivation is sound and centralised. The residual signature concern is already carried at INFO under L-2 — carrying it twice, once as a behavioural defect, is double-counting.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:11 — "Events do not include the destination, so parent and child can race against changing props."
killed.refutation: REFUTED AS DIAGNOSED, and the prescribed cure is structurally inert. PaginationBar is stateless: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:37-47 declares four props and two zero-payload emits and holds no ref, no local page, no watcher. Props flow one way; the child never writes. A "parent/child race" requires two writers to one value — there is exactly one writer (`page` lives in the composable, useAdminAudit.ts:37). Worse for the axis: the live handlers are bound as bare references, `@prev="audit.prevPage"` / `@next="audit.nextPage"` (AdminAuditPanel.vue:88-89, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:131-132), and `prevPage()`/`nextPage()` take NO parameters (useAdminAudit.ts:73,80) — so adding a destination to the emit would be silently discarded at every call site and would cure nothing. A real ordering hazard does exist, but it is two concurrent fetches inside the composable with no request identity (`entries.value = res.data`, useAdminAudit.ts:61, last-write-wins) — a different defect at a different locus, already carried under C-4/D-2, and unfixable from the event signature.

killed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:11 — "Events prev/next carry no target page, query generation, or request identity."
killed.refutation: REFUTED for the same reason as C-3 and by the same bytes. The observation is literally true (PaginationBar.vue:44-47 `prev: []; next: []`) but names no defect: the emitting component owns no page and no query, so it has no target, generation, or identity to carry. Request identity is a property of the fetch, and the fetch lives in /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:48-71 / useAdminFlagged.ts:59-79 — neither of which receives anything from this event, since both handlers are zero-arity. Threading identity through a presentational bar would invert the ownership the rest of the panel is built on (`pm.audit` / `pm.flagged` as the single state authority, /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:72-73, 245).

killed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:11 — "The bar disappears whenever pageCount <= 1; that conflates a verified single page with unknown count, loading, error, and invalid negative/zero totals."
killed.refutation: REFUTED on its two load-bearing limbs, and INVERTED on one. LOADING: the bar does NOT disappear during a load. `pageCount` is a computed over `total`, and `total` is never cleared on the way in (/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:51 sets only `loading.value = true`), so mid-load the bar keeps its previous value and stays mounted and interactive beside the skeleton (AdminAuditPanel.vue:36-38 vs :83-90). ERROR: the bar does not disappear either — it PERSISTS, because the catch block writes only `loadError` (useAdminAudit.ts:64-67) and leaves `total` intact. So the axis has the sign backwards on both, and the real defect is the opposite of the one alleged; I have re-derived it and filed it as M2 in `missed`. NEGATIVE/ZERO TOTALS: `Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/pageSize))` (:44) floors pageCount at 1 for any total ≤ 0, so "invalid negative totals" never reach the guard. The only surviving limb is "a verified single page looks like an unloaded panel" — and even that is disambiguated in practice, since the first-paint window (total=0 → pageCount=1 → hidden) is exactly the window the skeleton occupies (AdminAuditPanel.vue:36-38). Not carryable as written.

killed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:12 — "The live-region sentence is locally authored; other paginated surfaces can announce at a different phase."
killed.refutation: REFUTED — the divergence risk is empty because the set of "other paginated surfaces" is empty. PaginationBar.vue is the only paginator in the product: the admin directory (/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/) contains AdminAuditPanel, AdminFlaggedPanel, AdminListItem, AdminListSkeleton, AdminNamesPanel, AdminTagsPanel, AdminUsersPanel and PaginationBar, and a grep for page/offset/limit pagination markers across those .vue files returns hits only from PaginationBar's two call sites. Nothing else in /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo paginates. A single implementation cannot diverge from itself; the sentence at PaginationBar.vue:17-19 IS the one phase, applied uniformly. (The phase it picks is wrong — that is C-5/D-4, confirmed — but it is not inconsistent.)

killed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:13 — "This generic pattern belongs either in glass-ui or in a shared application collection package, not independently in each admin panel."
killed.refutation: REFUTED on its factual premise, and unproven on its prescription. The premise — that the pattern is reimplemented "independently in each admin panel" — is false: there is exactly ONE 48-line PaginationBar.vue, imported by exactly two panels (/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminAuditPanel.vue:102 and AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:144). It already is the shared collection the axis asks someone to create; no duplication exists to extract. On the prescription: glass-ui 7.0.0 ships no data-paginator to bypass — the nearest primitive is `PagerDots` (/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/pager-dots/PagerDots.vue.d.ts), whose props are `count` / `orientation` / `windowFit` / `pattern: "tabs"|"group"` — a carousel/deck snap rail with a tablist ARIA register, not a prev/next data pager over a server-offset query. Promoting PaginationBar to the producer may be a good idea; it is a proposal for a component with two consumers, not a boundary violation, and nothing in the tree supports SOURCE-RED on this ground.

missed.claim: M1 — Deleting the last item on the last flagged page strands the admin on a phantom page, and PaginationBar's own `v-if` deletes the only escape hatch. The panel then presents 20 real flagged palettes as an empty moderation queue, for the rest of the session.
missed.proof: All three axes gestured at "stale page after deletion" as a TEST CELL (challenge-C-implementation.md:15, challenge-D-design.md:19) and none executed it. Executed: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:93-103 `deletePalette` (and :81-91 `dismiss`) mutate state PURELY LOCALLY — `items.value = items.value.filter(...)` and `total.value = Math.max(0, total.value - 1)` (:98-99) — with no refetch and no re-clamp of `page`. Arithmetic (pageSize=20, useAdminFlagged.ts:51), verified by node: total=21, page=2 → pageCount=2, bar visible, page 2 holds 1 item. Admin deletes it → total=20 → pageCount = Math.max(1, ceil(20/20)) = 1 → `page` is still 2. Now /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:3 `v-if="pageCount > 1"` evaluates FALSE and UNMOUNTS THE ENTIRE BAR — including the Previous button, whose own `hasPrev` (page>1) is still true and which is the only control that could rescue the user. `items` is now [] so /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:37-41 renders the EmptyState "No flagged palettes." There is no route back: `page` is never reset anywhere in useAdminFlagged.ts (contrast AdminAuditPanel.vue:114, which does reset page on filter change — the flagged panel has no such path), and the composable is instantiated once at the composition root and provided app-wide (/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:73 `const flagged = useAdminFlagged();`, :245 `provide(ADMIN_PORT_KEY, adminPort)`), so the state survives every pane switch. Even remounting the panel does not help: `onMounted(() => flagged.loadFlagged())` (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:152) refetches at `offset = (2-1)*20 = 20` against total=20 → empty again. Only a full browser reload clears it. Why this is PaginationBar's defect and not only the composable's: line 3 converts a recoverable inconsistency (page>pageCount, which would still render a working Previous — the total=41 variant does exactly that, rendering "Page 3 of 2" with Previous live) into an UNRECOVERABLE one, purely because the guard tests pageCount instead of testing whether any navigation is still possible. A guard of `hasPrev || hasNext` would have made this self-healing. Severity MAJOR not BLOCKER: it needs ≥21 flagged palettes plus a delete on the final page, and a page reload recovers.

missed.claim: M2 — The bar survives the error state and paints a navigable ledger over a panel that has just declared the ledger unreachable — the exact pathology the repo's own codified "error ≠ empty" law was written to forbid, one surface over.
missed.proof: challenge-D-design.md:11 asserted the opposite (that the bar disappears and thereby conflates error with other states); the truth is inverted, and no axis caught it. In /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:64-67 the catch block writes ONLY `loadError.value`; `total.value` is deliberately untouched, so `pageCount` (:44) retains the value from the last successful load. In /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminAuditPanel.vue the error EmptyState is a v-else-if branch at :42-53 ("The ledger is unreachable.") but `<PaginationBar>` at :83-90 is OUTSIDE that chain entirely — a plain sibling. So after any non-first load failure (token expiry, backend restart, a failed Retry at :49) the admin sees, simultaneously, "The ledger is unreachable" AND a live "Page 2 of 5" with working arrows (PaginationBar.vue:3 is satisfied, :17-19 renders, :10/:24 are enabled). Clicking Next then increments `page` against a dead backend (useAdminAudit.ts:75) with no data and no rollback, so a later successful reload lands on an arbitrary offset. Identical shape in AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:22-33 vs :126-133. The law this violates is codified in this repo and cited in these very files: useAdminAudit.ts:65 "never costume a dead backend as a clear ledger" and AdminAuditPanel.vue:40-41 "error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as a clear ledger" (W5-5 / F-2). The panel obeys the law for its list; the pagination bar breaks it by costuming a dead backend as a NAVIGABLE one.

missed.claim: M3 — Activating the arrow that carries you to the last (or first) page destroys keyboard focus: the button disables itself under the user's own hands and focus falls to <body>. Deterministic, 100% reproducible, and structurally unfixable through the producer's current Button API.
missed.proof: No axis raised focus management at all — challenge-D-design.md:19 lists "keyboard/touch" as a required CELL but nothing was executed against it. Chain: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:24 binds `:disabled="!hasNext"`. Pressing Enter/Space on Next while on page N-1 runs `nextPage()` (/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:73-78) → `page` becomes N → `hasNext = page < pageCount` (:45) flips false → the prop becomes `disabled=true`. The producer then sets the NATIVE disabled attribute: in /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js the computed guard is `m = p.loading || p.disabled === !0 || p.disabled === "true"` and the applied binding is `disabled: h.value ? m.value : void 0` where `h = !asChild && as === "button"` — true here, since PaginationBar passes neither. Per HTML, disabling the focused element blurs it and resets focus to the document body (all three engines). The keyboard admin therefore loses their place at the exact moment they reach the end of the list, and must Tab from the top of the document to return to Previous. Same on the first page via `hasPrev` (PaginationBar.vue:10). It is aggravated by /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/styles.css:1 `.button:disabled { pointer-events: none }`, which also silently swallows the pointer user's follow-up tap. Note for the cure: the focus-preserving pattern (keep the control focusable, set `aria-disabled="true"`, no-op the handler) is NOT reachable from the consumer — Button.vue.d.ts:17 accepts `disabled` but the compiled component emits `aria-disabled` ONLY on the non-native branch (`"aria-disabled": !h.value && m.value ? "true" : void 0`), so with the default `as="button"` there is no way to get it. The honest fix is either a parent-side focus hand-off or a producer ask; a naive "just add aria-disabled" prescription would not compile against glass-ui 7.0.0. Marked CONFIRMED rather than needs-live because the blur-on-disable is specified behaviour, not an observation.

missed.claim: M4 — The bar is a bare <div> with no navigation landmark, no accessible group name, and no association between the two commands and the page sentence that describes them. A keyboard screen-reader user tabbing onto Next hears no positional context.
missed.proof: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:2-5 is `<div class="flex items-center justify-center gap-2 py-3">` — no `<nav>`, no `role`, no `aria-label`, and the live-region span at :17 carries no `id`, so neither button can `aria-describedby` it. Consequences: (a) the pagination control is not exposed in the landmark/rotor list, so an SR user cannot jump to it — on a panel whose list is 20 rows long, that is the difference between one gesture and a full traversal; (b) tabbing onto "Next page" (:25) announces only the name — the "Page 3 of 5" context at :18 is adjacent text, not part of either button's accessible name or description, so it is announced only AFTER activation via the live region, never before; (c) the two commands are not grouped, so their relationship is inferred from visual adjacency alone. This is a departure from an established house discipline, not an invented standard: the shell uses real landmarks — `<nav class="dock-band">` at /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/color-picker/App.vue:24, with /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/styles/shell.css:30 stating "The a11y landmarks are the two band rows" — and the producer's own pager primitive takes an explicit group name and a declared ARIA register (`ariaLabel`, `pattern: "tabs"|"group"`) at /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/pager-dots/PagerDots.vue.d.ts. The cure is three attributes and one id.

missed.claim: M5 — The buttons are icon-only in fact but do not declare it, so they miss the producer's square icon-command geometry and its coarse-pointer hit-target hook. (I explicitly killed the touch-target limb of this myself — the target is compliant by a different route.)
missed.proof: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:7-15 and :21-29 pass `variant`/`size`/`disabled`/`aria-label` and a lone chevron child, but never `iconOnly` — which /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:12-13 documents as exactly this case: "Square geometry for an accessibly named icon command." Because it defaults false (button-Bu9F4uU6.js, `iconOnly: { type: Boolean, default: !1 }`), two data hooks are withheld: `data-icon-only` and `data-control-target`. Consequence 1 (geometry, real): without `[data-icon-only]` the rule `.button[data-icon-only]{inline-size:var(--button-size);block-size:var(--button-size);padding:0}` (/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/styles.css:1) never fires, so the arrows keep `padding-inline: 0.75rem` from `.button[data-size="sm"]` and render as 40×36px lozenges instead of the producer's 36×36 square — off-register against every other icon command in a glass-ui app. Consequence 2 (hit target) — REFUTED BY ME, recorded so it is not re-raised: `[data-control-target]` is what receives `min-block-size/min-inline-size: 2.75rem` under `@media (pointer: coarse)` (/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/utilities/responsive.css:1, reached via accessibility.css), so the omission does drop that hook — but the target is compliant anyway, because the same media query sets `--ui-scale: 1.5` and `--control-floor: 2.75rem` (/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/light-dark.css:1), making `--control-h-sm = max(2.25rem*1.5, 2.75rem) = 3.375rem` (54px) tall and 0.75rem*1.5*2 + 1rem = 3.25rem (52px) wide. Both exceed 44px. There is no touch-target defect here and any cure prescribing one is wrong.

missed.claim: M6 — The hard-coded `h-4 w-4` on the chevrons silently defeats the producer's `--ui-glyph` scaling: on coarse pointers the capsule grows 1.5× to 54px while the glyph stays frozen at 16px, so the arrow reads as a pinprick in a large pill on touch devices.
missed.proof: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:14 and :28 set `class="h-4 w-4"` on the lucide chevrons. The producer intends to own this: `.button > svg:not([class*="size-"]) { inline-size: var(--ui-glyph); block-size: var(--ui-glyph) }` (/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/styles.css:1), with `--ui-glyph: calc(1rem * var(--ui-scale))` (/Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/sizing.css:1). The `:not([class*="size-"])` clause is the producer's DECLARED opt-out channel — a consumer that means to fix a glyph size is expected to say `size-4`. `h-4 w-4` contains no "size-" substring, so the producer rule matches and believes it is in control — but loses on layer order: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/styles/foundation.css:1 opens with `@import "tailwindcss"`, which declares `@layer theme, base, components, utilities;` (glass-ui's own dist/styles/index.css:1 declares the identical order), and the glass-ui rule sits in `@layer components` while `.h-4`/`.w-4` land in `@layer utilities` — later layer wins regardless of specificity. The repo already knows this mechanism and documents it in its own words at /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/styles/utils.css:127 ("it wins over the `@layer components` recipe by layer order"). Verified the class actually survives to the SVG: @lucide/vue 1.17 rebuilds `class` in its own `h("svg", …)` call (dist/esm/Icon.mjs) but the consumer class returns via Vue's functional-component fallthrough (class/style/listeners only), so the rendered element carries `lucide lucide-chevron-left-icon lucide-chevron-left h-4 w-4`. Net effect on a phone (`pointer: coarse` → `--ui-scale: 1.5`): the capsule is 54px tall and the glyph is 16px instead of the intended 24px — 30% of the button height where the producer specified 44%. Honest scope: the `h-4 w-4` idiom is repo-wide (15 occurrences of `class="h-4 w-4"`, 5 of `class="h-3 w-3"`, zero of `size-N` across /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo), so the locus is systemic and PaginationBar is one instance; but the mobile consequence is sharpest here, where the glyph IS the entire control.

missed.claim: M7 — The two arrow targets slide horizontally whenever the page label changes digit count, so the button moves out from under the cursor during exactly the repeat-click gesture the control is designed for.
missed.proof: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:4 lays the row out with `justify-center` and :17-19 puts the variable-width sentence between the two buttons. `tabular-nums` (:17) equalises digit WIDTHS but not digit COUNTS, so "Page 9 of 12" → "Page 10 of 12" widens the label by one character (~0.55em ≈ 3.3px at the 12px `--type-caption` floor) and, under centring, pushes each button outward by half of that. The user paging 8→9→10 has the Next button step away between clicks. This is a one-rung-down instance of the pathology the repo's own card-lock law exists to prevent — /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/DESIGN.md:67-78 names TWO required mechanisms, "Tabular figures" AND "`ch` worst-case reservation … so sign flips, added decimals, and unit swaps re-ink the SAME box instead of re-flowing the row", the second of which is absent here (:17 has `px-2` but no `min-width` in `ch`). Stated fairly: the law's literal trigger is "live numeric values render at display scale" and this is the caption rung, and the containing CARD rect does not move — so this is an extension of the principle, not a law violation, and the magnitude is a few pixels. Filed MINOR on the Fitts's-law ground (moving an interactive target between repeat activations), and flagged as a legitimate downgrade candidate to INFO. The cure is one `min-w-[Nch]`, derived the same way ColorComponentDisplay's readoutReservation.ts derives its table.

superlatives: ZERO BESPOKE SURFACE. /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue is 48 lines with no <style> block, no scoped CSS, no keyframes, no rAF loop, no local ref and no watcher — it delegates 100% of chrome and motion to the producer Button (press spring, focus-ring, tap-squish, and the PRM guard `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){.button{transition:none}}` at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/styles.css:1). Independently corroborated: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md:274 vacuously clears PaginationBar on ALL THREE axes for having no motion content. In a repo whose constellation audit found a ~40-site 'PRM-RAF epidemic', a component that ships nothing to gate is the correct answer, not a gap.

ICON-ONLY A11Y DONE COMPLETELY, AND DATED. Both commands carry `aria-label` ("Previous page" :11, "Next page" :25) AND both decorative chevrons carry `aria-hidden="true"` (:14, :28) — the second half is the half almost everyone forgets, and I verified it survives lucide's own class/attr rebuild to the rendered <svg>. The provenance comment at :6 (`<!-- W5-a11y: icon-only pagination buttons need aria-labels -->`) ties the decision to the tranche-A W5 accessibility wave, so the intent is auditable from the source alone. Note that CHALLENGE-D itself concedes this (challenge-D-design.md:15, 'Icon-only buttons are named').

THE LIVE REGION IS CORRECTLY SPECIFIED. :17 declares `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` on the page sentence — polite (not assertive, which would rudely interrupt a moderator mid-row) and atomic (so "Page 3 of 5" is announced as one unit rather than a fragment). The phase it fires at is wrong (C-5/D-4, confirmed), but the register itself is textbook, and most hand-rolled paginators ship no live region at all. CHALLENGE-D:14 concedes 'The live page sentence is useful' — it is, and the fix is a one-line move of WHEN, not a rewrite of WHAT.

TABULAR FIGURES DECLARED WHERE THE LAW DID NOT EVEN REQUIRE THEM. :17 carries `tabular-nums` on the numeric sentence. /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/DESIGN.md:67-70 mandates this for readouts 'at display scale'; this label is at the caption rung, the smallest in the system, and the author applied the law anyway. That is the discipline of someone who understood the doctrine rather than pattern-matched it.

THE DERIVATION DISCIPLINE IN THE CONSUMERS IS WHY TWO ACCUSATIONS DIED. /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:44-46 and useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57 derive all four pagination scalars from the single pair (total, page) — `Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/pageSize))`, `page < pageCount`, `page > 1` — and both panels forward exactly those computeds (AdminAuditPanel.vue:84-87, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:127-130). The `Math.max(1, …)` floor in particular is what makes C-1's negative/zero-total limb unreachable. The corpus assumed four unrelated scalars; the tree has one source of truth and three views of it.

IT IS ALREADY THE SHARED ABSTRACTION THE LIBRARY AXIS DEMANDS. One 48-line file, two consumers (AdminAuditPanel.vue:102, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:144), identical prop and event wiring at both call sites, and no second paginator anywhere in /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo. challenge-L-library.md:13 asks for it to stop living 'independently in each admin panel' — it never did.

THE PROSE IS PLAIN AND CORRECT. 'Page {{ page }} of {{ pageCount }}' (:18) — no cute copy, no ornament, no em-dash affectation, on a moderation surface where a clever label would be a liability. It matches the plain register the sibling panels use for their machine readouts (AdminAuditPanel.vue:26-28 'N entries', with the correct entry/entries pluralisation).
unproven: UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE — whether two concurrent page fetches actually RESOLVE out of order against the running API. The absence of any request-identity guard is static and proven (`entries.value = res.data`, /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:61, last-write-wins; no generation counter, no AbortController in either composable), and the double-activation window is proven reachable (C-4). Whether real interleaving occurs, and how wide the window is against the live Hono/Mongo backend, is a network-timing question a static read cannot settle. Do not carry 'out-of-order responses' as a demonstrated failure without a probe.

UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE — the perceived screen-reader experience of the premature announcement (C-5/D-4). The DOM mutation ordering is proven (sync `page.value++` at useAdminAudit.ts:75 flushes the live region before the async `entries` write at :61), but whether NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver actually voice 'Page 3 of 5' before the row region settles, and whether the polite queue coalesces it, requires an AT probe. The ordering defect stands; the audible consequence is asserted, not measured.

UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE — the exact rendered geometry of the arrows on a coarse-pointer device (M5/M6). The cascade derivation is sound and I stand behind it (layer order fixed by `@import "tailwindcss"` at /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/styles/foundation.css:1; coarse `--ui-scale: 1.5` at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/light-dark.css:1), but the 54px-capsule / 16px-glyph figures are computed by hand from tokens, not read from a live getComputedStyle. A single DevTools read on a coarse-pointer emulation would settle both the glyph freeze and the 40×36 lozenge geometry.

UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE — whether `variant="outline"` is observable in the served DOM. The chain is fully derived (Button declares no `variant` prop and no `inheritAttrs: false`; reka-ui Primitive hand-applies every attr via `h(props.as, attrs, ...)` at node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Primitive/Primitive.js:26), so it should emit `<button variant="outline">`. This limb is secondary — the load-bearing and fully-proven part of D-5/L-1 is that the prop selects nothing and the arrows render at emphasis="secondary". If a probe ever contradicts the attribute leak, D-5 and L-1 still stand.

NOT A DEFECT, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT RE-RAISED — text contrast passes. The label at PaginationBar.vue:17 is `text-caption text-muted-foreground`, the smallest-and-faintest pairing in the app. Computed: `--muted-foreground: var(--neutral-5)` = hsl(30 22% 40%) on `--background: var(--neutral-0)` = hsl(40 30% 98%) gives a WCAG contrast ratio of 5.21:1, clearing the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold; `--type-caption: clamp(0.75rem, 0.71rem + 0.21vw, 1rem)` floors at 12px. Tokens at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/light-dark.css:1 and typography/scale.css. No finding.

OUT OF LENS, FLAGGED FOR THE C AXIS — PaginationBar has ZERO test coverage. Greps for 'Pagination', 'Previous page' and 'Next page' across /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/test and /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/e2e return nothing. challenge-C-implementation.md:15 prescribes a required test matrix; none of it exists, and M1 (the delete-strand) is precisely the cell that would have caught the worst defect in this component.

killed.claim: The Close affordance is "16x16 — under WCAG 2.5.8's 24x24", filed as a normative AA failure.
killed.refutation: The geometry is confirmed (see D-15/C-15) but the normative claim is overstated. WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) carries an explicit Spacing exception: an undersized target conforms if a 24 CSS-px diameter circle centred on its bounding box does not intersect another target or another undersized target's circle. The close control is positioned `absolute right-(--overlay-pad-inline) top-(--overlay-pad-block)` — a 24px inset in the dialog's top-right corner with no neighbouring target anywhere near it (the nearest is the first radio, a full header + description block below). The exception is satisfied, so this is not a 2.5.8 failure. It remains a legitimate ergonomic and internal-consistency defect, and D-15's framing — 16px against the 44px floor the same producer applies to the radios in the same dialog — is the correct one to carry.

The file has not been touched since 2026-07-17, so this is seat drift, not tree movement — note the L seat separately recorded that HEAD had moved to `ed047306` under the brief. killed.claim: "The dialog names palette B, the note about palette A is still in the box, Copyright violation is still selected, and Report is armed. One Enter files it."
killed.refutation: Overstated on the input mechanics. On reopen, initial focus lands on the first radio (measured by the C seat's probe P6 and consistent with reka's roving tabindex); Enter does not activate a radio — Space does — and Enter on a radio in a group with no `<form>` ancestor (there is none; FlagReportDialog.vue:15 wraps the body in a plain `<div>`) submits nothing. Filing the pre-armed report requires a click on Report, or Tab-to-Report then Enter/Space. The DEFECT is fully confirmed and remains a BLOCKER — a moderation dialog that reopens pre-armed against a different subject with a stranger's prose in the box — but the one-keystroke framing does not hold and should not be carried into a wave spec as written.

killed.claim: "Cancel renders in full-strength white; Report (disabled) renders muted. In dark mode the dialog's visually affirmative button is 'Cancel'."
killed.refutation: Rhetorically inverted causation. The observed asymmetry is entirely the `disabled` state, not a dark-scheme design inversion: the compiled Button adds `glass-capsule-hover` only when `isNeutralGlass && !disabled`, and native `disabled` applies the producer's disabled opacity. In light mode the identical asymmetry exists; with a reason selected the two become byte-identical in BOTH schemes (which is D-1's own measurement). The real defect is D-1 — there is no destructive register at all — and the dark frame adds nothing to it. D's §2.2 textarea observation (`rgb(11,10,9)`, a near-black hole punched through the glass) is the part of that section that survives and it is confirmed under D-4.

missed.claim: The disabled Report button is REMOVED FROM THE KEYBOARD TAB ORDER — the destructive primary action does not exist for a keyboard or AT user until a reason is chosen, with no announcement of the gate. The corpus's own evidence contains this defect and all three axes read it as a positive.
missed.proof: LIVE: FlagReportDialog.vue:43 `:disabled="!reason || submitting"`. glass-ui Button's compiled setup (dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js) computes `isNativeButton = !asChild && as === "button"` (default `as: "button"` → true) and binds `{ disabled: isNativeButton ? blocked : undefined, "aria-disabled": !isNativeButton && blocked ? "true" : undefined }` — so this renders a NATIVE `disabled` attribute, not `aria-disabled`. A natively disabled button is not focusable and is skipped by sequential focus navigation. There is no `aria-describedby` on it and no live region anywhere in the file explaining why. THE TELL: challenge-C-implementation.md:584-586 (Negative results #4) records the measured tab cycle as "textarea → Cancel → Close → radio → textarea → …" and files it as evidence that "The focus trap is intact." Report is absent from that cycle — the seat measured the defect and scored it as a pass. D's state table (challenge-D-design.md:637) gets closest with "disabled (Report) | partial | opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed and no explanation" but names only the visual limb, never the focus-order consequence. The producer ships the correct alternative on the same component: `loading` suppresses activation while keeping the control reachable and sets `aria-busy`.

missed.claim: The producer had ALREADY solved the radio target geometry with a token-derived gap, and the consumer's `class="flex flex-col gap-2"` — which is also redundant with the producer's own layout — is what breaks it. missed.proof: LIVE: glass-ui.css `.radio-group{--radio-face:1.125rem; --radio-seat:var(--touch-target,2.75rem); --radio-seat-offset:calc((var(--radio-seat) - var(--radio-face))/-2); align-items:flex-start; gap:calc(var(--radio-seat) - var(--radio-face)); flex-direction:column; display:flex}` — the producer sets `display:flex`, `flex-direction:column` AND a 26px gap computed from the same two tokens that size the 44px seat and the 18px face, so the seats tile exactly. FlagReportDialog.vue:16 passes `class="flex flex-col gap-2"`: the first two utilities restate what the producer already declares, and `.gap-2` (Tailwind `@layer utilities`) outranks `.radio-group`'s gap (I brace-walked glass-ui.css and confirmed `.radio-group` sits at depth 1 inside `@layer components{`), collapsing 26px to 8px. challenge-D-design.md:343-345 attributes the failure to "the consumer sets the row rhythm with `class=\"flex flex-col gap-2\"` — an 8px gap on an 18px glyph", i.e. a rhythm never chosen, when in fact a correct rhythm was overwritten. This is edict 5 in its purest form — a per-instance override defeating a root-level decision — and no axis recognised it as such.

superlatives: THE SERVER BOUNDARY IS EXACTLY HONOURED, TWICE, IN A FILE THAT GETS ALMOST EVERYTHING ELSE WRONG. FlagReportDialog.vue:33 `maxlength="500"` matches api/src/modules/palette/schema.ts:72 `detail: z.string().max(500).optional()` to the character (the C seat's probe P7 measured `typedLen=500 sentDetailLen=500`), and FlagReportDialog.vue:94 `detail.value.trim() || undefined` correctly collapses a whitespace-only detail to `undefined` rather than shipping `""` — matching `.optional()` rather than merely satisfying it (probe: `body={"reason":"other"}`, detail absent). Two hand-copied constants, both correct, both aligned with the semantic and not just the numeric contract. L-3 is right that the copy has no type link; it is worth recording that the copy is nonetheless right.

THE ONE TYPE DECISION THE FILE MAKES ITSELF IS CONFORMANT. FlagReportDialog.vue:23 puts `text-small` on the option labels — exactly the role docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:75 mandates ("control or label, including dropdown options | `text-small` | Plus Jakarta Sans, non-bold"). Every type defect in this file (D-10) is an INHERITED producer default the component failed to override; the one rung it chose for itself is the right one.

THE LABEL/RADIO WIRING IS CORRECT AND NON-OBVIOUS. FlagReportDialog.vue:22-23 derives `:id="`reason-${r.value}`"` and `:for` from the same reason value — stable, collision-resistant ids — onto a `<button role="radio">`. `button` is a labelable element, so `<label for>` legitimately binds and clicking the label text selects the radio (verified by the C seat, probe P1: `label[for="reason-copyright"]` click → `{"id":"reason-copyright","checked":"true"}`). Hand-rolled radio lists get this wrong far more often than they get it right.

THE PROVENANCE COMMENT AT FlagReportDialog.vue:5-8 IS HOW A KNOWING DEVIATION SHOULD BE RECORDED. It names the tranche and finding (`T.W4-6 (T-15/F7)`), states the producer default it is overriding (`the producer DialogTitle default is the body-voice text-subheading`), states the intent (`the demo's dialog headers join the display voice (≤500 non-bold)`), and — the rare part — records its own retirement condition (`Producer-root candidate recorded with the W4-6 sweep`). D-10 is correct that the patch shipped and the root fix did not; but as CRAFT, a self-documenting override that carries its own exit criterion is strictly superior to a silent one, and this repo should propagate the form even while it discharges the debt.

STRUCTURAL HYGIENE IS GENUINELY CLEAN. 101 lines, one concern, no god module. The component registers zero lifecycle hooks, zero listeners, zero observers, zero timers and zero `requestAnimationFrame` — I re-verified this by reading the whole file — so it is constitutionally immune to the constellation-wide PRM-RAF epidemic, and it makes no contact with WebGL, parsing or `ValueUnit`. None of the repo's named hazard classes land here. Recorded by the C seat as Negative result #7 and worth keeping.

THE C SEAT'S CONTROL DISCIPLINE IS THE BEST METHODOLOGICAL ARTEFACT IN THE CORPUS. challenge-C-implementation.md:566-575: a candidate finding (the dialog's enter transition stalled >1s, invisible and blurred, with three CSSTransitions at `currentTime:0`) was FALSIFIED by re-running the identical trace under WebKit (`currentTime:115` at t≈100ms, fully settled by t≈400ms), attributed to headless-Chromium/SwiftShader frame starvation, and NOT REPORTED — with the reusable fleet warning that any Chromium+SwiftShader capture of a `glass-reveal` overlay in this repo can photograph a transparent or blurred element. A seat that hunts its own false positives and publishes the negative is doing L-18's job before L-18 arrives.

D-5 IS THE FINEST MEASUREMENT IN THE THREE FILES AND IT REPRODUCES EXACTLY FROM SOURCE TOKENS. challenge-D-design.md:328-357 reports `radioSeatH: 44`, `faceDiameter: 18`, `radioPitch: 30.95`, three overlap pairs at `13.05px`, and an `elementFromPoint` probe at each midpoint returning the LOWER radio. I re-derived every number statically from `--radio-seat: var(--touch-target, 2.75rem)`, `--radio-face: 1.125rem` and `--radio-seat-offset: calc((44 - 18)/-2)`: 44 − 30.95 = 13.05, to the hundredth, three times. Finding an invisible target-overlap that no screenshot can show, quantifying it, and probing the hit-test to prove which control actually receives the tap — that is the standard the rest of the corpus should be held to.

A deliberate, unglamorous correctness detail: it is precisely what stops the globe from collapsing to a sliver when the label wraps at 320px, the failure mode D-8 documents (challenge-D-design.md:501-503). The author saw the wrap risk; only the `justify-start` half of the recipe was wrong.

COMPONENT — the pluralization is correct at the 0/1/n boundary: `const s = n !== 1 ? "s" : ""` (:81-82), verified by probe at count=1 and count=137 (challenge-D-design.md:623-627) with no overflow and no truncation. Trivial to get wrong; got right.

COMPONENT — `v-if="mode === 'switch'"` at :23 is doing real safety work. demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:94-99 has no `transfer` branch, so rendering that action in regenerate mode would produce a silent no-op. C-7 is right that a v-if is not a type system — but the guard is correct, and it is the reason the hole has never fired.

CORPUS — challenge-D-design.md:652-678, the state-coverage table. The strongest artifact in the three files: it enumerates every state the component can occupy — empty, populated, loading, error, success, dismissed, disabled, focused, hovered, pressed, selected, dragging, overflowing, RTL, reduced-motion, forced-colors, 200% zoom, 320px, dark — dispositions each against evidence, and refuses to fake the two it could not reach ("RTL … not probed", "forced-colors … not evaluable in WebKit"). That refusal is what makes the other seventeen rows worth reading.

CORPUS — challenge-C-implementation.md:558-599, the negative-results section: thirteen named repo hazards (the defineModel async round-trip, ValueUnit nesting, stableHue drift, the PRM-rAF epidemic, WebGL context loss, listener leaks, verbatimModuleSyntax, Vue 3.5 idiom, parseCssColor) attacked and cleared so that absence reads as evidence rather than omission. CORPUS — challenge-L-library.md:293-301, the self-refutation block. The seat raised two hypotheses that would have made its own MAJOR finding far more damaging (duplicate component identity across the root/subpath entrypoints; CSS side-effect retention defeating tree-shake), tested both, and recorded both as REFUTED with the chunk hash and the closure walk that killed them — then explicitly downgraded its own finding to "dev-time ergonomics plus the standing-edict violation". missed.claim: PaletteColorStrip's celebrated '8% legibility floor' is arithmetically cancelled by its own renormalisation, and is mathematically unreachable for any palette of 13 or more colours — including the 24-colour palette every probe in this folder used as its fixture. The D axis names this logic as the one genuinely good design in the folder.
missed.proof: `demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteColorStrip.vue:60-68`: `floored = effective.map(w => Math.max(w/total, WEIGHT_FLOOR))` then `flooredTotal = sum(floored)` then `return floored.map(x => (x/flooredTotal) * 100)`. Because every share already sums to 1, flooring can only raise the sum, so `flooredTotal ≥ 1` whenever the floor engages — and the renormalisation then divides the floor back down. Ran the shipped function verbatim: `n=24 equal → 4.17% each` (floor undershot by 48%); `n=13 equal → 7.69%`; `n=11` with one dominant weight `[90,1×10] → 52.94%, 4.71%×10`; `n=6` `[95,1×5] → 70.37%, 5.93%×5`; the realistic quantiser case `[50,25,15,8,2] → …, 7.55%, 7.55%`. For n ≥ 13 the floor cannot be met at all, since 13 × 0.08 > 1. The stated invariant at `:38-48` ('Segments size proportionally with an 8% floor so small clusters stay legible') is never delivered, and the failure is worst exactly where it matters most — many-colour extracted palettes with one dominant cluster.

killed.id: K1 — L-1 mechanism + L-2 cure (the corpus's single most load-bearing causal claim)
killed.claim: L-1:99-101 — "the barrel is a type-erasing hop: it re-exports the value binding without restating the contract, so a call site can keep passing a prop the real component deleted and nothing on the path objects"; L-1:106-110 and L-2:188-191 — "execute L-1 … with the alias layer gone and imports pointing at `@mkbabb/glass-ui/button`, `vue-tsc` types the props directly and every one of the 51 sites becomes a compile error rather than a silent visual defect."
killed.refutation: FALSE, and refuted by direct counterexample in the live tree. (1) A TypeScript `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui"` re-export is type-preserving — it resolves to the same declaration; it cannot erase props. The repo proves barrels forward types when types exist: demo/ui/badge/index.ts exports `badgeVariants, type BadgeVariants`, and demo/ui/alert/index.ts exports `type AlertVariants`. (2) DECISIVE COUNTEREXAMPLE, no barrel anywhere in the path: demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:70 imports `WatercolorDot` DIRECTLY from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/watercolor-dot` and :45-47 pass `tag="div"`; demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:62 imports it the same direct way and :17,:32 pass `tag="button"`. The producer's props are `{color, variant, animate, cycleDuration, range, seed}` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts:23-51) — there is no `tag`. `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` at HEAD 5e146edd -> exit 0, zero diagnostics. Direct subpath imports do NOT make an unknown prop a compile error. (3) The real gate hole is `vueCompilerOptions.strictTemplates`, which is absent from every tsconfig in the repo (`grep -rn strictTemplates tsconfig*.json package.json` -> no hits), so Vue's fallthrough-attribute allowance is unconstrained. DEFECT-LEDGER.md (~:22422) names the correct cure in its own text — "plus `vueCompilerOptions.strictTemplates: true` so the class cannot recur" — which L-1/L-2 dropped in favour of the directory deletion. NET: deleting `demo/ui/` would leave all 51 sites exactly as silent as they are today. The L-1 observation survives as a MINOR duplication/dual-path finding; its BLOCKER severity, its mechanism, and the cure L-2 hangs on it do not.

killed.id: K2 — the cure shared by L-5, C-4, D-2, D-17 and D §6
killed.claim: L-5:360-363 "glass-ui's `Button` already owns this affordance: `ButtonProps.loading` … 'Marks an in-flight command and suppresses activation until it settles'"; C-4:294-298 "Delete `Loader2`, delete the `@lucide/vue` import, delete `mr-2 h-4 w-4 animate-spin`, and bind `:loading="submitting"`"; D-17:604 "Producer `Button loading` replaces the whole line"; D §6:678 lists `Button loading` as the primitive that already exists for `Loader2 + submitting`.
killed.refutation: The producer's `loading` prop renders NO visible indicator. The compiled Button (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js) emits `data-loading`, `aria-busy` and a computed disabled state, and its template body is nothing but `renderSlot($slots, "default")` — there is no spinner node. Across ALL of glass-ui's shipped CSS, `grep -rn "data-loading" --include='*.css' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` matches exactly two files, and the only Button rule is `components/button/styles.css:1` -> `.button[data-loading] { cursor: progress; }`. There is no `::after` spinner, no keyframe, no `[aria-busy]` styling. So `loading` supplies SEMANTICS (activation suppression + aria-busy + a cursor), not an affordance. Executing the prescribed cure as written would delete the only visual in-flight mark the component has and replace it with a mouse cursor — strictly worse for touch and for the exact slow-network case C-4 measured. The correct cure keeps a rendered indicator in the Button's default slot (or relays a producer spinner to glass-ui) IN ADDITION to `:loading`. The defect (C-4/L-5/D-2: the spinner is unreachable) stands; the cure all three axes converge on is unsound.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:555-558 — "`role=\"dialog\"` … and **no `aria-modal`**, despite a working focus trap … Assistive tech is not told the background is inert." Routed as a glass-ui BH relay.
killed.refutation: The observation is true and the consequence is false. `grep -rn aria-modal node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Dialog/` -> zero hits, so `aria-modal` genuinely never renders. But reka-ui/dist/Dialog/DialogContentModal.js:45 calls `useHideOthers(currentElement)`, which applies `aria-hidden` to every sibling of the content node — assistive technology IS told the background is inert, by the stronger of the two mechanisms (aria-hidden removes the content from the tree; aria-modal merely asks the AT to behave as if it were). Omitting `aria-modal` while using hideOthers is a deliberate, widely-adopted pattern. Two further corrections: the finding is routed to the wrong owner (reka-ui renders the `role="dialog"` element at DialogContentImpl.js:77 — glass-ui never touches it), and it is not consumer-actionable at all. Downgrade to INFO at most; do not carry as a defect against this component.

missed.claim: PRODUCER TOKEN CONFLICT, repo-wide: glass-ui overrides its own `--radius` with Tailwind's compiled default at a WINNING cascade layer, so every `--radius`-derived token resolves to 4px instead of the design system's declared 10px. This is the actual cause of the 4px L-8 measured, of the 4px the DEFECT-LEDGER measured on skeletons, and of every 'shadcn-era `rounded-input`' judgement in the corpus.
missed.proof: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/theme/radius.css:1 declares `@theme { --radius: 0.625rem; … --radius-lg: var(--radius); --radius-input: var(--radius); --radius-button: var(--radius); }` — the design system's intent is 10px. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/components.css:1 (a compiled-Tailwind artifact — the same file also carries `.pointer-events-auto{…}`, `.sr-only{…}`) ships `:root { … --radius: 0.25rem; --radius-lg: 0.5rem; --radius-sm: 0.25rem; --spacing: 0.25rem; --text-sm: 0.875rem; … }` — Tailwind's stock defaults. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/index.css:1 declares `@layer theme, base, components, utilities;` and then imports that file as `@import "./components.css" layer(components)` — the components layer WINS over the theme layer, so Tailwind's `--radius: 0.25rem` beats glass-ui's `--radius: 0.625rem` at `:root` for the whole document. `--radius-input: var(--radius)` therefore computes to 4px (matching L's live read of `0.25rem` and the rendered `border-radius: 4px`), and `--radius-lg` is overridden outright to 0.5rem. demo/styles/foundation.css:57 pulls this in via `@import "@mkbabb/glass-ui/styles"`. All three axes stopped at the symptom: L-8:504-506 concluded "it is inheriting from glass-ui's `--radius` (also `0.25rem`), which means the demo has no independent input radius at all" — treating 0.25rem as the design system's value rather than as a leaked default that outranks it; C and D never touched the token. Cure is a BH relay: the producer must not ship its compiled theme defaults inside `layer(components)` (or must re-declare its own tokens after it). Fixing it moves `--radius-input` from 4px to 10px, at which point demo/DESIGN.md:195's "8 px" is still wrong but the diagnosis in L-8's cure ("define `--radius-input: 0.5rem` in `demo/styles/`") becomes an actively harmful consumer-side override of a producer token.

missed.claim: D-5's mechanism is inverted: the 13px radio overlap is not a producer 'coarse-pointer floor' spilling — it is the CONSUMER'S ONE CLASS defeating a compensating producer invariant. The cure is a deletion, not a LabeledField re-composition, and the overlap is present with a mouse.
missed.proof: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/radio-group/styles.css:1 defines the seat AND its compensation together: `--radio-face: 1.125rem`, `--radio-seat: var(--touch-target, 2.75rem)`, `--radio-seat-offset: calc((var(--radio-seat) - var(--radio-face)) / -2)`, `.radio-group__item { block-size: var(--radio-seat); margin: var(--radio-seat-offset) }` (a 44px box occupying 18px of layout) AND `.radio-group { gap: calc(var(--radio-seat) - var(--radio-face)) }` = 26px — so the producer's own 44px seats tile EXACTLY, edge to edge, with zero overlap and no visual bloat. FlagReportDialog.vue:16 overwrites that gap with `class="flex flex-col gap-2"` (8px) and :17-21 interposes `<div class="flex items-center gap-2">` rows so the items are no longer the group's own children: pitch collapses to row(~23px)+gap(8px)=31px against a 44px seat -> 13px of overlap, three times, exactly D's measured 13.05px and 30.95px. killed.claim: BLOCKER: "the four corners of the S×V domain are not hit-testable … pure white and the pure fully-saturated hue cannot be selected by any input this component accepts. A colour picker that cannot pick white."
killed.refutation: REFUTED at the headline. MiniColorPicker.vue:129 takes `setPointerCapture` on pointerdown, so every subsequent `pointermove` is retargeted to `.sv-canvas` regardless of where the pointer is, and `updateCanvas` (:134-140) clamps both axes with `Math.max(0, Math.min(1, …))`. A drag begun anywhere inside the field and carried past the top-left corner therefore lands exactly `sat = 0, val = 1`, and `currentHex` (:85-105) with s=0, v=1 yields r=g=b=1 → `#ffffff`. Past the top-right corner it lands `sat = 1, val = 1` = the pure hue. Drag-to-the-corner is the single most ordinary gesture in a colour picker. The probe that produced the claim never drags: probe-D2-4.mjs:45-56 issues only `page.mouse.click(x, y)` per corner, so it measured a corner *click* dead-zone (challenge-D-design.md:105-146) and generalised it to "any input this component accepts". RESIDUAL, real but MINOR: a fresh pointerdown inside the ~13.7px² quarter-disc outside the 8px radius does not actuate. The prescribed cure (challenge-D-design.md:142-146 — "the paint geometry and the hit geometry of a 2D colour domain must be separate concerns") does not follow from a defect a drag already routes around. The same refutation downgrades N-7's "the hue rail's right end does not actuate" (:319-332): `updateHue` (:153) clamps with `Math.min(360, …)`, so hue 360 is reachable by dragging past the end.

killed.claim: "that hand-rolled math disagrees on 4.2313% of the HSV lattice (39,730 / 938,961 samples)" — used to justify BLOCKER.
killed.refutation: The script behind it (`scratchpad/hsv-diff2.mjs`, challenge-L-library.md:115) died with the session and is not re-runnable, so the figure is unverifiable. The only persisted measurement, which I re-ran, disagrees on the rate and — decisively — bounds the error: `node probe-L9-hsv-magnitude.mjs` → 53361 samples, 6024 mismatches (11.29%), MAX |Δ| = 1 of 255, "no sample diverged by >=2 bytes". I confirmed the mechanism is a tie-break, not an algebraic error: `0.3 * 255 === 76.5` exactly, src/color/operations.ts:305-312 rounds half-to-even → 76, MiniColorPicker.vue:103 rounds half-up → 77. A ±1/255 difference cannot carry the framing at challenge-L-library.md:44-51. L-9 concedes exactly this at :501-516, which leaves L's own summary row (:649, "4.2313% measured disagreement") internally superseded by its own re-run. The duplication finding stands and is confirmed; the statistic and the severity it bought do not.

I replicated the component's exact reactive structure (lines 76-125) under the repo's own Vue 3.5.35 with jsdom: a bare mount with `hex="#4488cc"` emits `["#4488cc"]` and drives the parent's `colorText` to `"#4488cc"` with zero user interaction. missed.claim: A second, independent route into C-1's latched-drag state, which C-1's prescribed cure does not close.
missed.proof: MiniColorPicker.vue:127-131 sets `canvasDragging = true` (:128) BEFORE the unguarded `(e.target as HTMLElement).setPointerCapture(e.pointerId)` (:129), and identically at :142-146 for the rail. `setPointerCapture` throws `NotFoundError` for a stale or invalid `pointerId`; the throw aborts the handler, so `updateCanvas(e)` (:130) never runs and the flag is latched `true` with no capture taken and no pending `pointerup` on the element — C-1's exact end state, reached without any interruption. The canonical instrument guards the symmetric call: SpectrumCanvas.vue:83-87 wraps `releasePointerCapture` in `try { … } catch { // Element may be detached — safe to ignore }`. C-1's cure (challenge-C-implementation.md:59-66, bind `@pointercancel` and `@lostpointercapture`) cannot fire for a capture that was never taken, so applying it verbatim leaves this route open. Order the flag write after the capture, or guard the call.

missed.claim: The zero-rect guard is the one canonical cure every axis's enumeration omitted, and the clamp idiom the copy uses is NaN-transparent — with a concrete uncaught-throw tail.
missed.proof: `updateCanvas` (MiniColorPicker.vue:134-140) and `updateHue` (:149-154) divide by `rect.width` / `rect.height` with no zero check. SpectrumCanvas.vue:115 is exactly `if (rect.width === 0 || rect.height === 0) return;`, and the canonical file clamps with the library's own helper (:37 `import { clamp } from "@mkbabb/value.js/math"`) where the copy uses `Math.max(0, Math.min(1, x))` — which returns NaN for NaN (verified). Consequence chain, each step verified: NaN `sat`/`val` with a numeric `hue` reaches a matched case in the `switch` at :95-102, so `toHex(NaN)` = `Math.round(NaN).toString(16).padStart(2, "0")` = `"NaN"` and `currentHex === "#NaNNaNNaN"`; that is emitted (:107), written into the user's Input and into the trigger swatch's `backgroundColor` (SearchFilterBar.vue:177, :77); and if `Search` is then pressed, `hexToOklab` (:205-211) calls `parseColorIn` → `parsePickerColor` (demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:109-113) which THROWS `PickerColorError`, inside `applyColorSearchFromPicker` (:180-187), which has no error arm at all. Latent — a zero-size rect is hard to reach live — but C-1/C-6, L-2 and D §2 each enumerate SpectrumCanvas's cures (pointercancel, try/catch release, unmount teardown, rAF throttle, touch gate, `overflow: visible`) and none lists this one.

missed.claim: Wrong error at the wrong altitude in the sole consumer: the impossible failure is guarded, the reachable one escapes.
missed.proof: SearchFilterBar.vue:205-211 guards `if (L === "none" || a === "none" || b === "none") throw new Error("Hex color produced missing OKLab channels")`. OKLab is a rectangular space with no powerless channels, so for every input the picker or the `/^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i` gate at :218 can produce, that branch is unreachable dead code. The reachable failure — `parsePickerColor` throwing `PickerColorError` on an unparseable string (demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:112, `throw new PickerColorError("Invalid CSS color", result.diagnostics)`) — is unhandled at BOTH call sites: `applyColorSearch` (:213-225) uses `try`/`finally` with no `catch`, and `applyColorSearchFromPicker` (:180-187) has neither. The function is also misnamed: `hexToOklab` takes any string.

It is the standard consequence of implicit capture release on element removal, and the finding does not depend on it alone (Escape, outside click, the component's own `search` emit and route change all reach the same state).
superlatives: `demo/picker/controls/spectrumLuma.ts` (35 lines) is the repo teaching itself a law: `:4-9` names the three instruments that must agree about the same (s,v) region and states the rule — "Share the function, never copy the constant" — then `:20` and `:23-35` make sharing the only cheap option. A module whose entire purpose is to make a constant uncopyable is a genuinely excellent piece of design; the fact that MiniColorPicker walked past it (L-4) is a measure of the file's importance, not its failure.

`demo/picker/controls/SpectrumCanvas/SpectrumCanvas.vue` carries six independent cures in 272 lines, each with the reason written down: `:58-63` + `:205-210` `rawS`/`rawV` as the render source with a one-shot `spectrumIsSource` suppression ("Raw spectrum coords to avoid HSV roundtrip jitter") — the exact defect confirmed here as L-9/C-2; `:115` the zero-rect guard; `:81-91` a try/catch release annotated "Element may be detached"; `:168-175` lost-capture recovery; `:97-108` rAF coalescing with `:195-198` cancel-on-stop; `:217-224` unmount teardown. Three separate audit seats used this file as the standard of comparison, independently, and it held.

`vite.config.ts:37-50` generates the demo's seven self-aliases *from `package.json#exports`* with anchored regexes, so the demo physically cannot write a specifier a real npm consumer could not — and `:33-36` records the exact failure the anchoring prevents (a bare `.` prefix-match swallowing the `/math` subpath, "the R-era demo boot break"). The dogfood keystone is enforced by construction rather than by convention, which is why L-1's breach is legible as a breach at all.

`demo/palettes/browser/search/index.ts` is five lines that get encapsulation exactly right: a stated contract ("hardened public surface (T.W1 F7). NAMED re-exports only (PI-6)"), three named exports, and a deliberate omission of `MiniColorPicker`, which is consumed only by its sibling. `demo/palettes/browser/index.ts:35` re-exports precisely the same three. No barrel leak anywhere in the cluster.

`src/color/operations.ts:305-312` is a float-aware banker's rounder: the tie test is `Math.abs(fraction - 0.5) < Number.EPSILON * Math.max(1, Math.abs(value))`, epsilon-relative rather than exact. I watched it earn its keep — the library's own hsv→rgb for `hsv(0, 0, 0.3)` returns channels `[76.5, 76.5, 76.50000000000001]`, three values that a naive tie test would quantise to two different bytes and this one folds to `[76, 76, 76]`. A considered choice, not an accident.

`MiniColorPicker.vue:157-163` is the one thing this component gets right, and all three axes independently moved to protect it: the static black-to-transparent overlay lives in scoped CSS and only the dynamic `--hue` passes through `:style`, with the reason in the comment. D pass 1 negative proof #10 and D pass 2 §8.7 both explicitly instruct that it must survive into whatever replaces the file.

The L axis's own method note is the best sentence in the corpus: "a round-trip that starts on the quantised lattice cannot detect quantisation. Begin round-trip probes at the continuous input, never at the encoded one" (challenge-L-library.md:670-672), written while withdrawing its own first-pass negative. A programme that records why it was wrong, in a form the next seat can apply, is worth more than the finding it corrected — and the same failure shape is exactly what I found again in D pass 2's negative proof #2 (missed finding M2).

missed.claim: Drag-reorder corrupts the persisted order: VueUse's default `onUpdate` is still installed and synchronously splices the moved row OUT of the very array `filteredSaved` caches, before the site's own `onEnd` recomputes the id list from that same array.
missed.proof: PalettesPane.vue:183 passes `pm.filteredSaved.value` — a plain array snapshot, not a ref. node_modules/@vueuse/integrations/dist/useSortable.js builds `{...defaultOptions, ...resetOptions}`, and defaultOptions is `{onUpdate: e => moveArrayElement(list, e.oldIndex, e.newIndex, e)}`; the call site overrides only `onEnd` (:187), so the default onUpdate survives. In that same file `moveArrayElement` computes `const _valueIsRef = isRef(list); const array = _valueIsRef ? [...toValue(list)] : toValue(list)` — a non-ref argument means the ORIGINAL array is mutated: `array.splice(from, 1)` runs synchronously, and the re-insert is deferred to `nextTick`. node_modules/sortablejs/modular/sortable.esm.js dispatches `update` then `sort` then `end` in one synchronous block, so onEnd (PalettesPane.vue:187-196) runs while the array is one element short. useFilteredList.ts:8 returns `items.value` unchanged for an empty query, and usePaletteStore.ts:50-55 caches `savedPalettes` as a computed whose result array is exactly what was just spliced — mutating it dirties nothing, so `pm.filteredSaved.value` at :191 re-reads the SAME (n−1) array. Worked example [A,B,C,D,E], drag A from 0 to 2: onEnd builds ids=[B,C,D,E], removes ids[0]=B, re-inserts B at 2 → [C,D,B,E]; usePaletteStore.ts:153-166 then rebuilds the store from that list and appends the never-mentioned A at the end → [C,D,B,E,A] instead of [B,C,A,D,E]. challenge-D-design.md:566-617 (D3-10) quotes these exact lines verbatim and reads only the a11y/design surface; no axis inspected the wiring.

superlatives: PaletteColorStrip.vue:47-71 — the weighted-segment solver is the best code in the cone: it prefers explicit weights, falls back to the palette's own per-colour `weight` (so an extracted palette's population story rides on the palette itself, no twin strip), applies an 8 % legibility floor so small clusters survive, and then RENORMALISES by the floored total so the segments still sum to 100 %. The floor-then-renormalise step is the part most implementations get wrong.

PaletteCardMenu.vue:24-40 and :48-60 — the K-INV5 pattern: the doomed action is `:disabled="apiOffline"` AND names the degraded state in-register (a small-caps `offline` / `public` / `private` annotation), instead of firing a toast after the failure. The latch reads through an INJECTED seam (`useApiClient()`, :216) rather than a module singleton, so the leaf is testable.

usePaletteStore.ts:153-166 — `reorderPalettes` rebuilds from the id map and then appends every palette the caller did not mention, with the reason written down (:161-165). That defensive tail is the only reason the drag-reorder defect above is a wrong ORDER rather than silent data loss.

demo/color-session/useContrastSafeColor.ts:56-78 — `probeEpoch`: a documented, reactive cure for the detached-first-read problem (a computed evaluated during bottom-up mount would cache the static model referent forever), including the measured failure that earned it (3.59:1 against a real composited band). The paired `liveTintCache` (:234-251) stamps validity from DOM truth so a probe that raced a scheme flip self-heals on the next recompute. No polling, no workaround.

demo/palettes/browser/card/index.ts:1-3 — named-only re-exports with the rationale stated (SFC scoped <style> is a side-effecting import, so a star re-export would defeat per-consumer tree-shaking). Rare to see the reason recorded at the barrel.

PaletteRenameInput.vue — the one leaf built correctly: `useTemplateRef` (:48), a local draft with a resync watch (:49-51), focus+select on mount (:53-56), escape-to-cancel with `.stop` (:16), and a submit policy that treats an unchanged or empty name as a cancel (:58-65).

SwatchHoverMenu.vue:64-66 — `PANEL_LAYOUT` as a shared constant applied to BOTH the touch PopoverContent and the hover Teleport panel, explicitly so the two paths cannot drift. The right instinct, even though one of the two paths is the broken one.

PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11 — the comment explains why it is the div's FIRST CHILD rather than a sibling: a leading comment node would make the component multi-root and PalettesPane's `$el` read for useSortable would resolve to the comment. A real Vue hazard, documented at the exact point of risk.

missed.claim: The pointer-to-model map and the paint/marker map use DIFFERENT boxes. `updateCanvas` measures against `getBoundingClientRect()` — the BORDER box, 174x112 — while the gradient (default `background-origin: padding-box`) and the absolutely positioned thumb (containing block = padding box) both live in the 172x110 padding box. Sole cause: `border border-border` on the same element that owns both the paint and the hit test. Consequences: the column that RENDERS as the pure hue returns S = 172/174 = 0.9885; the column that renders as pure white returns S = 1/174 = 0.0057; and the marker sits up to 1px off the hand at the extremes (thumb at 1 + sat*172 while the pointer was at sat*174). This is the correctly-attributed version of what N-1 blamed on `rounded-lg`, and all three axes are blind to it because the canonical instrument cannot have it — SpectrumCanvas.vue declares a radius and `overflow: visible` and carries no border at all.

It records that `:has(> .katex)` was a direct-child test that could never match `div > span.katex-display > span.katex`, so the overflow-x container was dead with no error anywhere, and that the failure only became visible once the stylesheet came alive. Verified against the vendor rule that exposed it: `.katex-display>.katex{...white-space:nowrap}`.

Katex.vue:34-40 — the output:'htmlAndMathml' rationale is architecturally correct AND names its own residual risk unprompted ('WebKit's MathML-Core is the least mature, an S-22 (Safari-truth) risk'). Verified: katex.js:6070 puts aria-hidden='true' on the whole HTML layer, so MathML is the sole AX representation and dropping it would be strictly worse. A component that writes down the risk it is accepting is doing what most components do not.
