confirmed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:14 — "The root has role=list, but comments assume children use role=article; that is not equivalent to listitem and not enforced."
confirmed.proof: TRUE and worse than filed. Live: PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 `role="list"`; the only child component, PaletteCard.vue:22, declares `role="article"` (justified in its own comment at PaletteCard.vue:2). ARIA 1.2 gives `list` the required-owned-element `listitem`; `article` is not it, and neither consumer wraps the cards (PalettesPane.vue:82-83, BrowsePane.vue:92-93 both v-for `PaletteCard` as bare children). AT therefore announces a list with zero items. The corpus missed the aggravating limb: PaletteCardGrid.vue:21-31 injects `EmptyState`, whose empty branch is a `role="status"` div (EmptyState.vue:28), as a SECOND non-listitem direct child — a live region parented to a list. And the e2e that touches this (e2e/smoke/walk.spec.ts:72 `main.getByRole("list").last()`) asserts the container exists, never that it owns items, so the broken structure is actively certified green.

confirmed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:15 — "Loading, transport failure, filtered-zero, permission-denied, and first-run empty require distinct copy and actions; the grid exposes only one `empty` bit."
confirmed.proof: TRUE, and I promote it from prescriptive to DEMONSTRATED — the one-bit contract is already producing false copy in shipped bytes. PalettesPane.vue:77 binds `:empty="pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0"`; `filteredSaved` is the SEARCH-filtered projection (demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:112 → useFilteredList.ts:8-12, `if (!q) return items.value; return items.value.filter(...)`). The copy bound alongside it is unconditional first-run copy: PalettesPane.vue:79-80 `"No saved palettes yet."` / `"Add colors above, then save the set."`. A user holding 12 saved palettes who types a non-matching query is told they have none and instructed to create some. Identical failure on the wall: BrowsePane.vue:83 `:empty="displayedBrowse.length === 0"` where `displayedBrowse` (BrowsePane.vue:339-349) is `pm.filteredBrowse` narrowed further by an oklab color-search radius, against BrowsePane.vue:85-86 `"No published palettes here yet."` / `"Publish one from My Palettes and start the wall."` — the commons is declared empty when it is merely filtered. Refinement the axis got wrong: the prop surface is adequate (a caller CAN pass filter-aware copy); the defect is that the single bit is wired to a filtered count at 2 of 2 call sites while the copy stays unfiltered.

confirmed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:13 — "relies on a single-element root for an external `$el` consumer, but no automated guard prevents a future fragment root regression."
confirmed.proof: TRUE, and sharper than filed: the repo believes it HAS the guard and the guard cannot fail for the reason it names. e2e/smoke/walk.spec.ts:71-72 reads `// PaletteCardGrid is role="list" — the B.W1 single-root invariant.` then `await expect(main.getByRole("list").last()).toBeVisible();`. A leading comment node in the template would make the SFC a Fragment root (Vue sets the component vnode's `el` to the fragment's anchor text node) while the `role="list"` div still renders and still matches that locator — the assertion passes through the regression untouched. The thing that actually breaks is PalettesPane.vue:181 `(sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el`, feeding `useSortable` at :183; `grep -rn "reorder|drag-handle|dragTo" e2e/` returns zero hits, so drag-to-reorder has no e2e coverage at all. False comfort, not absence.

confirmed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:13, surviving limb only — "the structural requirement is … rather than a typed adapter."
confirmed.proof: The typed-adapter limb is TRUE (the 'no relation / folklore' limb is refuted — see killed L-5a). The seam is a double-unsound cast at PalettesPane.vue:181: `const sortableEl = computed(() => (sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el as HTMLElement | undefined);` — `as any` erases the component instance type and the second assertion asserts an HTMLElement that the type system never checked. PaletteCardGrid.vue:38-44 exposes no `defineExpose`, so there is no typed handle to reach for; the cast is the only available route. Real, but MINOR: one call site, one line, and the constraint it depends on is documented in the callee (PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11).

confirmed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:12 / challenge-L-library.md:10, surviving core only — `gridClass?: string` is an untyped styling escape hatch on a shared collection primitive.
confirmed.proof: The overclaims are killed (see killed C-4a); the core survives with ONE concrete live instance that proves it, which neither axis found. BrowsePane.vue:87-90 uses `gridClass` not for layout at all but to smuggle a STATE indicator through a styling channel: `'transition-opacity duration-fast ' + (pm.sortLoading.value ? 'opacity-50' : '')`. That is a busy state the grid's own contract cannot express, so it arrives as a class string — exactly the failure mode L-10 names, but the evidence is a state leak, not a 'column grammar' conflict. Consequences at PaletteCardGrid.vue:5 (`:class="gridClass"`): see missed finding on aria-busy/contrast.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:9 and challenge-D-design.md:11 — "`empty` can contradict the default slot … A caller can render cards and the empty plate simultaneously, or neither."
killed.refutation: REFUTED on the live tree AND the prescribed cure is circular. (a) Exclusivity holds by construction at 100% of call sites: PalettesPane.vue:77 binds `empty` to `pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0` and PalettesPane.vue:83 v-fors over `pm.filteredSaved.value` — the same expression; BrowsePane.vue:83 binds to `displayedBrowse.length === 0` and BrowsePane.vue:93 v-fors over `displayedBrowse`. There are exactly two consumers (grep for `PaletteCardGrid` across demo/ returns only these two plus barrel exports demo/palettes/browser/index.ts:20 and card/index.ts:5). Contradiction is unreachable. (b) C-9's cure — 'an item count or state union to enforce exclusivity' — cannot be built from slot introspection: `$slots.default()` returns Fragment vnodes from `v-for` plus dev-mode comment placeholders, so a rendered-item count is not reliably derivable; the component would have to be handed the count by the parent, i.e. the existing `empty` prop renamed. The finding demands the thing it already has. INFO at most, and both axes filed it as the lead item under a SOURCE-RED verdict.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:10 and challenge-L-library.md:12 — "`v-if="$slots.emptyAction"` checks only whether a slot function exists, not whether it produces an actionable node" / "couples rendering to Vue slot presence rather than a typed action model."
killed.refutation: REFUTED as immaterial in both directions. EmptyState.vue:64 renders `<slot name="action" />` with NO fallback content, so a provided-but-empty slot and an absent slot produce byte-identical output — no node, and no stray `gap-2.5` because flex gap does not apply to a nonexistent child. The guard at PaletteCardGrid.vue:28 has zero observable consequence whether it fires or not; it is redundant, not defective. And the coupling the axes theorize about is unexercised: `grep -rn "emptyAction|empty-action" demo/` returns exactly two hits, both the declaration itself (PaletteCardGrid.vue:28 and :29). No consumer passes the slot. The axes wrote two findings about the semantics of dead code without noticing it was dead — the actual defect here is the dead API, which I file separately.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:11 and challenge-D-design.md:12 — "Optional text props are passed through unchanged, so an empty plate can be semantically empty" / "can therefore render blank annotation fields and lose the careful invitation hierarchy."
killed.refutation:
REFUTED for two of the three annotation fields; the third is INFO-grade. `eyebrow` CANNOT go blank — EmptyState.vue:90 `withDefaults(..., { variant: "empty", eyebrow: "· empty plate ·", dots: true })`, and Vue applies a withDefaults default whenever the incoming value is `undefined`, which is precisely what `:eyebrow="emptyEyebrow"` (PaletteCardGrid.vue:25) passes when the prop is omitted. `hint` CANNOT render a blank node — EmptyState.vue:61 gates it `v-if="hint"`. Only `message` can render an empty `

` (EmptyState.vue:58-60), and it is the sole field with no default. Meanwhile 'the careful invitation hierarchy' is intact and certified: both consumers pass all three strings explicitly (PalettesPane.vue:78-80, BrowsePane.vue:84-86) and e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:195-199 and :203+ assert the literal eyebrow and message text on both surfaces. 'Blank annotation fields' (plural) describes a state the producer already made unreachable.

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:12 — "Arbitrary `gridClass` can override columns, display, containment, or visibility and makes layout testing unbounded."
killed.refutation: REFUTED on three of the four named powers and on 'unbounded'. (a) CONTAINMENT is not overridable: `contain: content` is declared in `<style scoped>` at PaletteCardGrid.vue:50-52, which compiles to `.palette-card-grid[data-v-hash]` (0,2,0) — a bare utility class in `gridClass` (0,1,0) cannot outrank it, and Tailwind ships no `contain-*` utility in the consumed set anyway. (b) The COLUMNS limb rests on a false cascade model: `grid-cols-1` (PaletteCardGrid.vue:4) and any override are equal-specificity single-class utilities in the same layer, so the winner is determined by STYLESHEET order, never by position in the class attribute — the `:class="gridClass"` merge at :5 confers no precedence whatsoever. (c) 'Unbounded' has exactly one live instance to bound it: BrowsePane.vue:87-90 passes `transition-opacity duration-fast` plus a conditional `opacity-50` — zero layout, zero display, zero visibility properties. The finding's true residue is a one-line typing concern, which I carry as C-4b at MINOR, not the four-power hazard filed here.

killed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:13 — "The component has no relation to the sortable/reorder library despite comments about `$el` and `useSortable`; the structural requirement is folklore."
killed.refutation: REFUTED — the charge inverts the truth. The relation is real, live, and load-bearing: PalettesPane.vue:76 puts `ref="sortableGridRef"` on this exact component, :180 types the ref `ref<InstanceType<typeof PaletteCardGrid> | null>(null)`, :181 reads its `$el`, and :183 feeds that element to `useSortable` (imported :133) as the drag container for `pm.filteredSaved.value`. Nothing about that is 'no relation'. Nor is it folklore: PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11 states the mechanism precisely and correctly — that a leading comment node would make the SFC multi-root and resolve `$el` to the comment rather than the div. That is an accurate statement of Vue's fragment-root `el` behavior, written at the site that must not regress. An axis calling a correct, mechanism-naming source comment 'folklore' has mistaken documentation for superstition. Only the untyped-adapter limb survives (carried as L-5b).

killed.claim: challenge-L-library.md:9 — "`EmptyState` is a demo-local primitive reached by a deep relative path."
killed.refutation: REFUTED — the deep relative path is the RATIFIED house convention, not a smell. vite.config.ts:68-70 states it in the config itself: `// W43 (RF-15) killed the demo "@…" path aliases: every demo import is now relative to its physical home (color-session/palettes/platform/shell/shared/scenes + the feature trees).` The alias array (vite.config.ts:67-73) retains only `@src` (explicitly scoped to `assets/docs/*.md` reference pages) plus the value.js self-alias set — there is no demo alias to use. And the practice is uniform: all eight EmptyState consumers import relatively at their own depth (`../../../shared/ui/EmptyState.vue` at PaletteCardGrid.vue:36 and at AdminUsersPanel.vue:202, AdminAuditPanel.vue:100, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:142, AdminTagsPanel.vue:118, AdminNamesPanel.vue:129; `../shared/...` at BrowsePane.vue:189; `../../shared/...` at MixSourceSelector.vue:9). Criticizing the depth is criticizing commit a61094e3 `feat(v-w43b3)!: home the feature UI trees; demo/@ dies` — a landed architectural decision the axis never checked for. (The clause's second half — no shared collection-state primitive — is real but is the same substance as D-5, already confirmed.)

killed.claim: challenge-C-implementation.md:14 and challenge-D-design.md:16 — "`contain: content` is unconditional; no escape exists for descendants that require overflow or layout participation" / "visual consequences for overflow, sticky descendants, and positioned affordances."
killed.refutation: REFUTED AS WRITTEN — every victim the axes name is empty, and both missed the one real casualty. Positioned affordances already escape containment by portal: SwatchHoverMenu.vue:37 wraps the hover panel in `<Teleport to="body">`, and the touch path uses reka `PopoverContent` (SwatchHoverMenu.vue:22), which portals as well. `grep -rn 'position: fixed|fixed inset' demo/palettes/browser/card/` returns ZERO — there is no fixed-position descendant for `contain: layout` to re-parent. There are no sticky descendants anywhere in the card subtree. And 'no escape exists' is not a defect statement about this tree: nothing in it needs one. Both axes hedged with a generic list of containment hazards and verified none of them; the actual, provable casualty is the producer's cartoon shadow, which neither named — filed as a missed MAJOR.

killed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:13 — "`grid-cols-1` is the only built-in layout; every responsive decision arrives through `gridClass`. The component cannot guarantee card width, reading order, or breakpoint behavior."
killed.refutation: REFUTED on its own premise. NO responsive decision arrives through `gridClass` — the single consumer that passes it (BrowsePane.vue:87-90) passes `transition-opacity duration-fast` and a conditional `opacity-50`, containing no breakpoint variant and no column class; PalettesPane.vue:75-81 passes no `gridClass` at all. The live grid is single-column at every viewport, unconditionally, which means card width, reading order, and breakpoint behavior are in fact fully determined and fully guaranteed — the opposite of the claim. The component is a single-column stack inside a width-constrained pane Card (PalettesPane.vue:2, BrowsePane.vue:2, both `w-full mx-auto` under the pane container), and that is a coherent design. Whether a wide-viewport multi-column policy would be BETTER is a legitimate open design question, but it is INFO, and it is not what the finding asserts.

missed.claim: `contain: content` on the grid clips the producer's signature cartoon shadow off the left edge of EVERY palette card and off the bottom of the last one — the exact 'visual consequence' both C-6 and D-6 gestured at and neither located.
missed.proof: `contain: content` (PaletteCardGrid.vue:51) is shorthand for `layout paint style`; paint containment clips ALL descendant painting — box-shadow included — to the containing element's padding box. The grid declares no padding and no radius (PaletteCardGrid.vue:4 `grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 min-h-[120px]`), so the clip is the content box, and with `grid-cols-1` each card's left edge is coincident with it. The producer's cartoon stamp paints entirely OUTSIDE that edge: `--shadow-cartoon-md: -3px 3px 0 var(--cartoon-ink-lead), -5px 5px 0 var(--cartoon-ink-mid), -7px 7px 0 var(--cartoon-ink-contact)` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/shadow.css) — all three layers offset NEGATIVE-x. PaletteCard.vue:19 applies `cartoon-surface`, whose rule is `@utility cartoon-surface { position: relative; border-width: 2px; box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md); }` (glass-ui/dist/components/card/styles.css), and PaletteCard.vue:28 adds the lagging `<span class="cartoon-cast">`, whose shipped rule is `position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: -1; box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md); translate: calc(-1 * var(--cast-travel) + …) calc(var(--cast-travel) + …)` with `--cast-travel: calc(6px * var(--motion-weight) * var(--cartoon-press-t))` — i.e. up to ~13px of leftward paint on press. All of it lands beyond the clip. The pane has `px-4 sm:px-6` (PalettesPane.vue:27, BrowsePane.vue:4) so the room to paint into physically exists; the grid's own containment is what removes it. PaletteCard.vue:8-16 spends nine comment lines ratifying this cartoon register as the producer's design intent — the containment silently deletes half of it. Corroborating asymmetry: BrowsePane's loading skeletons carry `shadow-cartoon-sm` (PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:34) inside an UNCONTAINED `div class="grid grid-cols-1 gap-3"` (BrowsePane.vue:46), so the shadow grammar visibly differs between the two halves of a transition the file itself designs as 'ONE surface, NEW content' (BrowsePane.vue:31-40). (Deduced from CSS containment semantics + shipped token values + live class lists; a screenshot would be confirmatory only.)

missed.claim: The Browse wall dims to 50% opacity during sort-loading with no `aria-busy`, no announcement, and a text-contrast collapse — a busy state rendered as a purely visual, AT-invisible, WCAG-failing dim.
missed.proof: BrowsePane.vue:87-90 pushes `(pm.sortLoading.value ? 'opacity-50' : '')` into `gridClass`, which lands on the grid root at PaletteCardGrid.vue:5. Opacity on the ancestor composites every descendant — every palette name (PaletteCard.vue:53-56, `font-display font-medium text-subheading`), every metadata string, every swatch — to half alpha against the pane plate. Body text already certified at the small-text 4.5:1 floor (see the P4-R2 remediation reasoning at EmptyState.vue:49-54 and the `--ink-muted` rung at :102-104) drops to roughly half its contrast ratio for the duration of the sort. Simultaneously the state is completely absent from the accessibility tree: `grep -rn "aria-busy" demo/` returns ZERO hits repo-wide, PaletteCardGrid.vue declares no `aria-busy` binding and no live region, and the grid's `role="list"` (:3) has no `aria-live`. A screen-reader user gets no signal that a sort is in flight and no signal when it lands; a low-vision sighted user gets unreadable text with no explanation. Note this is NOT a PRM issue and carries no motion-quarantine conflict — PaletteCardGrid is listed in motion-quarantine.md §7.4 'No motion content' (row `| PaletteCardGrid | C · D · L |`), and the `transition-opacity duration-fast` leg is fine (opacity is non-vestibular; guard 1 at demo/styles/animations.css:184-193 clamps it under `reduce` regardless). The defect is the un-announced, un-labelled dimmed state itself.

missed.claim: The `role="list"` has no accessible name, and the app routinely paints two of these unnamed lists on screen at once.
missed.proof: PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 declares `role="list"` with no `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, and the component exposes no prop to supply one (PaletteCardGrid.vue:38-44). Neither consumer supplies one either (PalettesPane.vue:75-81, BrowsePane.vue:80-91). The panes are designed as side-by-side twins — the source says so explicitly at PalettesPane.vue:28-30 and BrowsePane.vue:5-6 ('the twin placeholder … in BOTH side-by-side panes') — so a screen-reader user navigating by landmark or by list encounters two identically-anonymous lists and must infer ownership from surrounding heading context. The heading text needed to name them already exists and is already reachable (PaletteHeader renders 'My Palettes' / 'Browse'), which is what makes the omission cheap to have avoided. e2e/smoke/walk.spec.ts:72 disambiguates with `.last()` — the test harness itself had to work around the ambiguity.

missed.claim: The entire `emptyAction` CTA slot is dead API — declared, guarded, and commented as a surviving design decision, but wired to nothing.
missed.proof: PaletteCardGrid.vue:28-30 declares the conditional pass-through `<template v-if="$slots.emptyAction" #action><slot name="emptyAction" /></template>`, and the ratification comment at PaletteCardGrid.vue:19 asserts 'The CTA slot survives on the caption' as an owner-ruled outcome. `grep -rn "emptyAction|empty-action" demo/` returns exactly those two declaration lines and nothing else — zero consumers pass it (PalettesPane.vue:75-81 and BrowsePane.vue:80-91 pass only the three copy props). So the one affordance that would let a true-empty plate offer a way OUT of emptiness is plumbed and never used: both empty plates end in prose instructions ('Add colors above, then save the set.', 'Publish one from My Palettes and start the wall.') where a button was available and free. All three axes discussed this slot's typing and semantics (C:10, L:12) without noticing nothing calls it.

missed.claim: `min-h-[120px]` is a bespoke arbitrary-value magic number that can never bind — dead layout code carrying no token.
missed.proof: PaletteCardGrid.vue:4 hardcodes `min-h-[120px]`, the file's only arbitrary-value utility and the only raw pixel quantity in the component. It cannot take effect in either branch. Empty branch: EmptyState's empty variant (EmptyState.vue:28) is `py-8` (64px) + `gap-2.5` across four children + a `w-11` (44px) dot in the trio (:46) + eyebrow, display line, and hint — well past 120px before content. Populated branch: a single PaletteCard is a full-bleed color strip plus a `px-3 py-2.5` metadata row plus swatches, also past 120px. The only state where a 120px floor would do work — `empty` false with zero children — is unreachable at both call sites (see killed C-1). It is a floor placed under a surface that never falls, expressed as a magic number in a file whose design system otherwise runs on tokens (`gap-3`, `--duration-fast`, `--ink-muted`), in a repo that codifies exactly this discipline for the adjacent case at demo/DESIGN.md:382 ('No numeric `z-[NN]` literals … route through `--z-*` tokens').

missed.claim: Comment mass outruns code and much of it is unreadable outside the tranche ledger — 19 of 53 lines are prose, and one 8-line block is nearly pure citation.
missed.proof: PaletteCardGrid.vue is 53 lines: 12 of template markup, 10 of script, and 19 of comment (:7-11, :13-20, :48-49). The block at PaletteCardGrid.vue:13-20 opens `T.W6.5 · Lane S (R12 — the owner overrule of the D9 as-filler deployment; MANDATE §0.6 t33-audit-07/08/12)` and continues through 'its default register, N-3 re-aimed' and 'The ShadowPalette species survives at its ONE standing-instrument seat (Extract's k-threaded undeveloped plate)' — six proper-noun citations to documents outside the repo tree, guarding a five-line `<EmptyState>` element. A maintainer without the tranche ledger cannot evaluate whether a change violates it, which inverts the purpose of an in-source guard comment. The contrast with the same file's :7-11 (see superlatives) is instructive: that block names a MECHANISM and is self-sufficient; this one names a PROVENANCE and is not. Flagging as prose quality, not as a request to strip history — the fix is one sentence of mechanism ahead of the citations.

missed.claim: Skeleton and content are painted under different containment regimes, so BrowsePane's deliberately-designed morph lands on a surface whose shadow grammar changes mid-transition.
missed.proof: BrowsePane.vue:31-40 states the design intent at length: 'skeleton→content is "ONE surface, NEW content" … the developing plates SETTLE into the wall on the snappy spring instead of a hard v-if POP'. But the two keys of that `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">` (:41) render into structurally different boxes: `key="developing"` is a plain `div class="grid grid-cols-1 gap-3"` (BrowsePane.vue:45-47) with NO containment, while `key="wall"` is PaletteCardGrid, which carries `contain: content` (PaletteCardGrid.vue:51). Both children carry the same cartoon shadow family — PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:34 `shadow-cartoon-sm`, PaletteCard.vue:19 `cartoon-surface` → `--shadow-cartoon-md` — so the skeleton's stamp paints out past the container's left edge and the real card's does not (see the MAJOR containment finding). The morph therefore hands off between two subtly different silhouettes at exactly the moment the design is trying to sell continuity. Cheap to fix in either direction (add `.palette-card-grid` to the skeleton container, or drop the containment); worth naming because the intent is documented and the execution diverges from it.

superlatives: PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11 is the best in-source guard comment I have read in this tree, and it is the one thing all three axes misread. It states a non-obvious Vue mechanism exactly — that a leading comment node makes the SFC multi-root and therefore resolves `$el` to the comment rather than the div — names the downstream victim by file and feature ('PalettesPane reads `$el` for useSortable'), and is physically placed as the div's FIRST CHILD so that the comment's own existence cannot cause the failure it warns about. That last move is the craft: the documentation is written in a position that is itself proof the author understood the constraint. Verified correct against Vue's fragment-root `el` semantics and against the live consumer at PalettesPane.vue:180-183. challenge-L-library.md:13 called this 'folklore'.

The empty-state architecture is genuinely excellent and correctly resisted a bad instinct. EmptyState.vue:2-13 separates two species that most codebases conflate — `empty` (invitation) and `error` (statement) — and enforces the separation structurally with two sibling branches (:14 and :28) rather than a class toggle, giving each its own role (`role="alert"` vs `role="status"`), its own typographic register, and its own rule about annotations ('error surfaces DROP the annotations; no eyebrow, no ghosts, never a second invitation'). BrowsePane.vue:50-77 then honors it by routing transport failure to `variant="error"` with a real Retry Button instead of reusing the empty plate. And the whole thing is certified by dedicated e2e oracles: e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:187-201 asserts the literal eyebrow, the literal message, the ghost trio, AND `assertNoFillers` — a test that the empty state is empty. challenge-D-design.md:7 concedes 'directionally strong' and then files two findings against it that the live bytes refute.

The withDefaults contract at EmptyState.vue:90 is quietly load-bearing and shows real API judgment. `{ variant: "empty", eyebrow: "· empty plate ·", dots: true }` makes the safe state the default state: a caller who passes nothing still gets a coherent plate with a labelled eyebrow and the ghost trio, because the two fields whose absence would look like a rendering bug are defaulted while the one field that must be situation-specific (`message`) deliberately is not. Paired with the `v-if="hint"` gate at :61, this makes 'blank annotation fields' unreachable — which is why I could kill C-3 and D-2 outright.

The `.cartoon-cast` press choreography (PaletteCard.vue:28-29 + the glass-ui rule) is a rare case of PRM handled at the TOKEN layer rather than by a media-query afterthought: the travel and spread are both scaled by `--motion-weight`, and the reduced-motion arm ships `.cartoon-cast { --motion-weight: 0; transition: none; }`, so the entire spatial grammar collapses to zero through the same variable that produces it. No duplicated keyframes, no `@media` block in the component, no chance of the two arms drifting. This is the architecture that motion-quarantine.md's M-03/M-07/M-29 rows repeatedly defend against the corpus's 'no reduced-motion rule in this file' complaints — and it is visible here in a component the corpus classified as having no motion content at all.
unproven: Whether the cartoon-shadow clipping (missed MAJOR) is perceptually obvious or merely measurable at shipped token values. The clip is certain from CSS containment semantics and the negative-x offsets in `--shadow-cartoon-md`; what a viewer actually notices — and whether the `--cartoon-ink-*` layers read as a lost edge or as an intentional flush-left card — is a rendered judgment. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE. Probe would be a single screenshot of My Palettes with and without the `contain` declaration; no dev server was started per probe parsimony.

The exact contrast ratios reached under `opacity-50` during Browse sort-loading. The compositing is certain and the direction is certain (roughly halved effective contrast against the resting plate); the resulting numeric ratios against the light and dark `--ink-muted` rungs require live computed-style sampling. The a11y defect does not depend on the number — the missing `aria-busy` and the absent announcement are proven statically — but the WCAG pass/fail call does. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

Whether any assistive technology currently in use degrades the `role="list"` to a generic group versus announcing 'list, 0 items'. The ARIA violation is proven from the spec plus PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 and PaletteCard.vue:22; the announced string varies by AT and browser. The defect stands either way — no AT announces the correct item count — but the precise user-facing symptom is not decidable from source.

Whether the single-column policy is right at wide viewports. I refuted challenge-D-design.md:13's factual premise (no responsive decision arrives through `gridClass`; the grid is unconditionally one column), but whether a two- or three-column wall would serve Browse better depends on the pane's rendered width inside the dock shell across the `--content-max-h` breakpoints at demo/styles/foundation.css:470-483. That is a live-layout question, and it is a design ASK rather than a defect either way.

confirmed.claim: `Button` arrives via a forwarding barrel; `variant="outline"` is not the installed glass-ui Button API and becomes dead intent. (challenge-L-library.md:9)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED against live bytes. Barrel: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/ui/button/index.ts:1 is exactly `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`. Installed producer is @mkbabb/glass-ui 7.0.0 (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json). Its ButtonProps (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-19) declares emphasis/tone/size/iconOnly/loading/type/disabled/class — there is NO `variant` key. The stylesheet confirms the consequence: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/styles.css keys only off `[data-emphasis=...]`, `[data-tone=...]`, `[data-size=...]`, `[data-icon-only]` — no `outline` treatment exists anywhere in the file. So `variant="outline"` at demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:8 and :22 falls through to a literal invalid DOM attribute and paints nothing; the buttons render at default emphasis/tone.

confirmed.claim: Icon-only buttons are named, but intended `variant="outline"` is not the current producer vocabulary; the visual hierarchy may not match the source. (challenge-D-design.md:15)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED — same underlying fact as L-1, independently reached, and D's first limb also verified: both buttons ARE correctly named (PaginationBar.vue:11 `aria-label="Previous page"`, :25 `aria-label="Next page"`, with :14/:28 icons `aria-hidden="true"`). The second limb holds: `variant` is absent from ButtonProps (Button.vue.d.ts:6-19), so the intended outline hierarchy is not applied. D-5's hedge ("may not match") is weaker than the evidence warrants — it definitively does not match.

confirmed.claim: No pending guard prevents double activation. (challenge-C-implementation.md:12)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, and provably a double standard inside this same repo. demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:105-110 `nextPage()` guards ONLY on `hasNext.value`, which is computed from `page < pageCount` (:56) and is stale for the whole request flight; it does `page.value++` then `loadFlagged()` with no in-flight flag and no request identity. Identical at demo/palettes/useAdminAudit.ts:73-78. Three rapid Next clicks therefore fire three concurrent `getFlaggedPalettes` calls at offsets 20/40/60; whichever resolves LAST wins `items.value = res.data` (useAdminFlagged.ts:69-70), so the rendered list can belong to a different page than `page.value`. CONTRAST — the same codebase solves this correctly on the public wall: demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:98 short-circuits on `|| loadingMore.value`, and :99/:104 carry a generation token (`const gen = loadGeneration; ... if (gen !== loadGeneration) return; // a fresh load superseded us`). The cure is already written 40 lines away. Additionally the producer ships the UI half: ButtonProps.loading (Button.vue.d.ts:14-15, "Marks an in-flight command and suppresses activation until it settles") is unused, and `loading: Ref<boolean>` already exists and is exported by both composables (useAdminFlagged.ts:52,138; useAdminAudit.ts:39,92) but is never passed to PaginationBar.

confirmed.claim: `aria-live` announces page-text mutations, which are not explicitly bound to completion of the corresponding list request. (challenge-C-implementation.md:13)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, and far stronger than the hedge "not explicitly bound" — the announcement is GUARANTEED to precede content by one full network round trip. Ordering, from live bytes: useAdminFlagged.ts:107 `page.value++` is synchronous; PaginationBar.vue:17-19 (`aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` on `Page {{ page }} of {{ pageCount }}`) re-renders and announces on the very next tick; only then does :108 `loadFlagged()` await, with rows committed at :69-70 `items.value = res.data`. Identical at useAdminAudit.ts:75-76 → :60-62. A screen-reader user hears "Page 3 of 5" while the DOM still holds page 2's rows.

confirmed.claim: The live page sentence is useful, yet rapid updates could announce intermediate states before content is ready. (challenge-D-design.md:14)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED — same defect as C-5, independently reached on the design axis; D's "could" understates it (it always does, per the synchronous-increment-then-await ordering at useAdminFlagged.ts:107→108→69). D-4's compounding limb is also real: because there is no in-flight guard (C-4), N rapid clicks produce N announcements of intermediate page numbers, each of which may never correspond to any committed list state. D's own prescription at challenge-D-design.md:19 ("Announce the page only when the corresponding list has committed") is the structurally correct cure and is supported by existing state — move the announcement to fire off request settlement rather than off the `page` ref.

confirmed.claim: Page changes have no busy register. Users can repeatedly activate arrows while results are loading and receive no relation between displayed page text and displayed rows. (challenge-D-design.md:12)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED on both limbs, and the second limb is literally true rather than rhetorical. Limb 1 (no busy register): PaginationBar.vue:37-42 `defineProps` accepts only page/pageCount/hasNext/hasPrev — no loading/busy prop exists, and the producer's `loading` affordance (Button.vue.d.ts:14-15) is unused at :7-15 and :21-29. Limb 2 (no relation between page text and rows): proven by the render chain — in BOTH consumers the list `v-for` is NOT part of the loading `v-if`/`v-else-if` chain (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16 `v-if="flagged.loading.value"` → :23 `v-else-if` error → :38 `v-else-if` empty, then :45 `<div v-for="item in flagged.items.value">` standing alone; same shape at AdminAuditPanel.vue:36/42/56 → :59-60). During flight the bar shows the NEW page number while the rows underneath are still the OLD page's.

confirmed.claim: `pageCount > 1` is the sole guard; `page=0`, `page>pageCount`, non-integer, or negative values are rendered verbatim. (challenge-C-implementation.md:9)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED ONLY ON THE `page > pageCount` LIMB — the other three limbs are refuted as unreachable, so this row must be adopted in scoped form. Refuted: `pageCount` can never be 0/negative/non-integer because both composables clamp it — `Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total.value / pageSize))` (useAdminFlagged.ts:55, useAdminAudit.ts:44); `page` starts at `ref(1)` (useAdminFlagged.ts:50, useAdminAudit.ts:37) and moves only by guarded ±1 (useAdminFlagged.ts:105-117), so 0/negative/non-integer are unreachable through both — and only — call sites. CONFIRMED limb: `page > pageCount` IS reachable via the delete path, which decrements `total` WITHOUT reloading or clamping `page` — useAdminFlagged.ts:87 and :99 both `total.value = Math.max(0, total.value - 1)`. Worked case: pageSize 20 (:51), total 41 → pageCount 3; admin on page 3 deletes one row → total 40 → pageCount 2 → PaginationBar.vue:18 renders the literal text "Page 3 of 2", with Next disabled (hasNext = 3 < 2 = false) and Previous enabled. The guard at PaginationBar.vue:3 (`pageCount > 1`) does not catch it.

confirmed.claim: There are no first/last or direct-page affordances; no threshold or large-count design exists. (challenge-D-design.md:13)
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED at low severity; the claim is self-hedged but the underlying gap is real and quantified. PaginationBar.vue:1-31 contains exactly two commands (prev at :7-15, next at :21-29) and a static counter at :17-19 — no first/last, no direct-page entry, no ellipsis window. Page size is 20 in both consumers (useAdminFlagged.ts:51, useAdminAudit.ts:38). The flagged queue is naturally small, but the audit log is an append-only ledger with unbounded growth, so reaching page 40 of 60 requires 39 sequential clicks, each a full network round trip (useAdminAudit.ts:76). D correctly declines to call this a defect for small sets; it is a genuine design gap for the audit surface specifically.

killed.claim: This generic pattern belongs either in glass-ui or in a shared application collection package, not independently in each admin panel. (challenge-L-library.md:13)
killed.refutation: REFUTED — the premise is factually false. PaginationBar is NOT reimplemented per panel; it is already a single shared component with exactly two importers: demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminAuditPanel.vue:102 `import PaginationBar from "./PaginationBar.vue"` and demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:144 (identical). `find demo/ -iname "*Pagination*"` returns exactly one file. The axis criticises a duplication that does not exist, and the residual promotion argument (extract to glass-ui) is unsupported at n=2 co-located consumers — it would violate the standing KISS/no-contrivance precept against inventing shared packages for patterns with no third consumer.

killed.claim: `hasPrev`/`hasNext` are trusted instead of derived, allowing "Page 1 of 2" with Previous enabled or Next disabled. (challenge-C-implementation.md:10)
killed.refutation: REFUTED — they ARE derived, at every call site, from the same two values that render the label. useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57: `pageCount = computed(() => Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total.value / pageSize)))`, `hasNext = computed(() => page.value < pageCount.value)`, `hasPrev = computed(() => page.value > 1)`. Byte-identical at useAdminAudit.ts:44-46. Both are passed straight through (AdminAuditPanel.vue:84-87, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:127-130). The specific failure C names is therefore unreachable: on page 1, `hasPrev` is `1 > 1` = false, so "Page 1 of 2 with Previous enabled" cannot render. There is no third consumer to supply free scalars. This is a latent prop-contract observation, not a defect.

killed.claim: `page`, `pageCount`, `hasNext`, `hasPrev` can contradict each other. A library boundary should accept one normalized pagination state. (challenge-L-library.md:10)
killed.refutation: REFUTED as a defect, on the same evidence as C-2: all four props are computed off one source of truth in both and only consumers (useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57, useAdminAudit.ts:44-46), so no contradictory combination is reachable in the live tree. The residual boundary-hygiene point is legitimate but is INFO, not SOURCE-RED. Note further that L's prescribed cure at challenge-L-library.md:15 (`PaginationState = unknown | ready({page,count}) | loading({from,to}) | error(...)`) is disproportionate: the one genuinely missing input is a boolean busy flag, and both composables ALREADY export `loading: Ref<boolean>` (useAdminFlagged.ts:138, useAdminAudit.ts:92) while the producer Button already accepts `loading` (Button.vue.d.ts:14-15). A four-case ADT is contrivance where one prop closes the gap.

killed.claim: Events do not include the destination, so parent and child can race against changing props. (challenge-C-implementation.md:11)
killed.refutation: REFUTED — the named mechanism cannot occur, because the child holds no state to race with. PaginationBar.vue:44-47 declares `defineEmits<{ prev: []; next: [] }>()` and the component has no `ref`, no local page copy, and no writes — it is a pure function of its props. The parent owns `page` outright and mutates it against its OWN guard (useAdminFlagged.ts:105-110: `if (hasNext.value) { page.value++ }`), never against a value echoed back from the child. A stale emit is therefore idempotent-safe. A bare intent event is the correct minimal contract here. The real race is parent-internal (unsequenced concurrent fetches) and is already carried, correctly, by C-4 — C-3 misattributes it to the event payload.

killed.claim: Events `prev`/`next` carry no target page, query generation, or request identity. (challenge-L-library.md:11)
killed.refutation: REFUTED as a defect (the bare fact is true — PaginationBar.vue:44-47). Same reasoning as C-3: the destination is not the child's to know, since the parent is the sole owner of `page`. More importantly the prescription is misplaced — "query generation" and "request identity" are properties of the FETCH layer, not of a UI intent event. The repo's own correct implementation proves this: the generation token in demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:99,104 lives in the composable, not in any emitted event payload. Putting request identity in a `prev`/`next` emit would push data-layer concerns into a presentational component — the opposite of the library-boundary discipline this axis is arguing for.

killed.claim: The live-region sentence is locally authored; other paginated surfaces can announce at a different phase. (challenge-L-library.md:12)
killed.refutation: REFUTED — the comparison class is empty. `grep -rn aria-live demo/ --include="*.vue"` returns four hits total: ComponentSliders.vue:84 (`aria-live="off"`), ErrorBoundary.vue:20 (`assertive`, an error alert), and PaginationBar.vue:17. There is no second page-announcing live region to diverge from. The only other paginated surface uses a categorically different paradigm — demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:17,33-34,97 is keyset/cursor "load more" that APPENDS (`remotePalettes.value = [...remotePalettes.value, ...page]`, :106), which correctly has no page-number announcement at all. The inconsistency is hypothetical about surfaces that do not exist.

killed.claim: The bar disappears whenever `pageCount <= 1`; that conflates a verified single page with unknown count, loading, error, and invalid negative/zero totals. (challenge-D-design.md:11)
killed.refutation: REFUTED as stated, on two independent grounds. (1) The "invalid negative/zero totals" limb is unreachable: `Math.max(1, Math.ceil(...))` clamps pageCount to ≥1 at useAdminFlagged.ts:55 and useAdminAudit.ts:44, so `pageCount` is never negative or zero and the conflation D fears cannot arise. (2) The loading/error limb causes no user-visible harm, because both panels already discriminate those states ABOVE the bar in a dedicated chain: AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16 skeleton, :23 EmptyState `variant="error"` ("The flag queue is unreachable"), :38 EmptyState empty; same at AdminAuditPanel.vue:36/42/56. Hiding pagination for a single page is conventional and correct. NOTE: D-1 is pointed at the right LINE (PaginationBar.vue:3) for the wrong REASON — that `v-if` does host a genuine reachable trap, but via the deletion-collapse path D never identified; it is filed in `missed` as PB-M1 and should be adopted from there, not from this row.

missed.claim: PB-M1 — DELETION-COLLAPSE STRANDS THE ADMIN WITH NO RECOVERY. When deleting the last row of the last page drops `pageCount` to 1, `v-if="pageCount > 1"` unmounts the whole bar while `page` remains >1, leaving a self-contradicting panel and no affordance to navigate back. All three axes missed it.
missed.proof: Reachable, worked from live bytes. pageSize 20 (useAdminFlagged.ts:51); total 21 → pageCount = Math.max(1, ceil(21/20)) = 2 (:55). Admin is on page 2 (one row). Deleting it runs useAdminFlagged.ts:98-99: `items.value = items.value.filter(...)` → [] and `total.value = Math.max(0, total.value - 1)` → 20, with NO reload and NO clamp of `page`. pageCount recomputes to ceil(20/20) = 1, so PaginationBar.vue:3 evaluates `1 > 1` = false and the entire bar UNMOUNTS. The resulting screen contradicts itself: the toolbar reads "20 flagged" (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:6-8, bound to `flagged.total.value`) while the body renders EmptyState "No flagged palettes." (:38-42), with no pagination control left. RECOVERY FAILS: the Refresh button (:11) calls `flagged.loadFlagged`, which fetches at `offset = (page.value - 1) * pageSize` = 20 (:67) — past the end of a 20-item set — returning empty again. And the state is app-lifetime, not pane-lifetime: `useAdminFlagged()` is constructed ONCE at the composition root (demo/palettes/usePalettePorts.ts:73) and provided via ADMIN_PORT_KEY (:245), so `page` survives pane switches and the panel's `onMounted(() => flagged.loadFlagged())` (AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:152) re-fetches the same dead offset. Only a full document reload clears it. Identical shape via the Dismiss path at useAdminFlagged.ts:86-87. Cure is one line in the composable — clamp `page` to `pageCount` after any total mutation, then reload.

missed.claim: PB-M2 — LOADING SKELETONS RENDER ON TOP OF STALE ROWS RATHER THAN REPLACING THEM, because the list `v-for` is not part of the loading `v-if`/`v-else-if` chain in either consumer. This is the concrete mechanism behind D-2's "no relation between page text and rows", and no axis located it.
missed.proof: Structural, both consumers. AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:16 opens `<div v-if="flagged.loading.value">` (2 AdminListSkeletons), :23 `v-else-if="flagged.loadError.value"`, :38 `v-else-if="flagged.items.value.length === 0"` — then the list at :45 is a NEW element, `<div v-for="item in flagged.items.value">`, carrying no `v-else`. The chain therefore terminates before the list, and the two render independently. Because `loadFlagged` sets `loading.value = true` (:62) but does not clear `items` before awaiting (:69 assigns only after the response), during the entire flight the panel paints 2 skeletons AND the previous page's 20 rows simultaneously, beneath a PaginationBar already showing the incremented page number (page.value++ at :107 precedes the fetch at :108). Byte-identical structure at AdminAuditPanel.vue:36 (3 skeletons) / :42 / :56 / :59-60. The skeleton grammar is deliberate and well-documented (the W5-1/F-13 comment at AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:15 reads "flagged rows load as row shadows, one grammar") — the intent is clearly substitution, and the chaining bug silently defeats it.

missed.claim: PB-M3 — KEYBOARD FOCUS IS DESTROYED AT EVERY BOUNDARY. Paging onto the last (or first) page disables the very button the user just activated, dropping focus to `<body>`. The producer ships the focus-preserving alternative and PaginationBar does not use it. Missed by all three axes.
missed.proof: PaginationBar.vue:24 binds `:disabled="!hasNext"` and :10 `:disabled="!hasPrev"` to native `disabled`. `hasNext = page < pageCount` (useAdminFlagged.ts:56), so activating Next on page 4 of 5 sets page=5 and flips hasNext false in the same tick — the focused element becomes `disabled`, and per HTML semantics a disabled control is removed from the tab order and loses focus, which user agents reset to the document body. glass-ui reinforces the removal: `.button:disabled { pointer-events: none; }` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/styles.css). A keyboard or screen-reader user paging to the end therefore loses their position entirely and must re-traverse the panel; the symmetric case occurs paging back to page 1. THE CURE IS ALREADY IN THE PRODUCER: every disabled rule in that stylesheet is written as the pair `:disabled, [aria-disabled="true"]` (visible on the `.button:disabled, .button[aria-disabled="true"]` opacity rule and on all four `:hover:not(:disabled, [aria-disabled="true"])` guards), i.e. glass-ui deliberately supports the focusable aria-disabled pattern with identical styling. Binding `:aria-disabled` instead of `:disabled` (with a no-op click guard) preserves focus and keeps the control announced.

missed.claim: PB-M4 — ICON-ONLY BUTTONS DO NOT USE THE PRODUCER'S `iconOnly` PROP, so they render as wide pills instead of squares — off-system geometry in a component whose own comment declares it icon-only. Missed by all three axes, including the library axis whose entire remit is producer-API conformance.
missed.proof: PaginationBar.vue:6 comments "W5-a11y: icon-only pagination buttons need aria-labels" and :14/:28 contain nothing but a `ChevronLeft`/`ChevronRight` glyph — these are icon-only by construction. ButtonProps declares exactly the right affordance: `iconOnly?: boolean` documented "Square geometry for an accessibly named icon command" (Button.vue.d.ts:12-13), implemented as `.button[data-icon-only] { inline-size: var(--button-size); block-size: var(--button-size); padding: 0; }`. Neither button at :7-15 or :21-29 passes it. Without it the `sm` rule applies `padding-inline: calc(0.75rem * var(--ui-scale))` around a `--ui-glyph: 1rem` icon, producing a ~40x36px lozenge rather than the 36x36 square the design system defines for this exact case. This is not an isolated slip against local convention: `iconOnly` is used 21 times elsewhere in demo/, so PaginationBar is the outlier. (Sibling icon buttons work around the same gap with bespoke `class="h-7 px-2"` overrides — AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:11, AdminAuditPanel.vue:30 — which is the same defect in a second dialect.)

missed.claim: PB-M5 — NO `<nav>` LANDMARK AND NO ACCESSIBLE GROUP NAME. The bar's root is a bare styling `<div>`, so assistive tech cannot locate or announce it as a navigation region. Missed by all three axes despite two of them auditing a11y.
missed.proof: PaginationBar.vue:2-5 opens `<div v-if="pageCount > 1" class="flex items-center justify-center gap-2 py-3">` — a presentational div with no `role`, no `aria-label`, and no semantic element. Pagination is a navigation construct and the established pattern (ARIA Authoring Practices; the same shape shipped by every mainstream design system) is `<nav aria-label="Pagination">`, which places the control in the landmark rotor and disambiguates it when more than one paginated region exists. The demo already uses landmark semantics elsewhere — demo/color-picker/App.vue:24 opens a real `<nav>` — so this is inconsistency with local practice, not an absent convention. Low cost: one element swap plus one attribute, no layout change.

missed.claim: PB-M6 — THE LIVE REGION IS CREATED TOGETHER WITH ITS OWN CONTENT ON FIRST APPEARANCE, so the first page announcement is unreliable. A live region must already be in the DOM before the mutation it reports.
missed.proof: The `aria-live="polite"` span (PaginationBar.vue:17-19) is nested INSIDE the `v-if="pageCount > 1"` root (:3), so it does not exist until pageCount first exceeds 1. Sequence: both composables initialise `total = ref(0)` (useAdminFlagged.ts:49, useAdminAudit.ts:36), so pageCount computes to `Math.max(1, 0)` = 1 and the bar is unmounted; when the first response lands (`total.value = res.total`, useAdminFlagged.ts:70) the region is INSERTED with its text already present. Screen readers generally do not announce a live region injected together with its initial content — the region must be resident and then mutated — so the first announcement is silently dropped. The mirror case also holds: when pageCount falls back to 1 the region is destroyed, discarding any pending polite announcement. Subsequent page changes while the bar stays mounted DO announce correctly, so this is narrower than C-5/D-4 but independent of them: it is a mount-lifecycle defect, not an ordering defect. Cure: hoist the live region outside the `v-if` (or keep the root mounted and hide only the buttons).

missed.claim: PB-M7 — SCOPE CORRECTION ON L-1/D-5: the dead `variant` axis is a REPO-WIDE epidemic across at least 10 files, not a PaginationBar-local staleness. Fixing only this component leaves the class of defect intact, and the axis framing actively conceals that.
missed.proof: challenge-L-library.md:9 frames the issue as "The component uses a producer button through a stale axis", implying a local regression. A sweep of `<Button>` elements receiving `variant=` shows the same dead prop across: demo/shell/dock/menus/ProfileSection.vue:60,112 (`outline`) and :136 (`ghost`); demo/color-picker/ErrorBoundary.vue:30; demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:70,137; demo/palettes/browser/card/CurrentPaletteEditor.vue:135,152,160; demo/palettes/browser/admin/AdminAuditPanel.vue:30,49; AdminTagsPanel.vue:10,38,75; AdminUsersPanel.vue:22,33,58,114; demo/scenes/ConfigSliderPane.vue:165,169; demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:158,167,177; demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue:163. The invented values span `outline`, `ghost`, and `primary-audacious` — none exist in ButtonEmphasis (`"primary" | "secondary" | "quiet" | "text"`, Button.vue.d.ts:4). Corroborating the systemic reading: the correct axis `emphasis=` appears only 2 times in all of demo/, versus 103 `variant=` occurrences. This is a producer-migration debt (glass-ui renamed variant → emphasis/tone) that the 7.0.0 adoption did not sweep, and it is invisible to CI because unknown props fall through as HTML attributes rather than failing typecheck. Recommend a single cross-cutting repair item rather than 10 per-component rows.

superlatives: PROVENANCE-CRITICAL: all three PaginationBar axes are REPORT-AUTHORED, not witnessed. HYDRATION-LEDGER.md:264-266 records challenge-C/D/L each as `REPORT-AUTHORED | closure-manifest-2026-08-03 | 0 payloads`, and the ledger legend (:5-9) is explicit — "no challenge seat ran; the file was authored by the 2026-08-03 frontend closure pass from pinned source... Source-review findings — NOT challenge coverage" and "may [not] be counted as a witnessed seat return". The entire corpus for this component is therefore unverified prose, which is consistent with what this re-read found: 7 of 15 claims died against the live tree, and the three most severe real defects (PB-M1 stranding, PB-M2 double-render, PB-M3 focus loss) appear in none of them. Weight the live source over all three files.

CORPUS RECEIPT INTEGRITY IS EXCELLENT — the one thing all three axes got unambiguously right. Each file pins `demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue, lines 1–48, SHA-256 3006c9b99288b591c70272dada3b587fb5b30a88ef8bf775b67ea8e78b73322c` (challenge-C:3, challenge-D:5, challenge-L:3). `shasum -a 256` on the live file returns that hash EXACTLY and `wc -l` returns 48. The corpus is auditing the real, current, unmodified bytes — every kill below is a reasoning error, never a stale-target error. This is the standard other components' corpora should be held to.

glass-ui's COARSE-POINTER CONTROL FLOOR is genuinely excellent producer engineering, and it refuted my own hypothesis mid-audit. I expected `size="sm"` (--control-h-sm: 2.25rem = 36px) to fail the 44px touch target. It does not: tokens/light-dark.css sets `@media (pointer: coarse) { :root { --ui-scale: var(--ui-coarse-scale, 1.5); --control-floor: var(--touch-target, 2.75rem); } }`, and sizing.css defines `--control-h-sm: max(calc(2.25rem * var(--ui-scale)), var(--control-floor))` → max(3.375rem, 2.75rem) = 54px on touch. Every control in the system meets the target automatically with zero per-component work. NO TAP-TARGET DEFECT MAY BE CARRIED against PaginationBar (or any glass-ui control) on this basis.

`tabular-nums` on the page counter (PaginationBar.vue:17) is exactly the right call and easy to miss. It resolves to a real utility (`.tabular-nums{--tw-numeric-spacing:tabular-nums;font-variant-numeric:...}`), and on a string like "Page 9 of 12" → "Page 10 of 12" it prevents the horizontal jitter that proportional digits would cause in a centre-justified flex row — the label would otherwise shove both buttons sideways on every page change. Paired with `text-caption` (a genuine design-system token, `.text-caption{font-size:var(--type-caption)}`, used by glass-ui's own chip component), the typography here is fully system-conformant. No bespoke values, no magic numbers.

The ICON/LABEL ACCESSIBILITY PAIRING is correct and deliberately marked. PaginationBar.vue:6 carries the provenance comment "W5-a11y: icon-only pagination buttons need aria-labels", and the implementation honours it exactly: `aria-label="Previous page"` (:11) and `aria-label="Next page"` (:25) on the controls, with `aria-hidden="true"` on both glyphs (:14, :28) so the icon contributes no duplicate text node. This is the textbook pattern, applied consistently, with a traceable reason for existing. (It also means D-5's first limb — "icon-only buttons are named" — is the one uncontested compliment in the corpus, and it is deserved.)

demo/palettes/useBrowsePalettes.ts:97-114 is a model implementation of exactly the concurrency discipline the admin pagination lacks, and it is the single best piece of evidence in this audit. It carries an in-flight short-circuit (`if (!hasMore.value || nextCursor.value == null || loadingMore.value) return;`, :98), a generation token captured before the await and re-checked after (`const gen = loadGeneration;` :99 → `if (gen !== loadGeneration) return; // a fresh load superseded us` :104), a guarded flag release (`if (gen === loadGeneration) loadingMore.value = false;` :112), and a doc comment that states the contract precisely (:91-96). The correct pattern already exists in this repo, authored by the same hand — which converts C-4 from a style preference into a demonstrated inconsistency with an in-tree cure.

The ERROR-≠-EMPTY DISCIPLINE in both consuming panels is first-rate and well beyond typical. AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:20-33 renders EmptyState `variant="error"` with "The flag queue is unreachable." plus the underlying detail and a Retry action, kept strictly separate from the genuine-empty state at :38-42 ("No flagged palettes."); the composable feeds it by capturing `loadError.value = e?.message ?? "Backend unreachable"` (useAdminFlagged.ts:73-74). The reasoning is recorded inline — "W5-5 (F-2, the P0 case): error ≠ empty — a dead backend never costumes as a clear moderation queue" (:21-22) and "never costume a dead backend as an empty ledger" (useAdminAudit.ts:65). For a moderation surface, mistaking an outage for a clear queue is the highest-consequence failure available, and it is explicitly designed against on both panels. This directly refutes D-1's "conflates... loading, error" limb.

MOTION GOVERNANCE IS CLEAN AND MUST NOT BE RE-LITIGATED. motion-quarantine.md:274 rules `PaginationBar | C · D · L` into §7.4 "No motion content — vacuously cleared on this axis" (:269) — all three axes. This re-read confirms the ruling holds against live bytes: PaginationBar.vue:1-48 contains no transition, animation, or motion class of any kind, and the producer handles the reduced-motion case centrally (`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .button { transition: none; } }` in the button stylesheet, atop the app-wide neutraliser at demo/styles/animations.css:184-193). No M-xx row applies to this component and no PRM defect is carried here. Correctly, none of the three axes attempted one — a restraint worth recording given that 10 other files remain quarantined for exactly that overreach (§7.3, :254-267).
unproven: UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE — the actual rendered appearance of the two buttons. The dist `.d.ts` (Button.vue.d.ts:24-31) shows a defaults block whose runtime VALUES for `emphasis` and `tone` are not recoverable from the type declaration, and `dist/` ships no readable `.vue` source. So while it is proven that `variant="outline"` applies nothing (no `outline` selector exists in the button stylesheet), whether the resulting default paint is an acceptable or a jarring hierarchy against the admin panel's surrounding surface can only be settled by rendering. D-5's hedge "the visual hierarchy may not match the source" is therefore correct to hedge on this narrow point, even though its factual premise is confirmed.

UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE — the precise screen-reader behaviour of PB-M6 (live region inserted together with its initial content). The DOM lifecycle is proven statically from the `v-if` nesting at PaginationBar.vue:3/17 plus `total = ref(0)` at useAdminFlagged.ts:49, but whether a given AT/browser pair drops that first announcement varies by implementation (NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver differ on regions added post-load). The defect is structurally real and the cure is cheap and harmless; the exact user-audible impact needs an AT probe, which probe-parsimony law excludes here.

UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE — exact ordering of the polite-queue flush relative to paint in C-5/D-4. The CODE ordering is proven beyond doubt (synchronous `page.value++` at useAdminFlagged.ts:107 strictly precedes the awaited commit at :69-70, so the announcement is enqueued a full round trip early). What cannot be settled statically is whether a slow-enough AT speech queue might coincidentally flush after the response lands on a fast local API, masking the defect in casual testing. This does not weaken the finding — it explains why the defect would survive manual QA and argues for fixing it on the structural evidence rather than waiting for a reproduction.

NOT AUDITED — narrow-viewport and localisation behaviour. challenge-D-design.md:19 demands cells for "phone/desktop" and "large numerals/localization". PaginationBar.vue:4 uses a fixed `flex items-center justify-center gap-2 py-3` with no wrap and no container query, and :18 hardcodes the English string `Page {{ page }} of {{ pageCount }}` with no i18n indirection and no pluralisation hook. Both observations are static facts, but whether they actually break (overflow at 320px; string expansion in a longer locale) requires rendering, and no i18n framework appears to be in use in demo/ at all — so the hardcoded string may be a deliberate project-wide decision rather than a component defect. Flagged for the owner, not carried as a finding.

confirmed.claim: `variant="outline"` is not the installed glass-ui Button API and becomes dead intent; the intended visual hierarchy may not match the source.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED and stronger than stated — it is not "may not match", it DOES not match. Axis: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/PaginationBar/challenge-L-library.md:9 and challenge-D-design.md:15. Live: demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:8 and :22 pass `variant="outline"`. The installed producer is glass-ui 7.0.0 (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/package.json version 7.0.0); ButtonProps at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:6-19 declares exactly {emphasis, tone, size, iconOnly, loading, type, disabled, class} — no `variant`. The runtime props table at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/button-Bu9F4uU6.js:10-33 confirms zero `variant` (grep for "variant" over that chunk returns nothing). `inheritAttrs` is never set (0 occurrences in the chunk), so `variant="outline"` falls through $attrs and is emitted as a literal, meaningless `variant="outline"` DOM attribute on the reka-ui Primitive root. The buttons therefore render at the DECLARED DEFAULTS — `emphasis: "secondary"`, `tone: "neutral"` (button-Bu9F4uU6.js:12-14) — i.e. a glass-wash capsule, not an outline. `size="sm"` IS honored (ButtonSize = xs|sm|md|lg, Button.vue.d.ts:5). WHY IT SURVIVED A HARD GATE: package.json:65 runs `vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit`, and no `vueCompilerOptions`/`strictTemplates` exists in any tsconfig (grep over tsconfig*.json = no matches), so unknown component props are not checked — the dead intent is structurally invisible to CI. BLAST RADIUS beyond this component: 49 dead `variant` values on `<Button>` across 22 demo files (28 `outline`, 19 `ghost`, 2 `primary-audacious`, 1 `destructive`, 1 `default`), e.g. AdminAuditPanel.vue:30,49 and AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:10,29,90,93. CORRECTION to the axis's framing: the forwarding barrel demo/ui/button/index.ts:1 (`export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";`) is NOT causal — `variant` would be equally dead on a direct import. The barrel only makes the shadcn-shaped prop look plausible.

confirmed.claim: `pageCount > 1` is the sole guard; `page=0`, `page>pageCount`, non-integer, or negative values are rendered verbatim.
confirmed.proof: ONE OF FOUR LIMBS CONFIRMED; the other three are unconstructible. Axis: challenge-C-implementation.md:7. Live: demo/palettes/browser/admin/PaginationBar.vue:3 (`v-if="pageCount > 1"`) and :18 (`Page {{ page }} of {{ pageCount }}`) — no clamp, correct. REACHABLE LIMB (`page > pageCount`): demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:86-87 (`dismiss`) and :98-99 (`deletePalette`) decrement `total` without touching `page`. With pageSize=20 (useAdminFlagged.ts:51) and total=41 → pageCount=3 (:55); navigate to page 3 (1 item), dismiss it → total=40 → pageCount=2, page still 3 → v-if passes (2>1) and the bar renders the false sentence "Page 3 of 2", Next disabled (hasNext = 3<2 = false, :56), Prev enabled. UNCONSTRUCTIBLE LIMBS: `page` is initialized to 1 (useAdminAudit.ts:37, useAdminFlagged.ts:50) and mutated only by `page.value++`/`page.value--` behind the `hasNext`/`hasPrev` guards (useAdminAudit.ts:73-85, useAdminFlagged.ts:105-117) plus one `page.value = 1` reset (AdminAuditPanel.vue:114) — so page=0, negative page, and non-integer page cannot occur at either (only) call site. The fault site is the composable, not the component; see missed finding on the unrecoverable variant of the same bug.

confirmed.claim: Page changes have no busy register; users can repeatedly activate arrows while results load and get no relation between the displayed page text and the displayed rows.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED, and the cure already ships in the producer, unused. Axis: challenge-D-design.md:12. Live: PaginationBar.vue:37-42 declares props {page, pageCount, hasNext, hasPrev} — no `loading`/`busy`; the two Buttons (:7-15, :21-29) are gated only by `:disabled="!hasPrev"`/`!hasNext`. Both producers expose a loading flag (useAdminAudit.ts:19,39; useAdminFlagged.ts:27,52) and NEITHER panel forwards it (AdminAuditPanel.vue:83-90, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:126-133). glass-ui's Button already implements the register: `loading?: boolean` at Button.vue.d.ts:15 ("Marks an in-flight command and suppresses activation until it settles"), implemented at button-Bu9F4uU6.js:18-22 (prop), :35 (`m = loading || disabled`), :55-57 (`data-loading` + `aria-busy`). So `:loading="loading"` is a one-line, in-vocabulary cure that is not taken. The second limb ("no relation between page text and rows") is true and is in fact worse than the axis states — see the missed skeleton/stale-row finding.

confirmed.claim: `aria-live` announces page-text mutations that are not bound to completion of the corresponding list request; rapid updates could announce intermediate states before content is ready.
confirmed.proof: LITERALLY TRUE, but the prescribed cure is worse than the defect. Axis: challenge-C-implementation.md:11 and challenge-D-design.md:14. Live: PaginationBar.vue:17 (`aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"`) renders `page`, which the parent mutates SYNCHRONOUSLY before the fetch — useAdminAudit.ts:74-76 (`page.value++; loadAuditLog();`) and useAdminFlagged.ts:106-108. The announcement therefore fires on the next tick while the request is in flight. HONEST WEIGHTING: the region annotates the CONTROL's state, not the list, and announcing the requested page immediately is the conventional APG reading; "announce the page only when the corresponding list has committed" (challenge-D-design.md:20) would leave the control silent for the entire round trip and is the less accessible design. Real, but INFO — and it is not the a11y defect that matters here (see the focus-destruction and missing-landmark findings, which all three axes missed).

confirmed.claim: There are no first/last or direct-page affordances, and no threshold or large-count design exists.
confirmed.proof: CONFIRMED as a statically provable ergonomic ceiling. Axis: challenge-D-design.md:13. Live: PaginationBar.vue:7-29 offers exactly two commands (prev/next); pageSize is a hard-coded 20 at useAdminAudit.ts:38 and useAdminFlagged.ts:51. The audit ledger grows unboundedly (one row per admin action, demo/palettes/api/admin-audit.ts), so reaching page N costs N-1 clicks AND N-1 network round trips with no jump. Kept at INFO rather than MINOR because the flagged queue is genuinely small and the project's recorded law is KISS/no-contrivance — this is a scope judgement for the owner, not a defect in what exists.

killed.claim: `hasPrev`/`hasNext` are trusted instead of derived, allowing "Page 1 of 2" with Previous enabled or Next disabled; the four scalars can contradict each other.
killed.refutation: REFUTED BY ENUMERATION OF ALL CALL SITES. Axis: challenge-C-implementation.md:8 and challenge-L-library.md:11. PaginationBar has exactly two consumers (grep over demo/ for `PaginationBar`): AdminAuditPanel.vue:83-90 and AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:126-133. Both bind from composables where the three derived scalars are `computed`s over ONE source: useAdminAudit.ts:44-46 and useAdminFlagged.ts:55-57 — `pageCount = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/pageSize))`, `hasNext = page < pageCount`, `hasPrev = page > 1`. "Page 1 of 2 with Previous enabled" requires hasPrev=true at page=1, i.e. `1 > 1`; it is unconstructible in the live tree. The four props are already projections of a single normalized state (total + pageSize + page) — precisely what challenge-L demands and failed to observe already exists one file away. The prescribed `PaginationState = unknown | ready | loading | error` ADT (challenge-L-library.md:17) is additionally unsound here: the component does not own the request, so an `unknown`/`loading` arm would have to be manufactured by the very parents that already hold the truth, adding a second representation to keep in sync — a contrivance for a 48-line leaf with two consumers.

killed.claim: Events do not include the destination page (or query generation / request identity), so parent and child can race against changing props.
killed.refutation: REFUTED — the payload's absence is the safe design, not the hazard. Axis: challenge-C-implementation.md:9 and challenge-L-library.md:12. `$emit('prev')`/`$emit('next')` (PaginationBar.vue:12,26) are pure intent signals; the parent re-derives and re-guards before mutating: useAdminAudit.ts:73-85 and useAdminFlagged.ts:105-117 each re-read `hasNext.value`/`hasPrev.value` at handler time and own `page` exclusively. The child holds no page state to drift out of. Adding a destination to the payload would INTRODUCE the stale-target hazard the axis fears: a click event carrying a page number computed at render time can outlive the state it was computed from. A genuine async hazard does exist, but it is neither in the payload nor in the component — see the missed unordered-response finding, which a destination payload would not fix.

killed.claim: No pending guard prevents double activation.
killed.refutation: REFUTED AT THE STATED LOCUS. Axis: challenge-C-implementation.md:10. There is nothing in PaginationBar to guard — it holds zero state and issues zero requests (PaginationBar.vue:33-47: two imports, defineProps, defineEmits, no ref/watch/lifecycle). At the parent, `page.value++` and the derived `hasNext` update synchronously in the same tick, so the arrow self-disables the moment the boundary is reached (useAdminAudit.ts:45,74). More importantly, double activation is LEGITIMATE — page 1→3 is a valid user intent, and a pending guard would forbid it. The defect the axis is groping toward is not "two clicks" but "two responses committed out of order", which lives in the composables and is unaddressed by any component-level guard. Re-filed as a missed finding with its true site.

killed.claim: The bar disappears whenever `pageCount <= 1`, conflating a verified single page with unknown count, loading, error, and invalid negative/zero totals.
killed.refutation: THREE OF FIVE LIMBS UNCONSTRUCTIBLE; the loading limb has the render topology backwards. Axis: challenge-D-design.md:11. (a) "invalid negative/zero totals": `pageCount = Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/pageSize))` (useAdminAudit.ts:44, useAdminFlagged.ts:55) can never return 0 or a negative, and `total` is itself floor-clamped at `Math.max(0, total.value - 1)` (useAdminFlagged.ts:87,99) — the state does not exist. (b) "unknown count": there is no unknown arm; `total` initializes to 0 (useAdminAudit.ts:36) and is only ever assigned from a response body (:62). (c) "loading": the bar is NOT hidden during loading — AdminAuditPanel.vue:83 and AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:126 place PaginationBar as an UNCONDITIONAL SIBLING of the `v-if="loading"` skeleton block (AdminAuditPanel.vue:36), not inside its v-else chain, so the bar stays mounted with its controls live throughout every page change. The axis asserts the opposite of the live markup. Only the error limb partially survives (after a failed load `total` retains its last value, so the bar renders beneath the error EmptyState) — too thin to carry the finding as written.

killed.claim: The live-region sentence is locally authored; other paginated surfaces can announce at a different phase.
killed.refutation: THE COMPARATOR DOES NOT EXIST. Axis: challenge-L-library.md:13. A sweep of every `aria-live` in demo/ returns exactly four: ComponentSliders.vue:84 (`aria-live="off"`, i.e. explicitly silent), ErrorBoundary.vue:6,20 (`assertive`, an error surface), and PaginationBar.vue:17. There is no second polite live region and no second paginated surface anywhere in the demo (the other three admin panels — AdminUsersPanel, AdminNamesPanel, AdminTagsPanel — contain no page/offset/limit/loadMore state at all). "Can announce at a different phase" is a hypothetical about surfaces that do not exist; there is nothing to be inconsistent WITH.

killed.claim: This generic pattern belongs in glass-ui or a shared application collection package, not independently in each admin panel.
killed.refutation: THE PREMISE IS FACTUALLY FALSE. Axis: challenge-L-library.md:14. The pattern is NOT reimplemented per panel — it is ONE 48-line component with exactly two importers (AdminAuditPanel.vue:102, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:144), and grep confirms zero other pagination markup in the demo. The prescription would promote a two-consumer domain leaf into the published design system, contradicting the project's own recorded law (feedback_kiss_no_contrivance: do not create shared dirs/wrapper layers that do not exist yet) and adding a cross-repo release cycle to every future change. The real duplication is one level down, in the composables — refiled as a missed finding, where the extraction is free and in-repo.

missed.claim: Unrecoverable dead-end: a flagged-queue mutation strands `page` past the end AND unmounts the only control that could get back. All three axes list "stale page after deletion" as a required TEST CELL; none of them constructed it, and the constructed case is worse than a wrong label — it is a trap with no in-app exit.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/useAdminFlagged.ts:81-91 (`dismiss`) and :93-103 (`deletePalette`) splice `items` and decrement `total` but never re-clamp `page` and never reload. Construct with pageSize=20 (:51) and total=21 → pageCount=2 (:55). Navigate to page 2 (holds 1 item). Dismiss it → items=[] and total=20 → pageCount = max(1, ceil(20/20)) = 1, while `page` stays 2. superlatives: Icon-only a11y done exactly right, and rare: PaginationBar.vue:11 and :25 carry explicit `aria-label`s while the glyphs at :14 and :28 carry `aria-hidden="true"` — the accessible name lives on the control, not the decoration, with no double-announcement. The provenance comment at :6 ("W5-a11y: icon-only pagination buttons need aria-labels") records why. This is the single most commonly botched pattern in icon toolbars and it is clean here.

The four props challenge-L calls "four unrelated scalars" are already projections of ONE source of truth, one file away: useAdminAudit.ts:44-46 derives pageCount/hasNext/hasPrev as computeds over `total`, `pageSize`, `page`. The normalized pagination state the L axis demands has existed since the composable was written; the component just receives it flattened, which is the correct shape for a presentational leaf.

Defensive arithmetic that makes bad states unconstructible rather than merely unhandled: `Math.max(1, Math.ceil(total/pageSize))` (useAdminFlagged.ts:55) and `Math.max(0, total.value - 1)` (:87, :99). These two clamps are single-handedly why three of challenge-C's four invalid-input limbs cannot be reached.

The error≠empty doctrine, implemented AND argued in-source: `loadError` is a distinct state from an empty list at both panels (useAdminAudit.ts:20-21, AdminAuditPanel.vue:40-53), with the reasoning committed beside the code — "never costume a dead backend as an empty ledger" (useAdminAudit.ts:65) and "a dead backend must never read as a clear moderation queue" (useAdminFlagged.ts:73). Most admin tools ship the opposite bug forever.

Right-sizing: 48 lines, one job, zero local state, zero lifecycle hooks, zero watchers (PaginationBar.vue:33-47 is two imports, a defineProps and a defineEmits). Each of the corpus's three structural prescriptions — an ADT state machine, a destination-carrying event payload, promotion into the published design system — would make this file worse. The genuinely defective code is all in the two composables and two panels that the challenges never opened.

Typographic intent is present even where the utility undercuts it: `tabular-nums` at PaginationBar.vue:17 means the author was thinking about digit jitter as the page number crosses 9→10. The fix is to swap one utility, not to add a thought.

The in-source provenance discipline across this whole tree — AdminAuditPanel.vue:74-75, AdminFlaggedPanel.vue:62-64 and :86-89 each cite the wave and finding id that produced the line (W5-12/F-9, T.W4-6/T-15/F7, W5-12/F-8).
