confirmed.claim: `contain: content` is unconditional on the grid root and has visual consequences that are not part of the design contract.
confirmed.proof: AXIS: challenge-C-implementation.md:14 + challenge-D-design.md:16. LIVE: demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCardGrid.vue:50-52 `.palette-card-grid { contain: content }` (= layout paint style; `paint` clips the subtree at the PADDING edge). The grid has zero padding and `grid-cols-1` (:4), and grid items default to `justify-self: stretch`, so every card is flush to both content edges. The child is `cartoon-surface` (demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:19), which in node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/card/styles.css:1 is `box-shadow: var(--shadow-cartoon-md)`, and node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/tokens/shadow.css:1 defines `--shadow-cartoon-md: -3px 3px 0 …, -5px 5px 0 …, -7px 7px 0 …` — LEFT + DOWN. demo/styles/foundation.css:366-367 and :518-519 re-point ONLY `--shadow-cartoon` / `--shadow-cartoon-hover` (to 8px RIGHT+down); `-md` is never re-pointed, so the producer's left-cast is what ships. Result: the whole left leg of the card's signature caster is clipped at both call sites, unconditionally, and the last row's bottom leg with it (interior bottom legs fall inside `gap-3` = 12px > 7px and survive). The collision is knowing: PaletteCard.vue:16-18 explicitly declines `overflow-hidden` to protect this caster, and the grid clips it one level up.

confirmed.claim: The root has `role=list` but the children are `role=article`; that is not `listitem` and is not enforced.
confirmed.proof: AXIS: challenge-D-design.md:14. LIVE: PaletteCardGrid.vue:3 `role="list"`; PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:22 `role="article"`; `role="listitem"` census across demo/ src/ e2e/ = 0 hits. ARIA 1.2 gives `list` a Required Owned Element of `listitem`; axe's `aria-required-children` is a serious-severity rule. The violation is BOTH-STATE, which no axis noticed: in the empty state the grid's only owned child is EmptyState's `role="status"` div (demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue:28), so a `list` owning a `status` — so any populated-state-only cure still leaves a malformed list. The in-file comment at PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-8 is wrong twice: `article` is not `listitem`, and neither `list` nor `article` is a landmark role — that false premise is what licensed the structure.

confirmed.claim: The grid exposes a single `empty` bit, so distinct empty species collapse onto one copy — CONFIRMED for filtered-zero, killed for the other four limbs.
confirmed.proof: AXIS: challenge-D-design.md:15. LIVE: PalettesPane.vue:77 computes `empty` from `pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0` (the SEARCH projection) while the header badge at :20/:24 and the delete-all trigger at :62-72 read `pm.savedPalettes.value.length` (the total). So with N saved palettes and a non-matching query the pane simultaneously shows badge "N", a live "Delete all saved palettes" button, and (PalettesPane.vue:79-80) the plate "No saved palettes yet. / Add colors above, then save the set." — a false statement with an inapplicable remedy, in the accessibility tree. BrowsePane.vue:83 has the same shape over `displayedBrowse`, which folds the OKLab color filter (BrowsePane.vue:339-349) and the search/tag/tier filters into the same one bit, then renders "No published palettes here yet. / Publish one from My Palettes and start the wall." (:85-86). One honest branch of copy keyed on query/filter state at the two HOSTS is the cure; the axis's `CollectionSurfaceState` prescription is killed separately.

confirmed.claim: The implementation relies on a single-element root for an external `$el` consumer, but no automated guard prevents a future fragment-root regression.
confirmed.proof: AXIS: challenge-C-implementation.md:13. LIVE: PaletteCardGrid.vue:2-32 is single-element-rooted with the load-bearing comment placed as the div's FIRST CHILD (:7-11) precisely so it cannot create a root fragment. The remote consumer is PalettesPane.vue:180-181: `const sortableEl = computed(() => (sortableGridRef.value as any)?.$el as HTMLElement | undefined)` — the `as any` is gratuitous (`$el` is already `any` on ComponentPublicInstance) and the `as HTMLElement` is unchecked, so a fragment root's anchor Text/Comment node would satisfy it silently and `useSortable` would bind to a non-element. The grid publishes no typed root: `defineExpose` / `defineOptions` census in PaletteCardGrid.vue = 0. The only named guard is mislabeled: e2e/smoke/walk.spec.ts:71-72 comments "PaletteCardGrid is role=\"list\" — the B.W1 single-root invariant" but asserts only `expect(main.getByRole("list").last()).toBeVisible()`, which is entirely insensitive to root arity — the exact regression it names keeps it GREEN.

killed.claim: "The component has no relation to the sortable/reorder library despite comments about `$el` and `useSortable`; the structural requirement is folklore rather than a typed adapter."
killed.refutation: AXIS: challenge-L-library.md:13. Flatly false, and the corpus's worst call. LIVE: PalettesPane.vue:133 `import { useSortable } from "@vueuse/integrations/useSortable"`; :180-183 mounts Sortable on the grid's `$el` with `pm.filteredSaved.value` as the list; `handle: ".drag-handle"` (:184) is satisfied by a class rendered ONLY by the grid's slot children (PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:49). The relation is three lines long and live. The "folklore" the axis dismisses is correct Vue semantics (a leading comment node yields a DEV_ROOT_FRAGMENT whose `$el` is an anchor node, not the div). The one surviving clause — that there is no typed adapter — is C-5, stated better there. And the seam this axis declared nonexistent is exactly where the cluster's only order-corrupting bug lives (see missed #1).

killed.claim: "Arbitrary `gridClass` can override columns, display, containment, or visibility and makes layout testing unbounded" / "every responsive decision arrives through `gridClass`" / "exports raw styling authority to every consumer."
killed.refutation: AXIS: challenge-C-implementation.md:12, challenge-D-design.md:13, challenge-L-library.md:10. Killed four ways. (a) The CONTAINMENT limb is false: PaletteCardGrid.vue:47-52 is a `<style scoped>` block, which compiles UNLAYERED as `.palette-card-grid[data-v-hash]`, while every Tailwind `contain-*` utility is emitted inside `@layer utilities` (demo/styles/foundation.css:1 `@import "tailwindcss"`); unlayered declarations beat layered ones regardless of specificity, so no utility passed through `gridClass` can defeat it. (b) The census refutes "every responsive decision": `gridClass|grid-class` has exactly ONE consumer repo-wide — BrowsePane.vue:87-90 — and it passes `transition-opacity duration-fast` plus a conditional `opacity-50`. Zero layout classes, zero responsive classes; NO responsive decision arrives through it. (c) Reading order is DOM order unconditionally; `gridClass` cannot reorder anything. (d) Decisively, the prescribed cure is structurally void: PaletteCardGrid.vue:35-45 has no `defineOptions`/`inheritAttrs: false` and the component is single-element-rooted, so Vue's default attribute fallthrough already merges any consumer `class` onto the root. Deleting or bounding the prop removes zero capability. The real finding under this family is that `gridClass` is a redundant second mechanism (missed #6).

killed.claim: "`empty` can contradict the default slot; there is no item count or state union to enforce exclusivity" / "A caller can render cards and the empty plate simultaneously, or neither."
killed.refutation: AXIS: challenge-C-implementation.md:9, challenge-D-design.md:11. Both — and only — consumers derive `empty` from the SAME array they iterate, on adjacent lines of the same render: PalettesPane.vue:77 `:empty="pm.filteredSaved.value.length === 0"` against :83 `v-for="palette in pm.filteredSaved.value"`; BrowsePane.vue:83 `:empty="displayedBrowse.length === 0"` against :93 `v-for="palette in displayedBrowse"`. There is no live producer of the contradiction. The implied cure is also unsound: counting `$slots.default?.()` VNodes cannot decide item count here, because the slot content is a v-for Fragment and, in dev, PaletteCard is itself a root-fragment component (PaletteCard.vue:2-5, leading comment before the root div) — VNode counting would introduce a new defect rather than close one.

killed.claim: "`v-if=\"$slots.emptyAction\"` checks only whether a slot function exists, not whether it produces an actionable node" / "couples rendering to Vue slot presence rather than a typed action model."
killed.refutation: AXIS: challenge-C-implementation.md:10, challenge-L-library.md:12. True of Vue in general, doubly inert here. (a) The guard is a no-op: EmptyState.vue:64 renders `<slot name="action" />` UNCONDITIONALLY with no fallback content, so a slot that renders nothing emits no flex item, no gap and no reserved box whether or not PaletteCardGrid guards it. (b) `emptyAction|empty-action` census across demo/ and e2e/ returns exactly two hits, both the declaration itself (PaletteCardGrid.vue:28-29) — the slot has ZERO consumers. Two axes independently typed the semantics of an API that is never instantiated; the real defect on those lines is that the in-file owner ruling "The CTA slot survives on the caption" (:19-20) survived in the primitive and died at every call site (see missed #8's sibling note).

killed.claim: "Optional text props are passed through unchanged, so an empty plate can be semantically empty" / "A true-empty surface can render blank annotation fields and lose the careful invitation hierarchy."
killed.refutation: AXIS: challenge-C-implementation.md:11, challenge-D-design.md:12. Refuted at the primitive: EmptyState.vue:90 hard-defaults `eyebrow: "· empty plate ·"` and `dots: true` (Vue applies `withDefaults` on explicit `undefined`), and `hint` is `v-if`-guarded at :61 so an omitted hint renders nothing at all. The plural "blank annotation fields" is false. One grain survives — `message` alone is unguarded — and it is filed as its own INFO row (missed #8) rather than as this claim.

killed.id: D-5 (non-filtered limbs) + D's "Required state matrix" rider

The three-state composition already ships ONE ALTITUDE UP and is better there: BrowsePane.vue:40-78 renders loading / error / wall as sibling branches of a single `<Transition name="vj-morph" mode="out-in">`, with the error plate OUTSIDE the list carrying the route's only real action (a Retry Button, :68-77), and paging as a deliberate sibling at :125-144. killed.claim: "`EmptyState` is a demo-local primitive reached by a deep relative path; the grid has no shared collection-state primitive."
killed.refutation: AXIS: challenge-L-library.md:9. The path is correct and is the ratified house form: PaletteCardGrid.vue:36 `import EmptyState from "../../../shared/ui/EmptyState.vue"` resolves from demo/palettes/browser/card/ to demo/shared/ui/EmptyState.vue (verified present, 105 lines) — demo path aliases were deliberately retired and demo/shared/ui/ carries no barrel. And EmptyState IS the shared primitive the axis says is missing: two typed species (`empty` / `error`) with differentiated roles (`role="status"` :28 vs `role="alert"` :17), a documented prop surface (:72-91), and 8 importers repo-wide (grep `import EmptyState` = 8). A convention read as a smell.

killed.claim: "Default and named slots are unconstrained. The root's list semantics depend on undocumented child behavior."
killed.refutation: AXIS: challenge-L-library.md:11. The child contract is documented IN FILE at PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-8 (`role="list"` — each child PaletteCard `role="article"`), and it is partly executable: e2e/smoke/oracles/o9-shadow-palette.spec.ts:187/:203 pin the TRUE-EMPTY branch on both hosts. confirmed.claim: Inline math is an atomic `inline-block` whose internal content wraps, so at 200% zoom and on mobile it grows a 112px-tall 'word' inside a 28px-leaded paragraph.

KaTeX's internal wrap points are real: `.katex .base{position:relative;white-space:nowrap;width:min-content}` — each `.base` span is nowrap but KaTeX emits MULTIPLE `.base` spans split at relation/binary boundaries, so the inline box wraps between them and grows in height. Note the display-mode counterpart `.katex-display>.katex{white-space:nowrap}` is what forbids the same wrap in display mode (D-2). The content-shape half of D-9's diagnosis is verified in live content: assets/docs/lab.md:50 is `L^* = 0 \text{ (black) to } 100 \text{ (diffuse white)}` — a sentence typeset as an equation — and the same shape recurs at lab.md:53,56, rgb.md:46,49,52, hsl.md:43,48,51, hsv.md:24,29,34, hwb.md:24,35,40, oklab.md:48,51,54, kelvin.md:22. killed.claim: BLOCKER — RTL mirrors scientific notation: subscripts and superscripts swap sides.
killed.refutation: MECHANISM TRUE, SEVERITY REFUTED — downgrade BLOCKER → MAJOR-latent. The mechanism is real and I confirmed it: `grep -o "direction:[a-z-]*" node_modules/katex/dist/katex.min.css` yields only `direction:column` / `direction:row` (both flex-direction), so `.katex` inherits document direction, and Katex.vue:2 emits no `dir` and no `unicode-bidi` isolation. But D's OWN severity definition (challenge-D-design.md:88) is "BLOCKER = loses or destroys content in a shipped, default configuration." The shipped default configuration is `dir="ltr"`, hard-coded at demo/color-picker/index.html:11, and I found NO product path that ever sets it otherwise: `grep -rn 'dir="rtl"|setAttribute("dir")' demo/ src/` returns nothing — no toggle, no locale switch, no router hook. The corruption is reachable only by an auditor typing `document.documentElement.setAttribute("dir","rtl")` in a console. That makes it a readiness defect against the declared RTL seam (whose own comment at index.html:2-6 calls it "RTL mechanical readiness"), not shipped content loss. The cure is sound and cheap and should still land; the BLOCKER label is over-severe and, sitting beside the genuinely-shipped D-2, distorts triage.

killed.claim: MAJOR (the gestalt one) — a 588 kB runtime typesetter on the landing route, against the repo's own established build-time idiom; a dual path (edict 2) at architectural altitude.

L-5 rests on: "Code snippets in these very doc pages are formatted and highlighted at build time by a plugin this repo wrote, precisely so no runtime library ships. Math — the only other rich content type in the same documents — takes the opposite path." (challenge-L-library.md:230-246, restated as "Precedent, not invention" at :485). (1) `?source` has ZERO consumers repo-wide — the only hits outside node_modules/docs/dist are plugins/vite-source-export.ts's own definition and the vite.config.ts:72 comment L-10 already convicts as false. (2) The 11 About documents contain ZERO fenced code blocks: `grep -c '^```' assets/docs/*.md` → 0 for every one of hex, hsl, hsv, hwb, kelvin, lab, lch, oklab, oklch, rgb, xyz. There is no build-time branch in live use to be the other half of a dual path — math is not the outlier, it is the ONLY rich content type in these documents at all. The corroborating comment at demo/scenes/about/markdown/composables/useMarkdownHighlighting.ts:71-73 ("Code blocks are pre-formatted and pre-highlighted at build time by the vite-source-export plugin") is itself stale prose describing the same dead path. killed.claim: MINOR — a display formula scrolled to lands entirely behind the sticky pane header; "occluded: 110.61px → 190.4% of the ink is above the header's bottom edge."
killed.refutation: THE METRIC IS IMPOSSIBLE AND THE TRIGGER HAS NO PRODUCT PATH. (1) 190.4% occlusion cannot exist — occlusion is bounded by 100%. D-12's own numbers say the ink spans y=129.98…188.06 (58.08px) and the header bottom is y=240.59, so the correct statement is that 100% of the ink is occluded; 110.61px is the ink-top-to-header-bottom distance, not occluded ink, and 110.61/58.08 = 1.904 is a ratio of two unlike quantities. (2) The stated trigger — "the browser's own in-page-anchor behaviour" — does not exist in this product. vite.config.ts:162 configures `Markdown({})` with no `markdownItSetup` and no anchor plugin; unplugin-vue-markdown's dependencies are only `@mdit-vue/plugin-component` and `@mdit-vue/plugin-frontmatter` (verified from its package.json), and markdown-it core adds no heading ids. So no heading in the About corpus carries an id, and the app is hash-routed (`/#/`) so a fragment would be consumed by the router anyway. The only remaining real path is find-in-page scroll. The finding survives at reduced strength; the headline number must be struck. (See also missed finding M-2: the same absence makes Markdown.vue:121's `scroll-m-20` itself dead — D-12's "family defect" note is truer than it knew, in the opposite direction.)

killed.claim: Cure — "Math is a specimen. Give it the specimen well (`bg-well`, the rung-2 tone the code fences and TOC already share — Markdown.vue:236,241,388)."
killed.refutation: THE CURE'S PRECEDENT DOES NOT RENDER. Two of the three cited `bg-well` consumers are dead for the only corpus that reaches this stylesheet. Fenced code: zero across all 11 documents (`grep -c '^```' assets/docs/*.md` → 0 each), so `pre { @apply bg-well … }` at Markdown.vue:234-238 never paints. TOC: zero (`grep -ln "toc" assets/docs/*.md` → no files), so `.toc { @apply bg-well … }` at Markdown.vue:385-390 never paints. The ONLY live `bg-well` consumer on this surface is the inline-code chip at Markdown.vue:249-253. So the cure's rationale — that the well tone is an established rung on this surface which math should join — is false; adopting it would make math the second, not the fourth, member. The FINDING (D-6's inverted chromatic hierarchy) stands and is well-proven; the cure must be re-argued from the inline-code chip alone, or from the canon, not from phantom siblings. Minor collateral: the line cites are also off — `bg-well` is at :235, :241 and :386, not :236/:241/:388.

missed.claim: M-2 · `scroll-m-20` on About headings and on `.toc` is dead — the About route has no in-page anchor mechanism at all, so no scroll target exists for any species, math included.
missed.proof: Markdown.vue:121 applies `@apply font-display font-bold scroll-m-20` to `> h1..h6` and Markdown.vue:389 applies `scroll-m-20` to `.toc`. Neither can ever fire: vite.config.ts:162 registers `Markdown({})` with no options and no `markdownItSetup`, and unplugin-vue-markdown's dependencies are only `@mdit-vue/plugin-component` and `@mdit-vue/plugin-frontmatter` (read from its package.json) — no `markdown-it-anchor`, and markdown-it core assigns no heading ids. The app is additionally hash-routed (`/#/`, demo/shell/viewSchema.ts), so a URL fragment is consumed by the router before it could act as an anchor. D-12 read this backwards — it treated math's `scroll-margin: 0` as the outlier in a "family defect" where the heading's 80px is merely "short". In fact the family is uniformly inert, which both weakens D-12's severity and reveals a separate, unnamed defect: a documented spacing token (`scroll-m-20`) carried on the two most-styled species with nothing on the route able to trigger it.

missed.claim: M-3 · The inline-math gutter is off the φ ladder and, being symmetric, detaches sentence-terminating punctuation from the formula it terminates at 4 live call sites.
missed.proof: Markdown.vue:286-289 sets `p div.inline-block:has(> .katex), li div.inline-block:has(> .katex) { @apply mx-1; }` — `mx-1` is 0.25rem, which is on neither φ rung that brackets it (φ-0 = 0.382rem, φ-1 = 0.618rem, demo/styles/foundation.css:458-459). This is despite demo/styles/foundation.css:149-156 registering `--spacing-phi-0…4` for exactly this purpose, with the comment "consumers write `py-phi-3` / `pb-phi-4`, never `py-[1.618rem]`" — `mx-phi-0` was available. Every other spacing declaration in the same rule-block family uses `var(--phi-*)` (:194, :207-208, :237, :259, :265, :271, :282, :304-305, :311). The visible consequence, which no axis measured: because `mx` is symmetric, the right margin also lands between the formula and any punctuation that follows it. Four live sites end a sentence directly on the closing tag — assets/docs/hwb.md:77 (twice, one comma and one full stop), assets/docs/hex.md:62, assets/docs/lab.md:74 — each rendering with a 4px orphaned punctuation mark. D-7 covered vertical rhythm and D-13 the centring axis; the horizontal inline gutter was covered by neither.

missed.claim: M-4 · A second glass-ui producer primitive for this exact port is bypassed and unnamed by any axis: `.scrollbar-thin`, bound to `--scrollbar-thumb` / `--scrollbar-track`.

Its only instantiation in the whole demo is ExtractWorkbench.vue:159 (`grep -rn "ShadowPalette" demo --include=*.vue`), and the artefact it stands in for at that seat is the card rendered at ExtractWorkbench.vue:145-150 with `:expanded="true"` and `swatch-class="w-12 h-12 sm:w-14 sm:h-14"` — i.e. ShadowPalette's 56px swatches and three-row height match its one seat exactly. The same is true of PaletteCardSkeleton at its Extract seat (ExtractWorkbench.vue:103). The mismatch is one deployment — PaletteCardSkeleton at BrowsePane.vue:49 and :130 — not "the ghosts" as a class. The measurement quoted under D3-6 (`probe-D5 → extract`, ghostRect 462×150) was taken on the artefact that is correct for its route and compared against a card on a different route.

killed.claim: "one host wires 15 of 16 emits, another 1 of 16 … Mean 5.2/16" over six hosts including demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue at 1/16.
killed.refutation: GenerateControls.vue is not a host. `grep -n "PaletteCard" demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue` returns exactly one line — :125, inside a comment ("the rung-2 WELL species (Q4: PaletteCard → well)"); the file instantiates PaletteColorStrip (:135), never PaletteCard. The real host set is five (BrowsePane, PalettesPane, AdminUsersPanel, ExtractWorkbench, MixSourceSelector), so the mean is 30/5 = 6.0/16, not 5.2/16 — the finding that exists to correct a wrong denominator carries a wrong denominator. The structural claim (two hosts wire one event and inherit fifteen silently-dropped menu actions) survives on the four remaining rows.

killed.claim: "PaletteCard.vue | 10 props | 17 emits" and "a 17-emit action bus".
killed.refutation: The live count is 16. PaletteCard.vue:200-218 declares click, delete, publish, save, vote, rename, editColor, addColor, feature, adminDelete, setVisibility, fork, versions, flag, editTags, export — parsed count 16 emits / 10 props. The C axis (challenge-C-implementation.md:516) and L-46 both say 16; the D axis's 17 is wrong twice in the same finding.

killed.claim: "Under prefers-reduced-motion the card still carries a 0.1s transition … 0.1 s is small, but it is not zero, and it is unowned — the value arrives from a utility nobody in this folder chose."
killed.refutation: The 0.1s is the design, and it is owned — by the producer, deliberately. glass-ui a11y-overrides.css (served, reached at demo/styles/foundation.css:56) sets `transition-duration: 0.1s` together with a property list narrowed to `opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow`: the spatial legs are deleted outright and only non-vestibular colour legs survive. The program's own motion adjudication rules this exact claim shape FALSE elsewhere for the identical mechanism — motion-quarantine.md M-17 ("The colour legs survive by deliberate design … there is nothing missing") and M-29/M-03 ("motion is governed centrally, not duplicated per component") — and records it as superlative S-1. The second limb of D3-20 (the JS height transition never joined the PRM-governed family) is not only true but is the corpus's own BLOCKER C4-1.

killed.claim: "WatercolorDot's `tag` prop is a no-op … Either honour `tag` and forward ARIA to the rendered element, or remove `tag` from the typed surface so a consumer cannot silently depend on it."
killed.refutation: The producer already did the second, and the first option contradicts ratified law. WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts at glass-ui 7.0.0 declares six props and no `tag` at all — there is no typed surface to remove it from. And VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:90 rules: "V **abrogates a selection outline and interactive host on `WatercolorDot`**. P051 removes the public `tag="button"`/interactive-host branch in the clean major; the organic face supplies color/specimen identity only", with W17 already owning the manifest of the ~25 stale `tag=` call sites. So the live defect is a stale CONSUMER call at SwatchHoverMenu.vue:17,33, not a producer gap, and asking the producer to honour `tag` would reverse a ratified ruling. The ARIA-forwarding limb (a data-bearing face hard-coding `aria-hidden` while §4.2 requires data-bearing faces to remain named content) survives as a real ask.

killed.claim: "Delete useHeightTransition.ts and its wiring; render the swatch panel as `<Transition name="vj-morph">` with `--vj-morph-collapse: 0px` / `--vj-morph-expanded: <cap>` on the panel, exactly as the rename row does."
killed.refutation: Structurally unsound for this content. vj-morph morphs `max-height` against a static cap (demo/styles/animations.css:107-140), which works for the rename row precisely because that row is one fixed-height input (`--vj-morph-expanded: 3rem`, PaletteCard.vue:358-363). The swatch panel's height is variable by construction — 1..24+ dots wrapping at `w-9 h-9 sm:w-10 sm:h-10`, plus an optional slug row — and the panel is `overflow-hidden` (PaletteCardSwatches.vue:2), so any fixed cap either clips a large palette or over-reserves for a small one. The correct primitive is already in the tree and already consumed by a sibling: glass-ui `Collapsible` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/collapsible/Collapsible.vue.d.ts, re-exported at demo/ui/collapsible, used at MixSourceSelector.vue:5), which owns the measured content height in CSS. The diagnosis stands; the cure needs replacing.

killed.claim: Greenfield lattice line: `└ <ExpandableContainer v-model:open>  glass-ui ./expandable-container` as the home of the card's swatch disclosure.
killed.refutation: Wrong producer primitive. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/expandable-container.js imports `Teleport`, reka-ui's `FocusScope`, Maximize2/Minimize2, locks `document.body.style.overflow`, and renders with `aria-modal` and a `fullscreen-chrome` slot — it is a fullscreen/modal expander, not an inline disclosure. Adopting it would turn a row's swatch reveal into a focus-trapped fullscreen overlay with a page scroll lock. Same correction as above: `Collapsible` is the shipped disclosure.

killed.claim: "an expanded card has exactly one tabbable element" / "The only accessible content on a five-colour palette is its name, the numeral 5, and 'Palette menu'"; and "only when `showSlug` is passed, i.e. only on `/#/browse`".
killed.refutation: Both are route-scoped generalisations taken from a local-palette fixture. The vote button renders under `v-if="!palette.isLocal"` (PaletteCardMeta.vue:44) and the slug row plus its named `Copy slug` button render under `v-if="displaySlug"` (PaletteCardSwatches.vue:4-19), so on /#/browse an expanded card has at least three tab stops, not one. And `show-slug` is passed at two sites, not one: BrowsePane.vue:100 and AdminUsersPanel.vue:146. Neither correction touches the colour limb — no colour in any state carries an accessible name — nor the deadness of EMPTY_PALETTE_SWATCH.

killed.claim: "`PROPORTION-AUDIT.md` PR-05 already carries the terminal verb: 'Dividers, **caster shadows** and corner marks repeat a boundary → **REMOVE**.'"
killed.refutation: The live row's verb is conditional, not terminal: docs/tranches/V/PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:49 reads `| PR-05 | Dividers, caster shadows and corner marks repeat a boundary | **REMOVE / KEEP** | …`. missed.claim: Every clipboard write in the component discards the producer's discriminated result and gives the user no confirmation and no failure signal — in the component whose entire purpose is copying colours, and which owns an unused feedback chip.
missed.proof: glass-ui ships `writeClipboard(text): Promise<CopyResult>` where `CopyResult = {ok:true} | {ok:false, reason}`, documented at node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts:31-37 as "the honest primitive … for consumers that own their own feedback", alongside `useClipboard()` which exposes a `status` (:23-29). Meanwhile PaletteCard.vue:238-244 defines `showFeedback` and mounts ActionFeedback (:123-128) — the confirmation surface exists and is never used for copies. On any platform where the clipboard API rejects (non-secure context, Safari gesture-chain loss) the user is told nothing and the colour is simply not copied. All three axes discuss clipboard only as a duplicated serializer (L-35); none audits its feedback.

missed.claim: Focus is destroyed on every disclosure close: nothing restores it after rename submit/cancel or after collapse.

missed.claim: The card field's loading announcement is both malformed and multiplied: an aria-label on a roleless div, plus one live region per ghost row saying the same sentence four times.

Simultaneously each PaletteCardSkeleton declares its own `role="status" aria-label="Loading palette"` (PaletteCardSkeleton.vue:35-36) and BrowsePane renders SKELETON_COUNT = 4 of them (:50, :207) plus 2 more on load-more (:130) — four to six polite live regions carrying one message, each inserted into the DOM already populated (a live region added with its content commonly announces nothing at all). The sibling ShadowPalette solves exactly this correctly and documents why (ShadowPalette.vue:36-40, :44 aria-hidden, no role=status). All three axes examined the ghosts' geometry and material; none examined what they say.

missed.claim: The metadata rail's entire meaning lives in `title` attributes on non-focusable spans, and one glyph carries two different meanings side by side.
missed.proof: PaletteCardMeta.vue:10 (`Remixed from ${forkOf}`), :19 (`${forkCount} remix(es)`) and :29 (`${versionCount} versions`) render an icon plus a bare numeral, with the semantics only in `title`. `title` surfaces on pointer hover alone — no touch route, no keyboard route, and unreliable AT exposure on a non-interactive `<span>`. Worse, :12 and :21 both render `GitFork`: the first means "this palette is a fork OF something", the second means "N forks OF this palette", adjacent in the same row with no textual distinction. Nothing in the corpus's a11y inventories (D3-2's AT transcript, C4-5's live-region count) reaches the meta rail.

missed.claim: `scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth"})` is the one motion in the folder that neither PRM guard can reach.
missed.proof: useHeightTransition.ts:48 calls `htmlEl.scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth", block:"nearest"})` unconditionally on expand. Both guards act only on animation/transition properties (demo/styles/animations.css:184-193; glass-ui a11y-overrides.css), and `scroll-behavior: auto !important` at animations.css:186 governs only scrolls whose behavior is "auto" — an explicit "smooth" argument wins by spec. It is latent today solely because C4-1's hang stops `onAfterEnter` from running under PRM, i.e. correct behaviour arrived at by a bug; any minimal repair of C4-1 that keeps the hook ships un-gated smooth scrolling to reduced-motion users. This is the same class as the sweep's own new defect MQ-1 (motion-quarantine.md:131-169) — a guard that demonstrably fires and is powerless — and no axis asserts it.

The name promises an action the control will not perform. missed.claim: The loading ghosts depict the wrong species: rounded rectangles where the real swatch is a seeded organic blob.

The ghost→card transition therefore changes shape as well as size. Three axes measured the ghosts' height, width, border and shadow; none checked what shape they promise.

unproven: D3-6's "100 px of layout collapses under the user's scroll position every time a page lands" — the Browse skeleton was never captured live (challenge-L-library.md §4 #18 records "NO SKELETON OBSERVED" on /#/browse); the delta is inferred from a same-source sibling measured at a different route. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

C4-1 consequence 3 — that a PRM-retained `height:0` panel keeps the `Copy slug` button in the tab order on /#/browse. Its own author labels it DERIVED; probe F could not raise a remote card without the authed e2e fixture. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

My own extension of D3-2 — that reka-ui's `PopoverTrigger as-child` prop/listener/ref merge is swallowed by WatercolorDot's `inheritAttrs:false`, killing the touch route to per-colour actions. The producer bytes are certain (only attrs.class/attrs.style are read); the reka Primitive merge path should be confirmed on a real coarse-pointer context. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

The magnitude of D3-9's specimen falsification — how far a swatch composited at `opacity: 0.75` over the live /#/mix aurora drifts from its declared colour. The mechanism is certain; the number is not. UNPROVEN-NEEDS-LIVE.

D3-12's secondary clause "the shadow is also lighter than the plate it falls on" — the measurement compares shadow ink to the CARD ground (ΔL 0.0053), not to the pane plate the facets actually fall on. The primary claim (no dark-mode material identity) is proven at token level; this clause is not.

Whether the un-gated `scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth"})` (my finding) produces observable scrolling in practice given `block:"nearest"` — it will not move a fully visible row. The PRM-unreachability is provable statically; the user-visible amplitude is not.
superlatives: PaletteColorStrip.vue:47-71 — the weighted-segment logic is the best thing in the cone, and better than the corpus credits: an 8% legibility floor keeps small quantizer clusters visible, and the floored fractions are RENORMALISED (`floored.map(x => (x / flooredTotal) * 100)`) so the strip still sums to exactly 100% — the step most floor-clamped implementations drop, leaving overflow. It also degrades in two documented stages (explicit `weights` → the colours' own `weight` fields → equal widths), so an extracted palette carries its population story on the palette itself with no second twin strip.

ShadowPalette.vue:36-44 and :92-114 — the one file in the cone that gets announcement AND material right, and says why: the ghost is `aria-hidden` with no `role="status"` and no "Loading" label because nothing is loading ("a shimmering aria-hidden plate does not lie to AT"), and its ink ladder fades by `color-mix` steps rather than element opacity, citing the D6 rule — the same VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:143 law that its own sibling call site (MixSourceSelector's `opacity-75`) breaks.

PaletteCardMenu.vue:24-40 — the K-INV5 pattern: a tripped availability latch (`apiOffline`, :217, read through the injected api-client seam rather than a module singleton) both `:disabled`s the doomed action and NAMES the degraded state in-register as a small-caps "offline" annotation, instead of letting the user fire it and catch a toast. Better failure design than most of the product.

PaletteCardGrid.vue:7-11 — a comment that earns its lines: it explains that it is deliberately the div's FIRST CHILD rather than a preceding sibling, because a leading comment node makes the SFC multi-root and PalettesPane reads `$el` for useSortable, which would then resolve to the comment node. A real, non-obvious, action-at-a-distance hazard documented at the exact site that causes it.

demo/palettes/browser/card/index.ts — named-only re-exports with the reason stated (PI-6): a star re-export of SFCs is a side-effecting import because scoped `<style>` blocks ride along, so named exports are what let the bundler tree-shake per consumer. Rare discipline, correctly explained.

The motion idiom the folder actually uses: PaletteCard.vue:358-363 (`.rename-morph`) and ActionFeedback.vue:50-57 (`.feedback-chip`) parameterise a shared, centrally PRM-governed CSS family through geometry custom properties instead of forking keyframes — exactly the architecture the program's own motion sweep records as superlative S-1 (motion-quarantine.md:175-179). C4-1 is the sharper for it: the one transition that left this family is the one that breaks.

useHoverPopover.ts:26-31 — `if (!canHover.value || e.pointerType === "touch") return` guards the hover path against a touch pointer on a device whose media query reports hover, which is the failure mode most hover-popover implementations ship with.

PaletteCard.vue:60-63 — the local `golden-text-shimmer` keyframe was retired ONTO glass-ui's `.gold-shimmer` / `metal-shimmer-sweep` register rather than deleted, and the scoped block that remains keeps only what the producer register does not own (the outline hue and the icon ink at :343-354). The house rule is "moved, not deleted"; this is it, done correctly, with the seam named.

missed.claim: useHeightTransition never removes its transitionend listeners except on the one success path, and never checks the event target — so cancelled transitions and (under PRM) every single expand leave a permanently attached listener on a node that is itself never released.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHeightTransition.ts:35-39 and :66-70 both do `htmlEl.addEventListener("transitionend", function handler(e) { if (e.propertyName !== "height") return; htmlEl.removeEventListener(...); done(); })`. The removal is INSIDE the height branch, so any path that does not reach it leaks the listener: (a) a transition interrupted by Vue (the user collapses mid-expand) — Vue calls the guarded `_enterCb`, the DOM listener stays attached forever; (b) unmount — there is no onUnmounted/onScopeDispose anywhere in the folder (grep exit 1); (c) under PRM the height leg never fires at all, and challenge-C-implementation.md:141 measured that the SAME retained node is reused on re-expand, so every expand/collapse cycle stacks another listener on one element that is never GC'd. onAfterEnter (:42-49) and onAfterLeave (:73-78) clear height/opacity/transition and call scrollIntoView but never removeEventListener. Second, distinct hazard from the same two lines: transitionend BUBBLES, and there is no `e.target === htmlEl` guard, so a descendant that ever transitions `height` resolves the parent's done() early. C4-1 found the node retention; nobody stated the listener accumulation or the missing target guard, and the prescribed cure (delete the composable) happens to fix both — but only if the composable is actually deleted rather than patched.

missed.claim: The certified-ink path has no error boundary: parseOklch treats parseCssColor as total, and parseCssColor is not — `oklch()` throws a TypeError instead of returning {ok:false}.
missed.proof: demo/color-session/ink.ts:38-43 is `const parsed = parseCssColor(source); if (!parsed.ok) return null;` — a Result check with no try/catch. Measured against the installed library, read-only, no browser: `node -e "import('@mkbabb/value.js/css').then(m => m.parseCssColor('oklch()'))"` → THROWS `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`, while '', '  ', 'rgb(', 'not-a-color' and 'oklch(0.5 0.1)' all correctly return {ok:false}. The throw propagates parseOklch → certifyAccentInk (ink.ts:130-143, whose `if (!accent) return css` guard is never reached) → safeCss (useContrastSafeColor.ts:353-359) → PaletteCard.vue:230 `safeFirstColor`, which is read during render at PaletteCard.vue:144 for every expanded card. Blast radius beyond this component: the same unguarded safeCss is called at ColorNutritionLabel.vue:200, MobileMenuDropdown.vue:24, ExtractControls.vue:124 and useSpecimenRows.ts:69. superlatives: demo/picker/controls/spectrumLuma.ts — the single best artifact touched by this audit. Eighteen lines of docstring that name the anti-pattern they exist to prevent (`:8-9` "Share the function, never copy the constant"), enumerate every instrument bound by the rule (`:4-7`), and state the physical model and its derivation from the actual gradient stack (`:11-18`); then exactly one exported constant (`:20`) and one predicate (`:33`). It is the standard the rest of this component tree should be measured against, and MiniColorPicker's real offence is being outside its reach rather than inside it.

SpectrumCanvas.vue's pointer lifecycle — every line of it is a bug someone already paid for. `releaseCapture()` with a try/catch and a comment naming the detached-element case (`:81-91`); `@pointercancel` AND `@lostpointercapture` bound together (`:18-19`); rAF coalescing that FLUSHES the pending sample on stop rather than dropping the user's last movement (`:191-194`); an `onUnmounted` that both releases capture and cancels the frame (`:217-224`); and a zero-rect guard before the divide (`:115`). C-1, C-6 and my missed zero-rect row are each the absence of one of these.

SpectrumCanvas.vue:58-63 — three comment lines that state the round-trip-jitter law, the persistence rule and the invalidation rule ("Raw spectrum coords to avoid HSV roundtrip jitter. Persists after mouseup so the dot stays where the user placed it. Cleared when color changes from a non-spectrum source"), backed by the `rawS`/`rawV` refs and the `spectrumIsSource` latch at `:61-75`. The exact defect this audit's strongest finding describes — solved, and written down, one directory away.

vite.config.ts:37-49 — the demo's seven self-aliases are GENERATED from `package.json#exports` and compiled to anchored regexes, so the demo provably cannot consume a specifier a real npm consumer could not write; `:24-36` records the prefix-rewrite failure that motivated the array form and names the exact boot break it caused. Machinery that makes a whole class of dogfood violation unrepresentable rather than merely forbidden — and it holds repo-wide (`grep -rn '"@src' demo/` → 0, re-verified at HEAD).

demo/palettes/browser/search/index.ts — cluster-private scoping done exactly right: a header stating the rule and its provenance, named re-exports only, and `MiniColorPicker` deliberately withheld because it is consumed solely by its sibling (SearchFilterBar.vue:132). Even at its worst the component leaked no public surface; whatever replaces it inherits a clean boundary.

useSpectrumPlateStyle.ts:1-6 — a cohesion lift that documents its own reason (keeping the SFC under the 400-LoC cap after two motion beats landed) and asserts byte-equivalence with the computeds it replaced. The right way to write down why a file exists.

MiniColorPicker.vue:157-163, inside the subject itself — the static overlay lives in scoped CSS and only the dynamic `--hue` crosses through `:style`, with a comment stating the split. All three axes independently probed it, all three ruled it correct, and both D passes explicitly demand it be carried into whatever replaces the file (challenge-D-design-pass1-c654824e.md:565-567, challenge-D-design.md:458-460). One genuinely good decision inside a defective component.

src/color/operations.ts:305-312 — a real `roundHalfEven` whose half test is scaled to the magnitude of the value (`Number.EPSILON * Math.max(1, Math.abs(value))`) rather than a naive `=== 0.5`, applied at exactly one byte quantiser (`:324`). The library has one rounding law and states it once; the whole L-1 finding exists because a leaf component wrote a second one.

killed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:319-332 — 'The hue rail's right end does not actuate … same `rounded-full` hit-clip as N-1, at a 12px-tall rail whose end caps are 6px semicircles.'
killed.refutation: Refuted twice over. (a) The geometry is mis-attributed. The rail is 174×12 with `rounded-full` (MiniColorPicker.vue:26), so the right cap is a circle centred at (168,6) with r=6; the last real pixel column (173.5, 6) is 5.5px from that centre and is therefore INSIDE the shape. What probe-D2-3.json actually commanded was `x = 100%` = `rect.left + 174` — one pixel past a half-open border box, which lands outside EVERY element regardless of `border-radius`. The doc's own left arm proves the asymmetry is a probe artefact: `x = 0` DID actuate (`left: "0%"`). (b) Even granting the miss, no colour is lost. `currentHex` at hue 360 gives `h = 1`, `i = Math.floor(6) = 6`, `i % 6 = 0`, `f = 0` → `(v, p, p)` = pure red — identical to hue 0 — and the gradient's last stop `#f00` (:27) is its first. hue 360 ≡ hue 0, which is reachable at the left end. Limb 2 (handle 50.0% clipped at `left: 0%`) is real and is folded into the confirmed C-4 row.

killed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:17-21, :128-140 — 'A colour picker that cannot pick white'; the best reachable near-white is `(x=1,y=20) → S=0.006, V=0.821` or `(x=20,y=1) → S=0.115, V=0.991`, and 'neither is white.'
killed.refutation: Contradicted by the finding's OWN evidence file. probe-D2-3.json arm `inset+2,+2` records `before "#4488cc" → after "#f8fafb"`, `changed: true` — rgb(248,250,251), 1.4% from white. The geometry the doc itself states (`(x−8)² + (y−8)² ≤ 64`) admits more still: (3,3) is 7.07 from the centre, hence live, and yields S=0.017, V=0.973 ≈ #f8f8f4. So the claimed 'best reachable' of S=0.006/V=0.821 — a mid-grey around #d1d1d1 — is off by an order of magnitude in perceptual distance. The dead quarter-disc is real (confirmed above) but the severity built on it is not: exact `#ffffff` is unreachable while the visually-white neighbourhood is reachable 2px inside the corner, and the downstream consumer is a colour search filtered by OKLab distance ≤ 0.15 (demo/palettes/BrowsePane.vue:343), where ΔL ≈ 0.01 changes no result. BLOCKER → MAJOR.

killed.claim: challenge-D-design.md:483-484 — 'One `Search` owner — the tray's inline button, which already carries the pending state (N-11, pass-1 D-9).'
killed.refutation: The tray's button carries no pending state; it carries a dead one, on two independent grounds. (a) `applyColorSearch` (SearchFilterBar.vue:213-225) is declared `async` but contains no `await`: `searching.value = true`, then a synchronous `hexToOklab` → `parseColorIn` (:205-211) and a synchronous `emit`, then `finally { searching.value = false }` — all in one task, so Vue never renders the `true` state and the `Loader2 v-if="searching"` + `:disabled="searching"` + `disabled:opacity-50 disabled:cursor-not-allowed` arm at :97-104 is unreachable code. Consolidating the two `Search` verbs onto the tray button is still right; the stated reason for choosing it is false. The same correction applies to N-11 (:380-381) and pass-1 D-17 (:474), which both frame `searching` as a working arm the child merely failed to receive.

The cure is therefore structurally unsound: deleting `useLiquidPress` would delete the card's only press feedback, in a component already indicted for having none. Two riders die with it: (a) C4-3's "no `@keydown`" (challenge-C-implementation.md:227) is false in letter — the same handler bag binds `onKeydown`/`onKeyup`/`onBlur` at PaletteCard.vue:24; (b) the template's "PRM-instant by construction" comment (:262) is TRUE — dist/useSpring-9u2_shxV.js defaults `respectReducedMotion: u.respectReducedMotion !== !1`.

missed.claim: The touch / coarse-pointer route to the per-colour actions is dead too, by a second mechanism no axis names: reka's `PopoverTrigger as-child` forwards its handlers and ARIA as ATTRS into a component that discards attrs.
missed.proof: demo/palettes/browser/card/SwatchHoverMenu.vue:8-25 is the `!canHover` arm — `<Popover><PopoverTrigger as-child><WatercolorDot …/></PopoverTrigger>`. `as-child` works by cloning the child VNode with the trigger's `onClick`, `aria-expanded`, `data-state` and ref merged in as props/attrs. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js compiles with `inheritAttrs: !1`, spreads no `$attrs`, and forwards only `attrs.class`/`attrs.style` — so the trigger's click handler and state attributes never reach the rendered `<span>`, which additionally carries inline `pointerEvents:"none"`. The touch popover therefore cannot open. Both governing axes attribute the dead touch path to the consumer's own `onSwatchClick` (challenge-D-design.md:185-187) — but `onSwatchClick` is the HOVER-arm handler; the touch arm goes through `@update:open` → `onPopoverUpdateTouch` (PaletteCard.vue:153, useHoverPopover.ts:47-49) and never involves it. Net: add/edit/copy for a palette's colours is unreachable by mouse (panel unpositioned + aria-hidden), by keyboard (no tab stop), and by touch (trigger unbound) — a complete feature that cannot be operated by anyone.

missed.claim: The two governing axes prescribe mutually exclusive cures for the SAME owner mark, and the two normative homes they cite disagree — neither report acknowledges the other.
missed.proof: MT-F036's shadow half: challenge-D-design.md:254-263 and :970-981 rule that the entity card "carries no shadow at all", citing docs/tranches/V/VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:54 (frozen tuple `shadow=false`, "no cartoon") and :186 ("matte specimen slips … not cartoon casters stacked within casters") — both verified verbatim. challenge-L-library.md:740-750 rules the opposite: mint `.well-card` and have PaletteCard, PaletteCardSkeleton and ShadowPalette all ride `--shadow-cartoon-sm`, citing demo/DESIGN.md:98 and demo/styles/utils.css:122. Both cures cannot land: one removes the caster, the other standardises it. The underlying conflict is between two normative documents — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:54/186 (V canon, shadow=false, no cartoon) and demo/DESIGN.md:98 (T.W3-1 material ladder, rung 2 = well + cartoon stamp) — and it must be ruled before either wave input is actionable.

missed.claim: The press handlers are bound to the card ROOT, so they fire on descendants: pressing Space or Enter while typing in the inline rename field squashes the whole card.
missed.proof: PaletteCard.vue:24 binds `v-bind="press.handlers"` on the article root. That bag (dist/useLiquidPress-BOxuDkKa.js) includes `onKeydown: e => (e.key==="Enter"||e.key===" "||e.key==="Spacebar") && !e.repeat && press()` and `onKeyup`/`onBlur` releases, and it never inspects `e.target`. PaletteRenameInput is rendered INSIDE that root (PaletteCard.vue:112-120) and stops only `escape` (PaletteRenameInput.vue:16), so every space bar in a palette name bubbles to the root and drives the spring — a scale squash of the entire card per keystroke. The same leak fires from any focused descendant (the vote button, the menu trigger) on Enter/Space.

missed.claim: Focus is dropped on the one keyboard path that provably works: submitting or cancelling a rename unmounts the focused input with no focus restoration.
missed.proof: PaletteRenameInput.vue:53-56 focuses and selects the input on mount (correctly). On submit or cancel, PaletteCard.vue:118 / :287 set `renaming = false`, unmounting the focused element; nothing returns focus to the invoker (the menu item or the title span), so focus falls to `<body>` and the keyboard user loses their place in a list of cards. killed.claim: BLOCKER — "`useHoverPopover` reads `e.currentTarget` after dispatch; every swatch hover throws" (challenge-L-library.pass-2-2026-07-27.md:93-150), carried as STANDS through passes 3, 4 and 5 (challenge-L-library.md:688).
killed.refutation: REFUTED — the finding is an artifact of the probe's own synthetic dispatch. (a) Spec: DOM §dispatch clears `currentTarget` only after the whole invoke loop; HTML's "clean up after running script" performs a microtask checkpoint the moment the JS execution stack empties, which for a browser-initiated event is immediately after the listener callback returns — while `currentTarget` is still the wrapper element. Vue's `nextTick` is a promise microtask, so `positionPanel(e.currentTarget)` at `useHoverPopover.ts:30` runs DURING dispatch and receives the live `div.relative` (`SwatchHoverMenu.vue:2-6`). It is null only when dispatch is initiated from JS (`el.dispatchEvent(...)` inside an `evaluate`), where the stack is non-empty and the microtask is deferred past dispatch completion — which is exactly what pass 2 did ("hover dispatched on the swatch wrapper", pass-2:112). (b) The corpus refutes itself: pass 4's probe D2, after a real Playwright `.hover()`, recorded `"inlineStyle": "top: 587.625px; left: 788px; transform: translateX(-50%);"` (probe-C4d-pass4-results.json → `D2_floatingPanel`) — `positionPanel` demonstrably ran and wrote real viewport coordinates. Pass 2's `top: 0px; left: 0px` is the untouched initial `reactive({top:"0px",left:"0px"})` (`useHoverPopover.ts:17`). What survives: `e.currentTarget as Element` is a masking assertion over a value that IS null for any programmatic dispatch — a latent fragility worth a MINOR, not a BLOCKER. The panel's real defect is L-15's missing CSS, and killing L-16 does not touch it.

`demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteColorStrip.vue:47-71` — the weighted-segment computation is the best code in the folder: total on the empty case (`if (n === 0) return []`), a named 8% legibility floor so small quantizer clusters survive, renormalisation after flooring so the segments still sum to 100, and a three-tier fallback (explicit `weights` → the colours' own `weight` fields → equal widths) whose rationale is recorded on the prop. The 0.1 s is glass-ui's deliberate house-wide floor: node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/utilities/a11y-overrides.css sets, under `reduce`, `transition-duration: 0.1s !important` together with `transition-property: opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow !important` — i.e. the surviving 0.1 s can only carry non-vestibular colour legs; every spatial property is struck from the transition set entirely. codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md:57-66 measured exactly this and §5 S-1/S-4 (:175-192) records it as correct central governance, and rules the identical claim shape FALSE in eight sibling files (M-03, M-07, M-11, M-17, M-26, M-29, M-31, M-32) — "motion is governed centrally, not duplicated per component". Worse for the claim: the C axis's own measurement (challenge-C-implementation.md:387) shows the card's declared transition at no-preference is `transition-property: all; transition-duration: 0s` — it animates nothing at all, so PRM does not shorten a motion, it adds a colour-only floor. Nothing in PaletteCard.vue:337-364 or its class strings authored this. The second limb of D3-20 (the height transition never joined the PRM-safe family) is real and is confirmed as C4-1.

killed.claim: "`dist/styles/glass/glass-atom.css` — the only sheet declaring `.cartoon-cast` — is not in the demo's loaded cascade" (challenge-C-implementation.md:411-414).
killed.refutation: The premise is false. `grep -rl cartoon-cast node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/` returns three files, and dist/styles/glass/liquid-enter.css — which IS reachable, via dist/styles/glass.css's `@import "./glass/liquid-enter.css"` → dist/styles/index.css → foundation.css:56 — declares `.cartoon-cast` four times, all scoped `.liquid-enter.is-cel > .cartoon-cast`. The conclusion (PaletteCard.vue:30's span is inert) survives, but for a different reason: the rule is loaded and simply does not match, not absent. challenge-L-library.md:168-218 (L-44) already made this correction with a live cascade enumeration; the C axis's pass-4 text was not reconciled to it, and the distinction matters because it is exactly what makes the earlier "restore the missing import" cure wrong.

missed.claim: The Featured badge's gold shimmer fails text contrast in light mode, and the producer's reduced-motion gate parks it at its least legible stop — permanently, for exactly the users who asked for less motion.
missed.proof: PaletteCard.vue:64 applies glass-ui's `.gold-shimmer` to the badge. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/styles/utilities/base-misc.css declares `.gold-shimmer { background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--color-gold-dark), var(--color-gold-light), var(--color-gold), var(--color-gold-light), var(--color-gold-dark)); background-size: 250% 100%; background-clip: text; color: transparent; }` and gates the sweep inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .gold-shimmer { animation: metal-shimmer-sweep … infinite } }`. demo/styles/foundation.css:104-105 pins `--color-gold: #D4AF37` and `--color-gold-light: #F5E6A3` as scheme-invariant hex, overriding glass-ui's `light-dark()` ramp while leaving `--color-gold-dark` producer-owned — a chimeric gradient. Against the card's own light-mode ground (`bg-well`, measured oklab L 0.913 in challenge-D-design.md:907-912 ⇒ relative luminance ≈ 0.76): #F5E6A3 ≈ 1.03:1, #D4AF37 ≈ 1.6:1, and even the darkest producer stop only reaches ≈ 3:1 — the ramp never touches 4.5:1 anywhere. The label is `text-mono-small` = `clamp(0.875rem, 0.8rem + 0.25vw, 1.25rem)` ≈ 16.4 px at 1440, i.e. normal text under WCAG 1.4.3. Because the animation is absent under `reduce`, `background-position` rests at its `0% 0` initial, which maps the visible 0–40 % of a 250 %-wide image across the word and parks the near-white stop mid-label — a static ~1:1 rendering, not a transient one. The border shares the fault: the scoped `.featured-badge { border-color: var(--color-gold) }` (PaletteCard.vue:343-345) is 1.6:1 against the same ground, below the 3:1 non-text minimum. All three axes missed it, and challenge-D-design.md:1028-1029 lists this exact code under "What is genuinely right".

missed.claim: The palette name is an unconditional dead zone at three of the five call sites: `@click.stop` swallows the click and then performs nothing.
missed.proof: PaletteCard.vue:58 is `@click.stop="editableName && startRenaming()"`. Vue's `.stop` modifier compiles to `withModifiers(handler, ["stop"])`, which calls `stopPropagation()` before the handler body runs — so propagation dies whether or not `editableName` is set. `editableName` is passed only at PalettesPane.vue:89 and ExtractWorkbench.vue:151. At BrowsePane.vue:92-102 (`@click="pm.toggleExpand(palette.slug)"`), AdminUsersPanel.vue:140-148 and MixSourceSelector.vue:246-268 it is absent, so clicking the largest, most obvious target in the row does nothing at all — and at Mix specifically it defeats the wrapper `<button @click="togglePalette(palette)">` (:263), meaning the palette's own name cannot select the palette. D3-7 reaches the touch/rename half on `/#/palettes` and C4-6 reaches the focusability half, but neither states that the same line is a silent no-op on the majority of consumers.

missed.claim: `copyAll` is implemented and unreachable — and with the swatch popover dead, there is no working path at all to copy a palette's colours from the card.
missed.proof: PaletteCard.vue:294 registers `copyAll: () => void writeClipboard(props.palette.colors.map(c => c.css).join(", "))` in the menu dispatch table. `grep -rn copyAll demo/` returns exactly that one line: PaletteCardMenu.vue emits no such action anywhere in its 228 lines. The verb is dead code — and it is the only bulk-copy affordance the component implements, so with the per-swatch Copy button living inside the undeclared `.floating-panel` (confirmed C4-12) and the swatch's own click swallowed by `inheritAttrs: !1` (confirmed D3-2), the card ships no functioning colour-copy path whatsoever. challenge-C-implementation.md:501-506 audits the same dispatch table for its lack of a gate and counts its entries, but does not notice that one of them is unreachable.

missed.claim: The coarse-pointer Popover path is structurally inoperative for the same reason as the hover path, so the corpus's "the touch route is the accessible route" comment is false.
missed.proof: SwatchHoverMenu.vue:13-21 renders `<PopoverTrigger as-child><WatercolorDot … /></PopoverTrigger>`. reka-ui's `as-child` clones the child vnode and merges the trigger's props, listeners and template ref onto it; for a component child those arrive as `$attrs`, and dist/watercolor-dot.js compiles `inheritAttrs: !1` and forwards only `class` and `style`. So no `onClick`, no `data-state`, no `aria-expanded` and no element ref reach the rendered `<span>` — which also carries inline `pointerEvents: "none"`. The comment at SwatchHoverMenu.vue:38-39 ("The reka-ui Popover (touch path) is the accessible route") therefore describes a route that does not exist. challenge-D-design.md:186 asserts the touch-toggle path is dead by association with `onSwatchClick`, but that is the hover path's handler; the `as-child` + `inheritAttrs` mechanism is never reached, and probe-D5g never measured it (probe-D5g-results.json shows `swatchCount: 0` — the tap renamed instead).

superlatives: PaletteColorStrip.vue:50-71 — the weighted-segment computation is the one place in the folder that treats the specimen as data: it prefers explicit `weights`, falls back to the colours' own `weight` fields so an extracted palette carries its population story on the palette itself, applies an 8 % legibility floor (`WEIGHT_FLOOR`, :48) so small clusters survive, then renormalises. Correct, closed, and no twin strip anywhere.

PaletteCardMenu.vue:24-40 and :42-60 — the K-INV5 pattern: a tripped availability latch DISABLES the doomed action and names the degraded state in-register (`offline`, `public`, `private`, small-caps, `ml-auto`) instead of firing a toast the user must catch. It reads the latch through an injected client seam (`useApiClient()`, :216) rather than a module singleton, and it names the CURRENT state next to the verb that changes it (:52-59) — better interaction design than most of the product.

demo/palettes/browser/card/index.ts:1-9 — named-only re-exports with the reason written down (PI-6: an SFC `<style scoped>` block makes the module side-effecting, so a star re-export defeats tree-shaking). A correct bundler-level rationale recorded at the point of the decision is genuinely rare.

PaletteRenameInput.vue:58-65 — the submit policy treats an unchanged or whitespace-only name as a cancel rather than emitting a no-op rename, so the parent's `rename` emit is always a real mutation; paired with `useTemplateRef` + focus-and-select on mount (:48, :53-56) and `@keydown.escape.stop` (:16), it is the most idiomatic Vue 3.5 file in the folder.

node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js — the producer internalises its own SVG turbulence filter with a per-instance namespaced id (`watercolor-filter-${uid}`) so there is zero consumer plumbing, and its animation loop is constructed with `respectReducedMotion: !0` and `pauseWhenHidden: !0`. On the axis the consumer cannot reach, the producer does the right thing by default — which sharpens rather than softens the `tag`/`aria-label`/`pointer-events` indictment.

The audit corpus's own hygiene. challenge-C-implementation.md:449-478 records four hypotheses that measurement KILLED (including the author's own `@click`-is-keyboard-dead theory) so a later pass does not re-spend the probes, and :50-57 publishes an apparatus correction that invalidates part of the prior fixture (`probe-D5.mjs` seeded a bare array the store silently discards). challenge-L-library.md:41-45 finds and removes a prior seat's 12-deep empty directory left by a shell-quoting accident, with a `find -type f` receipt proving no content was lost. Self-correction with receipts is scarcer than findings.

confirmed.claim: Under prefers-reduced-motion the expand/collapse Transition never completes; the swatch subtree is never unmounted.
confirmed.proof: Axis: challenge-C-implementation.md:87-193. Live: /Users/mkbabb/Programming/value.js/demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHeightTransition.ts:35-39 and :66-70 both read `if (e.propertyName !== "height") return;` before the ONLY done() call sites (:38, :69). Both hooks are 2-arity (onEnter(el,done) :27, onLeave(el,done) :59), so Vue's DOM Transition treats them as explicit-callback hooks and never auto-resolves — the element is held until done() fires. Independently corroborated as a PROPERTY-LIST REWRITE and cascade winner at docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/codex-provenance/motion-quarantine.md:47-62. Wired at PaletteCard.vue:131-138 and :269-278. Mechanism confirmed statically end-to-end; only the node arithmetic rests on probe-C4e-pass4.
